units.english: "The loss of the thing done,—the enjoyment of the fruit of a thing not done,—the dissolution of all existence,—and the abolition of memory,—bold indeed is the Buddhist antagonist, when, in the teeth of these four objections, he seeks to establish his doctrine of momentary destruction!"

units.sanskrit: न च समसमयवर्तिता शङ्कनीया। सव्येतरविषाणवत्कार्यकारणभावासंभवेनाग्राह्यस्यालम्बनप्रत्ययत्वानुपपत्तेः।
units.english: Nor may you suppose that the object and the perception are simultaneous, because this would imply that, like the two horns of an animal, they did not stand in the relation of cause and effect [as this relation necessarily involves succession], and consequently the Ālambana, or the object's data [supra, p.

units.sanskrit: अथ भिन्नकालस्यापि तस्याकारर्पकत्वेन ग्राह्यत्वम्तदप्यपेशलम्।
units.english: If you say that "the object may still be perceived, inasmuch as it will impress its form on the perception, even though the one may have existed in a different moment from the other," this too will not hold.

units.sanskrit: क्षणिकस्य ज्ञानस्याकारार्पकताश्रयताया दुर्वचत्वेन साकारज्ञानवादप्रत्यादेशात्। निराकारज्ञानवादेपि योग्यतावशेन प्रतिकर्मव्यवस्थायाः स्थितत्वात्।
units.english: For if you maintain that the knowledge acquired by perception has a certain form impressed upon it, you are met by the impossibility of explaining how a momentary perception can possess the power of impressing a form; and if you say that it has no form impressed upon it, you are equally met by the fact that, if we are to avoid incongruity, there must be some definite condition to determine the perception and knowledge in each several case.

units.sanskrit: तथा हि प्रत्यक्षेण विषयाकाररहितमेव ज्ञानं प्रतिपुरुषमहमहमिकयाघटादिग्राहकमनुभूयते न तु दर्पणादिवत्प्रतिबिम्बाक्रान्तम्। विषयाकारधारितत्वे च ज्ञानस्यार्थे दूरनिकटादिव्यवहाराय जलाञ्जलिर्वितीर्येत।
units.english: Thus by perception the abstract consciousness, which before existed uninfluenced by the external object, becomes modified under the form of a jar, &c., with a definite reference to each man's personality [i.e., I see the jar], and it is not merely the passive recipient of a reflection like a mirror.

units.sanskrit: न चेदमिष्टापादनमेष्टव्यम्। दवीयान्महीधरो नेदीयान्दीर्घों बाहुरिति व्यवहारस्य निराबाधं जागरुकत्वात्। न चाकाराधायकस्य तस्य दवीयस्त्वादिशालितया तथा व्यवहार इति कथनीयम्। दर्पणादौ तथानुपलम्भात्। किं चार्थादुपजायमानं ज्ञानं यथा तस्य नीलाकारतामनुकरोति तथा यदि जडतामपि तर्ह्यर्थत्तदपि जडं स्यात्।
units.english: Moreover, if the perception only reproduced the form of the object, there would be an end of using such words as "far," "near," &c., of the objects.[5] Nor can you accept this conclusion, "as exactly in accordance with your own views," because, in spite of all our logic, the stubborn fact remains that we do use such phrases as "the mountain is nearer" or "further," "long" or "large." Nor may you say that "it is the object (which supplies the form) that really possesses these qualities of being 'further,' &c., and they are applied by a fashion of speech to the perception [though not really belonging to it]"—because we do not find that this is the case in a mirror [i.e., it does not become a far reflection because it represents a far object.] And again, as the perception produced by an object follows it in assuming the form of blue, so too, if the object be insentient, it ought equally to assume its form and so become itself insentient.

units.sanskrit: तथा च वृद्धिमिष्टवतो मूलमपि ते नष्टं स्यादिति महत्कष्टमापन्नम्।
units.english: And thus, according to the proverb, "wishing to grow, you have destroyed your root," and your cause has fallen into hopeless difficulties.

units.sanskrit: अथैतद्दोषपरिजिहीर्षया ज्ञानं जडतां नानुकरोतीति ब्रूषे हन्त तर्हि तस्या ग्रहणं न स्यादित्येकामनुसंधित्सतोपरं प्रच्ययत इति न्यायापातः। ननु मा भूज्जडताया ग्रहणम्।
units.english: If, in your wish to escape this difficulty, you assert that "the perception does not follow the object in being insentient," then there would be no perception that the object is insentient,[6] and so it is a case of the proverb, "While he looks for one thing which he has lost, another drops." "But what harm will it be if there is no perception of a thing's being insentient?" [We reply], that if its being insentient is not perceived, while its blue form is perceived, the two may be quite distinct [and as different from each other as a jar and cloth], or it may be a case of "indeterminateness" [so that the two may be only occasionally found together, as smoke with fire].

units.sanskrit: किं नश्छिन्नम्। तदग्रहणेपि नीलाकारग्रहणे तयो र्भेदोनेकान्तो वा भवेत्। नीलाकारग्रहणे चागृहीताजडता कथं तस्य स्वरूपं स्यात्। अपरथा गृहीतस्य स्तम्भस्यागृहीतं त्रैलोक्यमपि रूपं भवेत्।
units.english: And again, if insentience is not perceived contemporaneously with the blue form, how could there then be conformity between them [so that both the blue and the insentience should together constitute the character of the thing?] We might just as well maintain that, on perceiving a post, the unperceived universe entered into it as also constituting its character.[7]

units.sanskrit: तदेतत्प्रमेयजातं प्रभाचन्द्रप्रभृतिभिरर्हन्मतानुसारिभिः प्रमेयकमलमार्तण्डादौ (प्र.क.मा.पृ.२७) प्रबन्धे प्रपञ्चितमिति ग्रन्थभूयस्त्वभयान्नोपन्यस्तम्।
units.english: All this collection of topics for proof has been discussed at full length by the Jaina authors, Pratāpacandra and others, in the Prameyakamalamārtaṇḍa, &c., and is here omitted for fear of swelling the book too much.

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्पुरुषार्थाभिलाषुकैः पुरुषैः सौगती गतिर्नानुगन्तव्या। अपि त्वार्हत्येवार्हणीया।
units.english: Therefore those who wish for the summum bonum of man must not accept the doctrine of Buddha, but rather honour only the Ārhata doctrine.

units.sanskrit: अर्हत्स्वरूपं च हेमचन्द्रसूरिभिराप्तनिश्चायालंकारे निरटङ्कि।
units.english: The Arhat's nature has been thus described by Arhachcandra-sūri,[8] in his Āptaniścayālaṅkāra.

units.sanskrit: सर्वज्ञो जितरागादिदोषस्त्रैलोक्यपूजितः। यथास्थितार्थवादी च देवोर्हन्परमेश्वरः॥इति।
units.english: "The divine Arhat is the supreme lord, the omniscient one, who has overcome all faults, desire, &c.,—adored by the three worlds, the declarer of things as they are."

units.sanskrit: ननु न कश्चित्पुरुषविशेषः सर्वज्ञपदवेदनीयः प्रमाणपद्धतिमध्यास्ते। तत्सद्भावग्राहकस्य प्रमाणपञ्चकस्य तत्रानुपलम्भात्।
units.english: But may it not be objected that no such omniscient soul can enter the path of proof, since none of the five affirmative proofs can be found to apply, as has been declared by Tautātita [Bhaṭṭa Kumārila[9]]?

units.sanskrit: दृष्टो न चैकदेशोस्ति लिङ्गं वा योनुमापयेत्॥ न चागमविधिः कश्चिन्नित्य सर्वज्ञबोधकः।
units.english: "No omniscient being is seen by the sense here in this world by ourselves or others; nor is there any part of him seen which might help us as a sign to infer his existence.

units.sanskrit: न च तत्रार्थवादानां तात्पर्यमपि कल्प्यते॥२॥ न चान्यार्थप्रधानैस्तैस्तदस्तित्वं विधीयते।
units.english: "His existence is not declared by those passages which refer to quite other topics; and it cannot be contained in any emphatic repetitions (anuvāda), as it had never been mentioned elsewhere before.

units.sanskrit: न चानुवदितुं शक्यः पूर्वमन्यैरबोधितः॥३॥ अनादेरागमस्यार्थों न च सर्वज्ञ आदिमान्।
units.english: "An omniscient being who had a beginning can never be the subject of the eternal Veda; and how can he be established by a made and spurious Veda?

units.sanskrit: कृत्रिमेण त्वसत्येन स कथं प्रतिपाद्यते॥४॥ अथ तद्वचनेनैव सर्वज्ञोज्ञैः प्रतीयते।
units.english: "Do you say that this omniscient one is accepted on his own word? How can you establish either when they thus both depend on reciprocal support?

units.sanskrit: प्रकल्प्येत कथं सिद्धिरन्योन्याश्रययोस्तयोः॥५॥ सर्वज्ञोक्ततया वाक्यं सत्यं तेन तदस्तिता। कथं तदुभयं सिध्येत्सिद्धमूलान्तरादृते॥६॥
units.english: "[If you say,] 'The saying is true because it was uttered by one omniscient, and this proves the Arhat's existence;' how can either point be established without some previously established foundation?

units.sanskrit: असर्वज्ञप्रणीतात्तु वचनान्मूलवर्जितात्। असर्वज्ञमवगच्छन्तः स्ववाक्योक्तिं न जानते॥७॥
units.english: "But they who accept a [supposed] omniscient on the baseless word of a parviscient know nothing of the meaning of a real omniscient's words.

units.sanskrit: सर्वज्ञसदृशं कं चिद्यदि पश्येम संप्रति। उपमानेन सर्वज्ञं जानीयाम ततो वयम्॥
units.english: "And again, if we now could see anything like an omniscient being, we might have a chance of recognising him by the [well-known fourth] proof, comparison (upamāna).

units.sanskrit: उपदेशोपि बुद्धस्य धर्माधर्मादिगोचरः। अन्यथा नोपपद्येत सार्वज्ञयं यदि नाभवत्॥ एवमर्थापत्तिरपि प्रमाणं नात्र युज्यते।
units.english: "And the teaching of Buddha [as well as that of Jina], which embraces virtue, vice, &c., would not be established as authoritative, if there were not in him the attribute of omniscience,[10] and so on."

units.sanskrit: उपदेशस्य सत्यत्वं यतो नाध्यक्षमीक्ष्यते॥१०॥ इत्यादि अत्र प्रतिविधीयते। यदभ्यधायि तत्सद्भावग्राहकस्य प्रमाणपञ्चकस्य तत्रानुपलम्भादितितदयुक्तम्।
units.english: We reply as follows:—As for the supposed contradiction of an Arhat's existence, derived from the failure of the five affirmative proofs,—this is untenable, because there are proofs, as inference, &c., which do establish[11] his existence.

units.sanskrit: यद्यग्द्रहणस्वभावत्वे सति प्रक्षीणप्रतिबन्धप्रत्ययं तत्तत्साक्षात्कारि यथापगततिमिरादिप्रतिबन्धं लोचनविज्ञानं रूपसाक्षात्कारि।
units.english: Whatever thing has a natural capacity for knowing any object, will, when its hindrances to such knowledge are done away, actually know it, just as the sense of vision cognises form, directly the hindrances of darkness, &c., are removed.

units.sanskrit: तद्ग्रहणस्वभावत्वे सति प्रक्षीणप्रतिबन्धप्रत्ययश्च कश्चिदात्मा। तस्मात्सकलपदार्थसाक्षात्कारीति न तावदशेषार्थग्रहणस्वभावत्वमात्मनोसिद्धम्। चोदनाबलान्निखिलार्थज्ञानोत्पत्तयन्यथानुपपत्तया सर्वमनेकान्तात्मकं सत्तवादिति व्याप्तिज्ञानोत्पत्तोश्च। चोदना हि भूतं भवन्तं भविष्यन्तंस सूक्ष्मं व्यवहितं विप्रकृष्ठमित्येवंजातीयकमर्थमवगमयतीत्येवंजातीयकै रध्वरमीमांसागुरुभिर्विघिप्रतिषेधविचारणानिबन्धनं सकलार्थविषयज्ञानं प्रतिपद्यमानैः सकलार्थग्रहणस्वभावकत्वमात्मानोभ्युपगतम्।
units.english: Now there is such a soul, which has its hindrances done away, its natural capacity for grasping all things remaining unchanged; therefore there is an omniscient being. Nor is the assertion unestablished that the soul has a natural capacity for grasping all things; for otherwise the Mīmāṃsist could not maintain that a knowledge of all possible cases can be produced by the authoritative injunction of a text,[12]—nor could there otherwise be the knowledge of universal propositions, such as that in our favourite argument, "All things are indeterminate from the very fact of their existence" [and, of course, a follower of the Nyāya will grant that universal propositions can be known, though he will dispute the truth of this particular one].

units.sanskrit: न चाखिलार्थप्रतिबन्धकावरणप्रक्षयानुपपत्तिः। सम्यग्दर्शनादित्रयलक्षणस्यावरणप्रक्षयहेतुभूतस्य सामग्रीविशेषस्य प्रतितत्वात्।
units.english: 1, 2], "A precept makes known the past, the present, the future, the minute, the obstructed, the distant, &c." Nor can you say that "it is impossible to destroy the obstructions which hinder the soul's knowing all things," because we [Jainas] are convinced that there are certain special means to destroy these obstructions, viz., the three ["gems"], right intuition, &c.

units.sanskrit: अनया मुद्रयापि क्षुद्रोपद्रवा विद्राव्याः।
units.english: By this charm also, all inferior assaults of argument can be put to flight.

units.sanskrit: नन्वावरणप्रक्षयवशादशेषविषयं विज्ञानं विशदं मुख्यप्रत्यक्षं प्रभवतीत्युक्तं तदयुक्तम्। तस्य सर्वज्ञस्यानादिमुक्तत्वेनावरणस्यैवासंभवादिति चेत्तन्न।
units.english: But the Naiyāyika may interpose, "You talk of the pure intelligence, which, after all hindrances are done away, sees all objects, having sense-perception at its height; but this is irrelevant, because there can be no hindrance to the omniscient, as from all eternity he has been always liberated." We reply that there is no proof of your eternally liberated being.

units.sanskrit: न सर्वज्ञोनादिमुक्तः। मुक्तत्वादिरमुक्तवत्। वद्धापेक्षया च मुक्तव्यपदेशः।
units.english: There cannot be an omniscient who is eternally "liberated," from the very fact of his being "liberated," like other liberated persons,—since the use of the term "liberated" necessarily implies the having been previously bound; and if the latter is absent, the former must be too, as is seen in the case of the ether.

units.sanskrit: तद्रहिते चास्याप्यभावः स्यादाकाशवत्। नन्वनादेः क्षित्यादिकार्यपरंपरायाः कर्तृत्वेन तत्सिद्धिः। तथा हिक्षित्यादिकं सकर्तृकं कार्यत्वाद्धटवदिति।
units.english: "But is not this being's existence definitely proved by his being the maker of that eternal series of effects, the earth, &c.? according to the well-known argument, 'the earth, &c., must have had a maker, because they have the nature of effects, as a jar.'" This argument, however, will not hold, because you cannot prove that they have the nature of effects.

units.sanskrit: न च सावयवत्वेन तत्साधनमित्यभिधातव्यम्। यस्मादिदं विकल्पजालमवतरति।
units.english: You cannot establish this from the fact of their being composed of parts, because this supposition falls upon the horns of a dilemma.

units.sanskrit: सावयवत्वं किमवयवसंयोगित्वम् अवयवसमवायित्वम् अवयवजन्यत्वं समवेतद्रव्यत्वं सावयवबुद्धिविषयत्वं वा।
units.english: Does this "being composed of parts" mean (i.) the being in contact with the parts; or (ii.) "the being in intimate relation to the parts; or (iii.) the being produced from parts;" or (iv.) the being a substance in intimate relation; or (v.) the being the object of an idea involving the notion of parts?

units.sanskrit: न प्रथमः। आकाशादावनैकान्त्यात्। न द्वितीयः। सामान्यादौ व्यभिचारात्। न तृतीयः।
units.english: Not the first, because it would apply too widely, as it would include ether [since this, though not itself composed of parts, is in contact with the parts of other things;] nor the second, because it would similarly include genus, &c.

units.sanskrit: न चतुर्थः। विकल्पयुगलार्गलग्रहगलत्वात्। समवायसंबन्धमात्रवद् द्रव्यत्वं समवेतद्रव्यत्वमन्यत्र समवेतद्रव्यत्वं वा विवक्षितं हेतुक्रियते। आद्ये गगनादौ व्यभिचारः। तस्यापि गुणादिसमवायत्वद्रव्यत्वयोः संभवात्।
units.english: [as this resides in a substance by intimate relation, and yet itself is not composed of parts;] nor the third, because this involves a term ("produced") just as much disputed as the one directly in question;[13] nor the fourth, because its neck is caught in the pillory of the following alternative:—Do you mean by your phrase used above that it is to be a substance, and to have something else in intimate relation to itself,—or do you mean that it must have intimate relation to something else, in order to be valid for your argument? If you say the former, it will equally apply to ether, since this is a substance, and has its qualities resident in it by intimate relation; if you say the latter, your new position involves as much dispute as the original point, since you would have to prove the existence of intimate relation in the parts, or the so-called "intimate causes," which you mean by "something else." We use these terms in compliance with your terminology; but, of course, from our point of view, we do not allow such a thing as "intimate relation," as there is no proof of its existence.

units.sanskrit: अन्यशब्दार्थेषु समवायकारणभूतेष्ववयवेषु समवायस्य साधनीयत्वात्। तस्य सावयवबुद्धिविषयत्वेपि कार्यत्वाभावात्। न च निरवयवत्वेप्यस्य सावयवार्थसंबन्धेन सावयवबुद्धिविषयत्वमौपचारिकमित्येष्टव्यम्। निरवयवत्वे व्यापित्वविरोधात्परमाणुवत्।
units.english: Nor can the fifth alternative be allowed, because this would reach too far, as it would include soul, &c., since soul can be the object of an idea involving the notion of parts, and yet it is acknowledged to be not an effect.[14] Nor can you maintain that the soul may still be indiscerptible in itself, but by reason of its connection with something possessing parts may itself become metaphorically the object of an idea involving the notion of parts, because there is a mutual contradiction in the idea of that which has no parts and that which is all-pervading, just as the atom [which is indiscerptible but not all-pervading].

units.sanskrit: किं च किमेकः कर्ता साध्यते किं वानेके ।
units.english: And, moreover, is there only one maker? Or, again, is he independent?

units.sanskrit: स्थापत्यादीनां बहूनां पुरुषाणां तत्र कर्तृत्वोपलम्भात्। द्वितीये बहूनां विश्वनिर्मातृत्वे तेषु मिथो वैमत्यसंभावनाया अनिर्वार्यत्वादेकै कस्य वस्तुनोन्यान्यरूपतया निर्माणे सर्वमसमञ्जसमापद्येत।
units.english: In the former case your position will apply too far, as it will extend erroneously to palaces, &c., where we see for ourselves the work of many different men, as carpenters, &c., and [in the second case] if all the world were produced by this one maker, all other agents would be superfluous.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं वीतरागस्तुतौकर्तास्ति कश्चिज्जगतः स चैकः स सर्वगः स स्ववशः स नित्यः। इमाः कु हेवाकविडम्बनाः स्युः - स्तेषां न येषामनुशासकस्त्वम्॥ (वी.स्तु. ६) इति।
units.english: As it has been said in the Vītarāgastuti, or "Praise of Jina"— "There is one eternal maker for the world, all-pervading, independent, and true; they have none of these inextricable delusions, whose teacher art thou." And again—

units.sanskrit: अन्यत्रापिकर्ता न तावदिह कोपि यथेच्छया वा दृष्टोन्यथा कटकृतावपि तत्प्रसङ्गः।
units.english: "There is here no maker acting by his own free will, else his influence would extend to the making of a mat.

units.sanskrit: कार्यं किमत्र भवतापि च तक्षकाद्यै - राहत्य च त्रिभुवनं पुरुषः करोति॥
units.english: What would be the use of yourself or all the artisans, if Īśvara fabricates the three worlds?"

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्प्रागुक्तकारणत्रितयबलादावरणप्रक्षये सार्वज्ञं युक्तम्।
units.english: Therefore it is right to hold, as we do, that omniscience is produced when the hindrances are removed by the three means before alluded to.

units.sanskrit: न चास्योपदेष्ट्रन्तराभावात्सम्यग्दर्शनादित्रितयानुपपत्तिरिति भणनीयम्। पूर्वसर्वज्ञप्रणीतागमप्रभवत्वादमुष्याशेषार्थज्ञानस्य।
units.english: Nor need the objection be made that "right intuition," &c., are impossible, as there is no other teacher to go to,—because this universal knowledge can be produced by the inspired works of former omniscient Jinas.

units.sanskrit: न चान्योन्याश्रयादिदोषः। आगमसर्वज्ञपरंपराया बीजाङ्कु रवदनादित्वाङ्गीकारादित्यलम्।
units.english: Nor is our doctrine liable to the imputation of such faults as Anyonyāśrayatā,[15] &c., because we accept an eternal succession of revealed doctrines and omniscient teachers, like the endless series of seed springing from shoot and shoot from seed.

units.sanskrit: रत्नत्रयपदवेदनीयतया प्रसिद्धं सम्यग्दर्शनादित्रितयमर्हत्प्रवचनसंग्रहपरे परमागमसारे प्ररूपितं सम्यग्दर्शनज्ञानचारित्राणि मोक्षमार्ग इति। विवृतं च योगदेवेन।
units.english: The well-known triad called the three gems, right intuition, &c., are thus described in the Paramāgamasāra (which is devoted to the exposition of the doctrines of the Arhats)—"Right intuition, right knowledge, right conduct are the path of liberation." This has been thus explained by Yogadeva:—

units.sanskrit: येन रूपेण जीवाद्यर्थों व्यवस्थितस्तेन रूपेणार्हता प्रतिपादिते तत्त्वार्थे विपरीताभिनिवेशरहितत्वाद्यपरपर्यायं श्रद्धानं सम्यग्दर्शनम्। तत्त्वार्थसूत्रंतत्वार्थं श्रद्धानं सम्यग्दर्शनमिति। अन्यदपिरुचिर्जिनोक्ततत्त्वेषु सम्यक् श्रद्धानमुच्यते। जायते तन्निसर्गेण गुरोरधिगमेन वा॥इति॥ परोपदेशनिरपेक्षमात्मस्वरूपं निसर्गः।
units.english: (a.) When the meaning of the predicaments, the soul, &c., has been declared by an Arhat in exact accordance with their reality, absolute faith in the teaching, i.e., the entire absence of any contrary idea, is "right intuition." And to this effect runs the Tattvārtha-sūtra, "Faith in the predicaments[16] is right 'intuition.'" Or, as another definition gives it, "Acquiescence in the predicaments declared by a Jina is called 'right faith;' it is produced either by natural character or by the guru's instruction." "Natural character" means the soul's own nature, independent of another's teaching; "instruction" is the knowledge produced by the teaching of another in the form of explanation, &c.

units.sanskrit: व्याख्यानादिरूपपरोपदेशजनितं ज्ञानमधिगमः। येन स्वभावेन जीवादयः पदार्था व्यवस्थितास्तेन स्वभावेन मोहसंशयरहितत्वेनावगमः सम्यग्ज्ञानम्। यथोक्तम्यथावस्थिततत्त्वानां संक्षेपाद्विस्तरेण वा।
units.english: (b.) "Right knowledge" is a knowledge of the predicaments, soul, &c., according to their real nature, undisturbed by any illusion or doubt; as it has been said— "That knowledge, which embraces concisely or in detail the predicaments as they actually are, is called 'right knowledge' by the wise."

units.sanskrit: योवबोधस्तमत्राहुः सम्यग्ज्ञानं मनीषिणः॥इति॥ तज्ज्ञानं पञ्चविधं मतिश्रुतावधिमनःपर्यायके वलभेदेन। तदुक्तम् - मतिश्रुतावधिमनःपर्यायके वलानि ज्ञानमिति।
units.english: This knowledge is fivefold as divided into mati, śruta, avadhi, manas-paryāya, and kevala; as it has been said, "Mati, śruta, avadhi, manas-paryāya, and kevala, these are knowledge." The meaning of this is as follows:—

units.sanskrit: अस्यार्थःज्ञानावरणक्षयोपशमे सतीन्द्रियमनसी पुरस्कृत्य व्यापृतः सन् यथार्थं मनुते सा मति।
units.english: Mati is that by which one cognises an object through the operation of the senses and the mind, all obstructions of knowledge being abolished.

units.sanskrit: ज्ञानावरणक्षयोपशमे सति मतिजनितं स्पष्टं ज्ञानं श्रुतम्।
units.english: Śruta is the clear knowledge produced by mati, all the obstructions of knowledge being abolished.

units.sanskrit: सम्यग्दर्शनादिगुणजनितक्षयोपशमनिमित्तमवच्छिन्नविषयं ज्ञानमवधिः इर्ष्यान्तरायज्ञानावरणक्षयोपशमे सति परमनोगतस्यार्थस्य स्फु टं परिच्छेदकं ज्ञानं मनः पर्यायः। तपःक्रियाविशेषान्यदर्थं सेवन्ते तपस्विनस्तज्ज्ञानमन्यज्ञानासंसृष्टं के वलम्।
units.english: Avadhi is the knowledge of special objects caused by the abolition of hindrances, which is effected by "right intuition," &c.[17] Manas-paryāya is the clear definite knowledge of another's thoughts, produced by the abolition of all the obstructions of knowledge caused by the veil of envy. Kevala is that pure unalloyed knowledge for the sake of which ascetics practise various kinds of penance.

units.sanskrit: तत्राद्यं परोक्षं प्रत्यक्षमन्यत्। तदुक्तम् - विज्ञानं स्वपराभासि प्रमाणं बाधवर्जितम्। प्रत्यक्षं च परोक्षं च द्विधा ज्ञेयविनिश्चयात्॥
units.english: Thus it has been said— "True knowledge is a proof which nothing can overthrow, and which manifests itself as well as its object; it is both supersensuous and itself an object of cognition, as the object is determined in two ways."

units.sanskrit: अन्तर्गणिकभेदस्तु सविस्तरस्तत्रैवागमेऽवगन्तव्यः।
units.english: But the full account of the further minute divisions must be got from the authoritative treatise above-mentioned.

units.sanskrit: संसरणकर्मोंच्छित्तावुद्यतस्य श्रद्दधानस्य ज्ञानवतः पापगमनकारणक्रियानिर्वृत्तिः सम्यक्चरित्रम्।
units.english: (c.) "Right conduct" is the abstaining from all actions tending to evil courses by one who possesses faith and knowledge, and who is diligent in cutting off the series of actions and their effects which constitutes mundane existence.

units.sanskrit: तदेतत्सप्रपञ्चमुक्तमर्हता - सर्वथावद्ययोगानां त्यागश्चारित्रमुच्यते। कीर्तितं तदहिंसादिव्रतभेदेन पञ्चधा॥ अहिंसासूनृतास्तेयब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहाः।
units.english: This has been explained at length by the Arhat— "Right conduct is described as the entire relinquishment of blamable impulses; this has been subjected to a fivefold division, as the 'five vows,' ahiṃsā, sūnṛta, asteya, brahmacaryā, and aparigraha.[18]

units.sanskrit: न यत्प्रमादयोगेन जीवितव्यपरोपणम्। चराणां स्थावराणां च तदहिंसाब्रतं मतम्।
units.english: "The 'vow' of ahiṃsā is the avoidance of injuring life by any act of thoughtlessness in any movable or immovable thing.

units.sanskrit: प्रियं पथ्यं वचस्तथ्यं सूनृतं ब्रतमुच्यते॥
units.english: "A kind, salutary, and truthful speech is called the 'vow' of sūnṛta.

units.sanskrit: तत्तथ्यमपि नो तथ्यमप्रियं चाहितं च यत्।
units.english: That truthful speech is not truthful, which is unkind to others and prejudicial.

units.sanskrit: अनादानमदत्तस्यास्तेयव्रतमुदीरितम्। बाह्याः प्राणा नृणामर्थों हरता तं हता हि ते।
units.english: "The not taking what is not given is declared to be the 'vow' of asteya; the external life is a man's property, and, when it is killed, it is killed by some one who seizes it.

units.sanskrit: दिव्यौदरिककामानां कृतानुमतकारिकतैः। मनोवाक्कायतस्त्यागो ब्रह्माष्टादशधा मतम्॥
units.english: "The 'vow' of brahmacaryā (chastity) is eighteen-fold, viz., the abandonment of all desires,[19] heavenly or earthly, in thought, word, and deed, and whether by one's own action or by one's consent, or by one's causing another to act.

units.sanskrit: सर्वभावेषु मूर्छायास्त्यागः स्यादपरिग्रहः। यदसत्स्वपि जायेत मूर्छया चित्तविल्पवः।
units.english: "The 'vow' of aparigraha is the renouncing of all delusive interest in everything that exists not; since bewilderment of thought may arise from a delusive interest even in the unreal.

units.sanskrit: भावनाभिर्भावितानि पञ्चभिः पञ्चधा क्रमात्। महाव्रतानि लोकस्य साधयन्त्यव्ययं पदम्॥
units.english: "When carried out by the five states of mind in a fivefold order, these great 'vows' of the world produce the eternal abode."

units.sanskrit: भावनापञ्चकप्रपञ्चनं च प्ररूपितम्हास्यलोभभयक्रोधप्रत्याख्यानैर्निरन्तरम्। आलोच्य भाषणेनापि भावयेत्सूनृतं व्रतम्॥ इत्यादिना।
units.english: "Let him carry out the 'vow' of sūnṛta uninterruptedly by the abstinence from laughter, greed, fear, and anger, and by the deliberate avoidance of speech,"[20]—and so forth.

units.sanskrit: एतानि सम्यग्दर्शनज्ञानचारित्राणि मिलितानि मोक्षकारणं न प्रत्येकम्। यथा रसायनम्। तथा चात्र ज्ञानश्रद्धानाचरणानि संभूय फलं साधयन्ति न प्रत्येकम्।
units.english: These three, right intuition, right knowledge, and right conduct, when united, produce liberation, but not severally; just as, in the case of an elixir, it is the knowledge of what it is, faith in its virtues, and the actual application of the medicine,[21] united, which produce the elixir's effect, but not severally.

units.sanskrit: अत्र संक्षेपतस्तावज्जीवाजीवाख्ये द्वे तत्त्वे स्तः। तत्र बोधात्मको जीवः। अबोधात्मकस्त्वजीवः।
units.english: Here we may say concisely that the tattvas or predicaments are two, jīva and ajīva; the soul, jīva, is pure intelligence; the non-soul, ajīva, is pure non-intelligence.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं पद्मनन्दिना - चिदचिद् द्वे परे तत्त्वे विवेकस्तद्विवेचनम्। उपादेयमुपादेयं हेयं हेयं च कु र्वतः॥
units.english: Padmanandin has thus said— "The two highest predicaments are 'soul' and 'non-soul;' 'discrimination' is the power of discriminating these two, in one who pursues what is to be pursued, and rejects what is to be rejected.

units.sanskrit: हेयं हि कर्तृरागादि तत्कार्यमविवेकिता। उपादेयं परं ज्योतिरुपयोगैकलक्षणम॥इति॥
units.english: The affection, &c., of the agent are to be rejected; these are objects for the non-discriminating; the supreme light [of knowledge] is alone to be pursued, which is defined as upayoga."

units.sanskrit: सहूजचिद्रपपरिणतिं स्वीकु र्वाणे ज्ञानदर्शने उपयोगः। स परस्परप्रदेशानां प्रदेशबन्धात्कर्मणैकीभूतस्यात्मनोन्यत्वप्रतिपत्तिकारणं भवति। सकलजीवसाधारणं चैतन्यमुपशमक्षयक्षयोपशमवशादौपशमिकक्षयात्मकक्षायौपशमिकभावेन कर्मोंदयवशात्कलुषान्याकारेण च परिणतजीवपर्यायविवक्षायां जीवस्वरूपं भवति।
units.english: Upayoga [or "the true employment of the soul's activities"] takes place when the vision of true knowledge recognises the manifestation of the soul's innate nature; but as long as the soul, by the bond of pradeśa and the mutual interpenetration of form which it produces [between the soul and the body], considers itself as identified with its actions [and the body which they produce], knowledge should rather be defined as "the cause of its recognising that it is other than these."[22]

units.sanskrit: यदवोचद्वाचकाचार्यःऔपशमिकक्षायिकौ भावौ मिश्रश्च जीवस्य स्वतत्त्वमौदयिकपारिणामिकौ च (त.सू.२/१) इति।
units.english: "The aupaśamika, the Kṣāyika, and the 'mixed' states are the nature of the soul, and also the audayika and the Pāriṇāmika."

units.sanskrit: आर्हततत्त्वानुसंधानवशाद्रागादिपङ्कक्षालनेन निर्मलतापादकः क्षायिको भावः। कर्मणः क्षये सति जायमानो भावः क्षायिकः यथा पङ्कात्पृथग्भूतस्य निर्मलस्य स्फटिकादिभाजनान्तर्गतस्य जलस्य स्वच्छता। यथा मोक्षः।
units.english: The aupaśamika state of the soul arises when all the effects of past actions have ceased, and no new actions arise [to affect the future], as when water becomes temporarily pure through the defiling mud sinking to the bottom by the influence of the clearing nut-plant,[25] &c. The Kṣāyika state arises when there is the absolute abolition of actions and their effects, as in final liberation.

units.sanskrit: उभयात्मा भावो मिश्रः। यथा जलस्यार्धस्वच्छता।
units.english: The "mixed" (miśra) state combines both these, as when water is partly pure.

units.sanskrit: कर्मोंदये सति भवन्भाव औदयिकः।
units.english: The audayika state is when actions arise [exerting an inherent influence on the future].

units.sanskrit: कर्मोंपशमाद्यनपेक्षःसहजोभावश्चेतनत्वादिःपारिणामिकः।
units.english: The Pāriṇāmika state is the soul's innate condition, as pure intelligence, &c., and disregarding its apparent states, as (1), (2), (3), (4).[26] This nature, in one of the above-described varieties, is the character of every soul whether happy or unhappy.

units.sanskrit: तदेतद्यथासंभवं भव्यस्याभव्यस्य वा जीवस्य स्वरूपमिति सूत्रार्थः।
units.english: This is the meaning of the sūtra quoted above. This has been explained in the Svarūpa-sambodhana—

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं स्वरूपसंबोधने ज्ञानाद्भिन्नो न नाभिन्नो भिन्नाभिन्नः कथंचन। ज्ञानं पूर्वापरीभूतं सोयमात्मेति कीर्तितः॥
units.english: "Not different from knowledge, and yet not identical with it,—in some way both different and the same,—knowledge is its first and last; such is the soul described to be."

units.sanskrit: ननु भेदाभेदयोः परस्परपरिहारेणावस्थानादन्यतरस्यैव वास्तवत्वादुभयात्मकत्वमयु क्तमिति चेत्तदयुक्तम्। बाधे प्रमाणाभावात्।
units.english: If you say that, "As difference and identity are mutually exclusive, we must have one or the other in the case of the soul, and its being equally both is absurd," we reply, that there is no evidence to support you when you characterise it as absurd.

units.sanskrit: अनुपलम्भो हि बाधकं प्रमाणम्। न सोस्ति। समस्तेषु वस्तुष्वनेकान्तांत्मकत्वस्य स्याद्वादिनो मते सुप्रसिद्धत्वादित्यलम्।
units.english: Only a valid non-perception[27] can thus preclude a suggestion as absurd; but this is not found in the present case, since (in the opinion of us, the advocates of the Syād-vāda) it is perfectly notorious that all things present a mingled nature of many contradictory attributes.

units.sanskrit: अपरे पुनर्जीवाजीवयोरपरं प्रपञ्चमाचक्षते जीवाकाशधर्मा धर्मपुद्गलास्तिकायभेदात्।
units.english: Others lay down a different set of tattvas from the two mentioned above, jīva and ajīva; they hold that there are five astikāyas or categories,—jīva, ākāśa, dharma, adharma, and pudgala.

units.sanskrit: एतेषु पञ्चसु तत्त्वेषु कालत्रयसंबन्धितयास्तीति स्थितिव्यपदेशः। अनेकप्रदेशत्वेन शरीरवत्कायव्यपदेशः।
units.english: To all these five we can apply the idea of "existence" (asti),[28] as connected with the three divisions of time, and we can similarly apply the idea of "body" (kāya),[29] from their occupying several parts of space.

units.sanskrit: तत्र जीवा द्विविधाः संसारिणो मुक्ताश्च। भवाद्भवान्तरप्राप्तिमन्तः संसारिणः। ते च द्विविधाः, समनस्का अमनस्काश्च। तत्र संज्ञिनः समनस्काः।
units.english: The jīvas (souls) are divided into two, the "mundane" and the "released." The "mundane" pass from birth to birth; and these are also divided into two, as those possessing an internal sense (samanaska), and those destitute of it (amanaska).

units.sanskrit: शिक्षाक्रियालापग्रहणरूपा संज्ञा। तद्विधुरास्त्वमनस्काः।
units.english: The former possesses saṃjñā, i.e., the power of apprehension, talking, acting, and receiving instruction; the latter are those without this power.

units.sanskrit: ते चामनस्का द्विविधाः, त्रसस्थावरभेदात्।
units.english: These latter are also divided into two, as "locomotive" (trasa), or "immovable" (sthāvara).

units.sanskrit: तत्र द्वीन्द्रियादयः शङ्खगण्डोलकप्रभृतयश्चतुर्विधास्त्रसाः। पृथिव्यप्तेजोवायुवनस्पतयः स्थावराः।
units.english: The "locomotive" are those possessing at least two senses [touch and taste], as shell-fish, worms, &c., and are thus of four kinds [as possessing two, three, four, or five senses]; the "immovable" are earth, water, fire, air, and trees.[30] But here a distinction must be made.

units.sanskrit: तत्र मार्गगत धूलिः पृथिवी। इष्टकादिः पृथिवीकायः। पृथिवीकायत्वेन येन गृहीता स पृथिवीकायिकः। पृथिवींकायत्वेन यो ग्रहीष्यति स पृथिवीजीवः। एवमबादिष्वपि भेदचतुष्टयं योज्यम्।
units.english: The dust of the road is properly "earth," but bricks, &c., are aggregated "bodies of earth," and that soul by whom this body is appropriated becomes "earthen-bodied," and that soul which will hereafter appropriate it is the "earth-soul." The same four divisions must also be applied to the others, water, &c.

units.sanskrit: तत्र पृथिव्यादि कायत्वेन गृहीतवन्तो ग्रहीष्यन्तश्च स्थावरा गृह्यन्ते न पृथिव्यादिपृथिवीकायादयः। तेषामजीवत्वात्। ते च स्थावराः स्पर्शनैके न्द्रियाः।
units.english: Now the souls which have appropriated or will appropriate the earth, &c., as their bodies, are reckoned as "immovable;" but earth, &c., and the "bodies of earth," &c., are not so reckoned, because they are inanimate.[31] These other immovable things, and such as only possess the one sense of touch, are considered as "released," since they are incapable of passing into any other state of existence.

units.sanskrit: भवान्तरप्राप्तिविधुरा मुक्ताः। धर्माधर्माकाशास्तिकायास्त एकत्वशालिनो निष्क्रियाश्च द्रव्यस्य देशान्तरप्राप्तिहेतवः।
units.english: Dharma, adharma, and ākāśa are singular categories [and not generic], and they have not the attribute of "action," but they are the causes of a substance's change of place.

units.sanskrit: तत्र धर्माधर्मौ प्रसिद्धौ।
units.english: Dharma, "merit," and adharma, "demerit," are well known.

units.sanskrit: आलोके नावच्छिन्ने नभसि लोकाकाशपदवेदनीये तयोः सर्वत्रावस्थितिः। गतिस्थित्युपग्रहो धर्माधर्मयोरुपकारः। अत एव धर्मास्तिकायः प्रवृत्त्यनुमेयः। अधर्मास्तिकायः स्थित्यनुमेयः।
units.english: They assist souls in progressing or remaining stationary in the universally extended[32] sky [or ether] characterised by light, and also called Lokākāśa; hence the presence of the category "merit" is to be inferred from progress, that of "demerit" from stationariness.

units.sanskrit: अन्यवस्तुप्रदेशमध्येन्यस्य वस्तुनः प्रवेशोवगाहः। तदाकाशकृत्यम्।
units.english: The effect of ākāśa is seen when one thing enters into the space previously occupied by another.

units.sanskrit: स्पर्शरसगन्धवर्णवन्तः पुद्गलाः (त.सू.५/२४)।
units.english: Pudgala, "body," possesses touch, taste, and colour.

units.sanskrit: ते च द्विविधा अणवः स्कन्धाश्च।
units.english: Bodies are of two kinds, atomic and compound.

units.sanskrit: द्यणुकादयः स्कन्धाः। तत्र द्यणुकादिस्कन्धभेदादण्वादिरूत्पद्यते।
units.english: Atoms are produced by the separation of these binary and other compounds, while these arise from the conjunction of atoms.

units.sanskrit: क्वचिद्भेदसंघाताभ्यां स्कन्धोत्पत्तिः (त.सू.५/२६) अत एव पूरयन्ति गलन्तीति पुद्गलाः।
units.english: Compounds sometimes arise from separation and conjunction [combined]; hence they are called pudgalas, because they "fill" (pūr), and "dissolve" (gal).

units.sanskrit: कालस्यानेकप्रदेशत्वाभावेनास्तिकायत्वाभावेपि द्रव्यत्वमस्ति। तल्लक्षणयोगात्। तदुक्तं गुणपर्यायवद् द्रव्यम् ( त.सू.५/३८) इति द्रव्याश्रया निर्गुणागुणा (त.सू.५/३९)। यथा जीवस्य ज्ञानत्वादिधर्मरूपाः पुद्गलस्य रूपत्वादिसामान्यस्वभावाः। धर्माधर्माकाशकालानां यथासंभवं गतिस्थित्यवगाहवर्तनाहेतुत्वादिसामान्यानि गुणाः।
units.english: Although "time" is not properly an astikāya, because it does not occupy many separate parts of space [as mentioned in the definition], still it is a dravya [or tattva], as the definition will hold; "substance" (dravya) possesses "qualities and action."[34] Qualities reside in substance but do not themselves possess qualities, as the general qualities, knowledge, &c., of the jīva, form, &c., of the body, and the power of causing progress, stationariness, and motion into a place previously occupied, in the case respectively of "merit," "demerit," and ākāśa.

units.sanskrit: उत्पादस्तद्भावः परिणामः पर्याय इति पर्यायाः। यथा जीवस्य घटादिज्ञानसुखक्लेशादयः। पुद्गलस्य मृत्पिण्डघटादयः।
units.english: "Action" (paryāya) has thus been defined; the actions (paryāyāḥ) of a substance are, as has been said, its existence, its production, its being what it is, its development, its course to the end, as, e.g., in the jīva, the knowledge of objects, as of a jar, &c., happiness, pain, &c.; in the pudgala, the lump of clay, the jar, &c.; in merit and demerit, the special functions of progress, &c.

units.sanskrit: धर्मादीनां गत्यादिविशेषाः अत एव षड् द्रव्याणीति प्रसिद्धिः।
units.english: Thus there are six substances or tattvas [i.e., the five above mentioned and "time"].

units.sanskrit: के चन सप्त तत्तवानीति वर्णयन्ति।
units.english: Others reckon the tattvas as seven, as has been said—

units.sanskrit: तदाहजीवाजीवास्रवबन्धसंवरनिर्जरमोक्षास्तत्त्वानि। (त.सू.१/४) इति। तत्र जीवाजीवौ निरूपितौ।
units.english: "The tattvas are jīva, ajīva, āsrava, bandha, saṃvara, nirjarā, and mokṣa." Jīva and ajīva have been already described.

units.sanskrit: आस्रवो निरुप्यतेऔदारिकादिकायादिचलनद्वारेणात्मनश्चलनं योगपदवेदनीयमास्रवः।
units.english: Āsrava is described as the movement of the soul called yoga,[35] through its participation in the movement of its various bodies, audārika, &c.

units.sanskrit: यथा सलिलावगाहि द्वारं जलाद्यास्रवणकारणत्वादास्रव इति। निगद्यते तथा योगप्रणाडिकया कर्मास्रवतीति स योग आस्रवः।
units.english: As a door opening into the water is called āsrava, because it causes the stream to descend through it,[36] so this yoga is called āsrava, because by it as by a pipe actions and their consequences flow in upon the soul.

units.sanskrit: यथार्द्रं वस्त्रं समन्ताद्वातानीतं रेणुजातमुपादत्ते तथा कषायजलार्द्र आत्मा योगानीतं कर्म सर्वप्रदेशैगृह्नाति। यथा वा निष्टप्तायःपिण्डो जले क्षिप्तोम्भः समन्ताद् गृह्नाति तथा कषायोष्णो जीवो योगानीतं कर्म समन्तादादत्ते।
units.english: Or, as a wet garment collects the dust brought to it from every side by the wind, so the soul, wet with previous sins, collects, by its manifold points of contact with the body, the actions which are brought to it by yoga. Or as, when water is thrown on a heated lump of iron, the iron absorbs the water altogether, so the jīva, heated by previous sins, receives from every side the actions which are brought by yoga.

units.sanskrit: कषति हिनस्त्यात्मानं कु गतिप्रापणादिति कषायः क्रोधो मानो माया लोभश्च।
units.english: Kaṣāya ("sin," "defilement") is so called because it "hurts" (kash) the soul by leading it into evil states; it comprises anger, pride, delusion, and lust.

units.sanskrit: स द्विविधः शुभाशुभभेदात्।
units.english: Āsrava is twofold, as good or evil.

units.sanskrit: अत्राहिंसादिः शुभः काययोगः। सत्यमितहितभाषणादिः शुभो वाग्योगः।
units.english: Thus abstaining from doing injury is a good yoga of the body; speaking what is true, measured, and profitable is a good yoga of the speech.

units.sanskrit: तदेतदास्रवभेदप्रभेदजातं कायवाङ्मनःकर्मयोगः। स आस्रवः। शुभः पुण्यस्य।
units.english: "Āsrava is the impulse to action with body, speech, or mind, and it is good or evil as it produces merit or demerit," &c.

units.sanskrit: अपरे त्वेवं मेनिरेआस्रवयति पुरुषं विषयेष्यिन्द्रियप्रवृत्तिरास्रवः। इन्द्रियद्वारा हि पौरुषं ज्योतिर्विषयान्स्पृशद्रूपादिज्ञानरूपेण परिणमत इति।
units.english: Others, however, explain it thus:—"Āsrava is the action of the senses which impels the soul towards external objects; the light of the soul, coming in contact with external objects by means of the senses, becomes developed as the knowledge of form, &c."[37]

units.sanskrit: मिथ्यादर्शनाविरतिप्रमादकषायवशाद्योगवशाच्चात्मा सूक्ष्मैकक्षेत्रावगाहिनामनन्तप्रदेशानां पुद्गालानां कर्मबन्धयोग्यानामादानमुपश्लेषणं यत्करोति स बन्धः। तदुक्तं सकषायत्वाज्जीवः कर्मभावयोग्यान्पुद्गलानादत्ते स बन्धः।
units.english: Bandha, "bondage," is when the soul, by the influence of "false intuition," "non-indifference," "carelessness," and "sin" (kaṣāya), and also by the force of yoga, assumes various bodies occupying many parts of space, which enter into its own subtile body, and which are suited to the bond of its previous actions.
As has been said—

units.sanskrit: तत्र कषायग्रहणं सर्वबन्धहेतूपलक्षणार्थम्।
units.english: In this quotation the word "sin" (kaṣāya) is used to include the other three causes of bondage as well as that properly so termed.

units.sanskrit: बन्धहेतून्पपाठ वाचकाचार्यः - मिथ्यादर्शनाविरतिप्रमादकषायोगा बन्धहेतवः (त.सू.८/१) इति मिथ्यादर्शनं द्विविधं मिथ्याकर्मोंदयात्परोपदेशानपेक्षं तत्त्वाश्रद्धानं नैसर्गिकमेकम्। अपरं परोपदेशजम्।
units.english: Vācakācārya has thus enumerated the causes of bondage: "The causes of bondage are false intuition, non-indifference, carelessness, and sin." (a) "False intuition" is twofold,—either innate from one's natural character, as when one disbelieves Jaina doctrines from the influence of former evil actions, irrespectively of another's teaching,—or derived, when learned by another's teaching.

units.sanskrit: पृथिव्यादिषट्कोपादानं षडिन्द्रियासंयमनं चाविरतिः।
units.english: (b) "Non-indifference" is the non-restraint of the five senses, and the internal organ from the set of six, earth, &c.

units.sanskrit: पञ्चसमितित्रिगुप्तिष्वनुत्साहः प्रमादः।
units.english: (c) "Carelessness" (pramāda) is a want of effort to practise the five kinds of samiti, gupti, &c.

units.sanskrit: कषायः क्रोधादिः।
units.english: (d) "Sin" consists of anger, &c.

units.sanskrit: तत्र कषायान्ताः स्थित्यनुभवबन्धहेतवः प्रकृतिप्रदेशबन्धहेतुर्योंग इति विभागाः।
units.english: Here we must make the distinction that the four things, false intuition, &c., cause those kinds of bondage called sthiti and anubhāva; yoga [or āsrava] causes those kinds called prakṛti and pradeśa.

units.sanskrit: बन्धश्चतुर्विध इत्युक्तं प्रकृतिस्थित्यनुभवप्रदेशास्तद्विधयः (त.सू.८/३) इति।
units.english: "Bondage" is fourfold, as has been said: "Prakṛti, sthiti, anubhāva, and pradeśa are its four kinds."

units.sanskrit: यथा निम्बगुडादेस्तिक्तत्वमधुरत्वादिस्वभाव एवमावरणीयस्य ज्ञानदर्शनावरणत्वमादित्यप्रभाच्छादकाम्भोधरवत्प्रदीपप्रभातिरोधायककु म्भवच्च।
units.english: Thus obstructions (āvaraṇa)[39] cloud the knowledge and intuition, as a cloud obscures the sun or a shade the lamp. This is (a) jnānāvaraṇa, or (b) darśanāvaraṇa.

units.sanskrit: सदसद्वेदनीयस्य सुखदुःखोत्पादकत्वमसिधारामधुलेहनवत्।
units.english: (c) An object recognised as simultaneously existing or non-existing produces mingled pleasure and pain, as licking honey from a sword's edge,—this is vedanīya.

units.sanskrit: दर्शने महनीयस्य तत्त्वार्थाश्रद्धानकारित्वं दुर्जन - सङ्गवत्। चारित्रे मोहनीयस्यासंयमहेतुत्वं मद्यमदवत्।
units.english: (d) A delusion (mohanīya) in intuition produces want of faith in the Jaina categories, like association with the wicked; delusion in conduct produces want of self-restraint, like intoxication.

units.sanskrit: आयुषो देहबन्धकर्तृत्वं जलवत्। नाम्नो विचित्रनामकारित्वं चित्रिकवत्।
units.english: (e) Āyus produces the bond of body, like a snare.[40] (f) Nāman, or "the name," produces various individual appellations, as a painter paints his different pictures.

units.sanskrit: गोत्रस्योच्चनीचकारित्वं कु म्भकारवत्।
units.english: (g) Gotra produces the idea of noble and ignoble, as the potter fashions his pots.

units.sanskrit: दानादीनां विघ्ननिदानत्वमन्तरायस्य स्वभावः कोशाध्यक्षवत्।
units.english: (h) Antarāya produces obstacles to liberality, &c., as the treasurer hinders the king by considerations of economy.

units.sanskrit: सोयं प्रकृतिबन्धोष्टविधो द्रव्यकर्मावान्तरभेदमूलप्रकृतिवेदनीयः।
units.english: Thus is the prakṛti-bandha eightfold, being denominated as the eight mūla-prakṛtis, with subdivisions according to the different actions of the various subject-matter.

units.sanskrit: तथावोचदुमास्वातिवाचकाचार्यः आद्योज्ञानदर्शनावरणवेदनीयमोहनीयायुर्नामगोत्रान्तरायाः (त.सू.८/४) इति। तद्भेदं च समगृह्यात्पञ्च नवद्वयष्टार्विंशतिचतुर्द्विचत्वारिंशद्द्विपञ्चभेदा यथाक्रमम् ( त.सू.८/५) इति।
units.english: And thus has Umāsvāti-vācakācārya[41] declared: "The first kind of bandha consists of obstructions of the knowledge and the intuition, vedanīya, mohanīya, āyus, nāman, gotra, and antarāya;" and he has also reckoned up the respective subdivisions of each as five, nine, twenty-eight, four, two, forty, two, and fifteen.

units.sanskrit: एतच्च सर्वं विद्यानन्दादिभिर्विवृतमिति विस्तरभयान्न प्रस्तूयते।
units.english: All this has been explained at full length in the Vidyānanda and other works, and here is omitted through fear of prolixity.

units.sanskrit: यथाजागोमहिष्यादिक्षीराणामेतावन्तमनेहसं माधुर्यस्वभावादप्रच्युतिस्थितिस्तथा ज्ञानावरणादीनां मूलप्रकृतीनामादितस्तिसृणामन्तरायस्य च त्रिंशत्सागरोपमकोटिकोटयः परास्थितिः (त.सू.८/१४) इत्याद्युक्तकाला दर्दान्तवत्स्वीयस्वभावादुप्रच्युतिस्थिति।
units.english: As the milk of the goat, cow, buffalo, &c., have continued unswerving from their sweet nature for so long a period, so the first three mūla-prakṛtis, jnānāvaraṇa, &c., and the last, antarāya, have not swerved from their respective natures even through the period described in the words, "sthiti lasts beyonds crores of crores of periods of time measured by thirty sāgaropamas."[42] This continuance is sthiti.

units.sanskrit: यथाजागोमहिष्यादिक्षीराणां तीव्रमन्दादिभावेन स्वकार्यकरणे सामर्थ्यविशेषोनुभावस्तथा कर्मपुद्गलानां स्वकार्यकरणे सामर्थ्यविशेषोनुभावः।
units.english: As in the milk of goats, cows, buffaloes, &c., there exists, by its rich or poor nature, a special capacity for producing[43] its several effects, so in the different material bodies produced by our actions there exists a special capacity (anubhāva) for producing their respective effects.

units.sanskrit: कर्मभावपरिणतपुद्गलस्कन्धानामनन्तान्तप्रदेशानामात्मप्रदेशानुप्रवेशः प्रदेशबन्धः।
units.english: The bandha called pradeśa is the entrance into the different parts of the soul by the masses, made up of an endless number of parts, of the various bodies which are developed by the consequences of actions.

units.sanskrit: आस्रवनिरोधः संवरः येनात्मनि प्रविशत्कर्म प्रतिषिध्यते स गुप्तिसमित्यादिः संवरः।
units.english: Saṃvara is the stopping of āsrava—that by which the influence of past actions (karman) is stopped from entering into the soul.

units.sanskrit: संचारकारणायोगादात्मनो गोपनं गुप्तिः। सा त्रिविधा कायवाङ्मनोनिग्रहभेदात्।
units.english: Gupti is the withdrawal of the soul from that "impulse" (yoga) which causes mundane existence,—it is threefold, as relating to body, speech, or mind.

units.sanskrit: प्राणिपीडापरिहारेण सम्यगयनं समितिः।
units.english: Samiti is the acting so as to avoid injury to all living beings.

units.sanskrit: सेर्याभाषादिभेदात्पञ्चधा। प्रपञ्चितं च हेमचन्द्राचार्यैः।
units.english: This is divided into five kinds, as īryā,[44] bhāṣā, &c., as has been explained by Hemacandra.

units.sanskrit: लोकातिवाहिते मार्गे चुम्बिते भास्वदंशुभिः। जन्तुरक्षार्थमालोक्य गतिरीर्या मता सताम्॥
units.english: "In a public highway, kissed by the sun's rays, to walk circumspectly so as to avoid injuring living beings, this the good call īryā.

units.sanskrit: अनवद्यमृतं सर्वजनीनं मितभाषणम्। प्रिया वाचंयमानां सा भाषासमितिरुच्यते॥
units.english: "Let him practise[45] a measured utterance in his intercourse with all people; this is called bhāṣā-samiti, dear to the restrainers of speech.

units.sanskrit: द्विचत्वारिंशता भिक्षादोषैर्नित्यमदूषितम्। मुनिर्यदन्नमादत्ते सैषणासमितिर्मता॥
units.english: "The food which the sage takes, ever free from the forty-two faults which may accrue to alms, is called the eṣaṇā-samiti.[46]

units.sanskrit: आसनदीनि संवीक्ष्य प्रतिलङ्घय च यत्नतः। गृह्णीयान्निक्षिपेद्धयायेत्सादानसमितिः स्मृता।
units.english: "Carefully looking at it and carefully seating himself upon it, let him take a seat, &c., set it down, and meditate,—this is called the ādāna-samiti.

units.sanskrit: यत्नाद्यदुत्सृजेत्साधुः सोत्सर्गसमितिर्भवेत्॥ आस्रवः स्रोतसो द्वारं संवृणोतीति संवरः। इति निराहुः। तदुक्तमभियुक्तैः - अस्रवो भवहेतुः स्यात्संवरो मोक्षकारणम्। इतीयमार्हती सृष्टिरन्यदस्याः प्रपञ्चनम्॥
units.english: "That the good man should carefully perform his bodily evacuations in a spot free from all living creatures,[47]—this is the utsarga-samiti.[48] Hence samvara has been etymologically analysed as that which closes (sam + vṛṇoti) the door of the stream of āsrava,[49] as has been said by the learned, 'Āsrava is the cause of mundane existence, saṃvara is the cause of liberation;[50] this is the Ārhat doctrine in a handful; all else is only the amplification of this.'"

units.sanskrit: अर्जितस्य कर्मणस्तपःप्रभृतिभिर्निर्जरणं निर्जराख्यं तत्त्वम्। चिरकालप्रवृत्तकषायकलापं पुण्यं सुखदुःखे च देहेन जरयति नाशयति के शोल्लुञ्चनादिकं तप उच्यते।
units.english: Nirjarā is the causing the fruit of past actions to decay by self-mortification, &c.; it destroys by the body the merit and demerit of all the previously performed actions, and the resulting happiness and misery; "self-mortification" means the plucking out of the hair, &c.

units.sanskrit: सा निर्जरा द्विविधा यथाकालौपक्रमिकभेदात्।
units.english: This nirjarā is twofold,[51] "temporary" (yathākāla) and ancillary (aupakramaṇika).

units.sanskrit: तत्र प्रथमा यस्मिन्काले यत्कर्म फलप्रदत्वेनाभिमतं तस्मिन्नेव काले फलदानाद्भवन्ती निर्जरा कामादिपाकजेति च जेगीयते।
units.english: It is "temporary" as when a desire is dormant in consequence of the action having produced its fruit, and at that particular time, from this completion of the object aimed at, nirjarā arises, being caused by the consumption of the desire, &c.

units.sanskrit: यत्कर्म तपोबलात्स्वकामनयोदयावलिं प्रवेश्य प्रपद्यते सौपक्रमिकनिर्जरा।
units.english: But when, by the force of asceticism, the sage turns all actions into means for attaining his end (liberation), this is the nirjarā of actions.

units.sanskrit: यदाह - संसारबीजभूतानां कर्मणां जरणादिह। निर्जरा संमता द्वेधा सकामाकामनिर्जरा॥
units.english: Thus it has been said: "From the decaying of the actions which are the seeds of mundane existence, nirjarā arises, which is twofold, sakāmā and akāmā.

units.sanskrit: स्मृता सकामा यमिनामकामा त्वन्यदेहिनाम॥इति॥
units.english: That called sakāmā belongs to ascetics, the akāmā to other embodied spirits."[52]

units.sanskrit: मिथ्यादर्शनादीनां वन्धहेतूनां निरोधेभिनवकर्माभावान्निर्जरा हेतुसन्निधानेनार्जितस्य कर्मणो निरसनादात्यन्तिककर्ममोक्षणं मोक्षः। तदाहबन्धहेत्वभावनिर्जराभ्यां कृत्स्नकर्मविप्रमोक्षणं मोक्षः (त.सू.१०/२) इति।
units.english: Mokṣa. Since at the moment of its attainment there is an entire absence of all future actions, as all the causes of bondage (false perception, &c.) are stopped,[53] and since all past actions are abolished in the presence of the causes of nirjarā, there arises the absolute release from all actions,—this is mokṣa; as it has been said: "Mokṣa is the absolute release from all actions by the decay (nirjarā) of the causes of bondage and of existence."

units.sanskrit: तदनन्तरमूर्ध्वे गच्छत्यालोकान्तात् ( त.सू.१०/५)।
units.english: Then the soul rises upward to the end of the world.

units.sanskrit: यथा हस्तदण्डादिभ्रामिप्रेरितं कु लालचक्रमुपरतेपि तस्मिस्तद्बलादेवसंस्कारक्षयं भ्रमति तथा भवस्थेनात्मनापवर्गप्राप्तये बहुशो यत्कृतं प्रणिधानं मुक्तस्य तदभावेपि पूर्वसंस्कारादालोकान्तं गमनमुपपद्यते। यथा वा मृत्तिकालेपकृतगौरवमलाबुद्रव्यं जलेधः पतति पुनरपेतमृत्तिकाबन्धमूर्ध्वं गच्छति तथा कर्मरहित आत्मा असङ्गत्वादूर्ध्वं गच्छति। बन्धच्छेदादेरण्डबीजबच्चोर्ध्वं गतिस्वभावाच्चाग्निशिखावत्।
units.english: As a potter's wheel, whirled by the stick and hands, moves on even after these have stopped, until the impulse is exhausted, so the previous repeated contemplations of the embodied soul for the attainment of mokṣa exert their influence even after they have ceased, and bear the soul onward to the end of the world; or, as the gourd, encased with clay, sinks in the water, but rises to the surface when freed from its encumbrance, so the soul, delivered from works, rises upward by its isolation,[54] from the bursting of its bonds like the elastic seed of the castor-oil plant, or by its own native tendency like the flame.

units.sanskrit: अन्योन्यं प्रदेशानुप्रवेशे सत्यविभागेनावस्थानं बन्धः। परस्परप्राप्तिमात्रं सङ्गः।
units.english: "Bondage" is the condition of being unseparated, with a mutual interpenetration of parts [between the soul and the body]; saṅga is merely mutual contact.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं पूर्वप्रयोगादसङ्गत्वाद्वन्धच्छेदात्तथा गतिपरिणामाच्च (त.सू.१०/६)। आविद्धकु लालचक्रवद्व्ययपगतलेपालाबुवदेरण्डबीजवदग्निशिखावच्च (त.सू.१०/७) इति।
units.english: This has been declared as follows:— "[Liberation] is unhindered, from the continuance of former impulses, from the absence of saṅga, from the cutting of all bonds, and from the natural development of the soul's own powers of motion, like the potter's wheel, the gourd with its clay removed, the seed of the castor-oil plant, or the flame of fire."

units.sanskrit: अत एव पठन्ति।
units.english: Hence they recite a śloka:—

units.sanskrit: गत्वा गत्वा निवर्तन्ते चन्द्रसूर्यादयो ग्रहाः।
units.english: "However often they go away, the planets return, the sun, moon, and the rest;

units.sanskrit: अद्यापि न निवर्तन्ते त्वलोकाकाशमागताः॥ (प.न.) इति।
units.english: "But never to this day have returned any who have gone to Ālokākāśa."

units.sanskrit: अन्ये तु गतसमस्तक्लेशतद्वासनस्यानावरणज्ञानस्य सुखैकतानस्यात्मन उपरिदेशावस्थानं मुक्तिरित्यास्थिषत।
units.english: Others hold mokṣa to be the abiding in the highest regions, the soul being absorbed in bliss, with its knowledge unhindered and itself untainted by any pain or impression thereof.

units.sanskrit: एवमुक्तानि सुखदुःखसाधनाभ्यां पुण्यपापाभ्यां सहितानि नव पदार्थान् के चनाङ्गीचक्रुः।
units.english: Others hold nine tattvas, adding "merit" and "demerit" to the foregoing seven,—these two being the causes of pleasure and pain.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं सिद्धान्ते जीवाजीवौ पुण्यपापयुतावास्रवः संवरो निर्जरणं बन्धो मोक्षश्च नव तत्त्वानीति। संग्रहे प्रवृत्ता वयमुपरताः स्मः।
units.english: This has been declared in the Siddhānta, "Jīva, ajīva, puṇya, pāpa, āsrava, saṃvara, nirjaraṇa, bandha, and mokṣa, are the nine tattvas." As our object is only a summary, we desist here.

units.sanskrit: अत्र सर्वत्र सप्तभङ्गिनयाख्यं न्यायमवतारयन्ति जैनाः। स्यादस्ति स्यान्नास्ति स्यादस्ति च नास्ति च स्यादवक्तव्यः स्यादस्ति चावक्तव्यः स्यान्नास्ति चावक्तव्यः स्यादस्ति च नास्ति चावक्तव्य इति। तत्सर्वमनन्तवीर्यः प्रत्यपीपदत् - तद्विधानविवक्षायां स्यादस्तीति गतिर्भवेत्।
units.english: Here the Jainas everywhere introduce their favourite logic called the sapta-bhaṅgī-naya,[55] or the system of the seven paralogisms, "may be, it is," "may be, it is not," "may be, it is and it is not," "may be, it is not predicable," "may be, it is, and yet not predicable," "may be, it is not, and not predicable," "may be, it is and it is not, and not predicable." All this Anantavīrya has thus laid down:—

units.sanskrit: स्यान्नास्तीति प्रयोगः स्यात्तन्निषेधे विवक्षिते॥
units.english: "When you wish to establish a thing, the proper course is to say 'may be, it is;' when you wish to deny it, 'may be, it is not.'

units.sanskrit: क्रमेणोभयवाञ्छायां प्रयोगः समुदायभाक्। युगपत्तद्विवक्षायां स्यादवाच्यमशक्तितः।
units.english: "When you desire to establish each in turn, let your procedure likewise embrace both; when you wish to establish both at once, let it be declared 'indescribable' from the impossibility to describe it.

units.sanskrit: आद्यावाच्यविवक्षायां पञ्चमो भङ्ग इष्यते। अन्त्यावाच्यविवक्षायां षष्ठभङ्गसमुद्भवः॥
units.english: "The fifth process is enjoined when you wish to establish the first as well as its indescribableness; when the second as well as its indescribableness, the occasion for the sixth process arises.

units.sanskrit: समुच्चयेन युक्तश्च सप्तमो भङ्ग उच्यते॥
units.english: "The seventh is required when all three characters are to be employed simultaneously."

units.sanskrit: स्याच्छब्दः खल्वयं निपातस्तिङन्तप्रतिरूपकोऽनेकान्तद्योतकः। यथोक्तम् - वाक्येष्वनेकान्तद्योती गम्यं प्रति विशेषणम्।
units.english: Syāt, "may be," is here an indeclinable particle in the form of a part of a verb, used to convey the idea of indeterminateness; as it has been said—

units.sanskrit: यदि पुनरेकान्तद्योतकः स्याच्छब्दोयं स्यात्तदा स्यादस्तीति वाक्ये स्यात्पदमनर्थकं स्यात्। अनेकान्तद्योतकत्वे तु स्यादस्ति कथं चिदस्तीति स्यात्पदात्कथंचिदित्ययमर्थों लभ्यत इति नानर्थक्यम्।
units.english: If, again, the word syāt denoted determinateness, then it would be needless in the phrase, "may be, it is;" but since it really denotes indeterminateness, "may be, it is," means "it is somehow;" syāt, "may be," conveys the meaning of "somehow," kathaṃcit; and so it is not really useless.

units.sanskrit: तदाह - स्याद्वादः सर्वथैकान्तत्यागात्किं वृत्तचिद्विधेः। सप्तभङ्गिनयापेक्षो हेयादेयविशेषकृत॥इति॥
units.english: "The doctrine of the syād-vāda arises from our everywhere rejecting the idea of the absolute;[56] it depends on the sapta-bhaṅgī-naya, and it lays down the distinction between what is to be avoided and to be accepted."

units.sanskrit: यदि वस्त्वस्त्येकान्ततः सर्वथा सर्वदा सर्वत्र सर्वात्मनास्तीति नोपादित्साजिहासाभ्यां क्वचित्कदाचित्के नचित्प्रवर्तेत निवर्तेत वा। प्राप्ताप्रापणीयत्वादहेयहानानुपपत्तेश्च।
units.english: If a thing absolutely exists, it exists altogether, always, everywhere, and with everybody, and no one at any time or place would ever make an effort to obtain or avoid it, as it would be absurd to treat what is already present as an object to be obtained or avoided.

units.sanskrit: अनेकान्तपक्षे तु कथंचित्कचित्के नचित्सत्त्वेन हानोपादाने प्रेक्षावतामुपपद्येते।
units.english: But if it be relative (or indefinite), the wise will concede that at certain times and in certain places any one may seek or avoid it.

units.sanskrit: किं च वस्तुनः। सत्त्वं स्वभावः, असत्त्वं वेत्यादि प्रष्टव्यम्। न तावदस्तित्वं वस्तुनः स्वभाव इति समस्ति। घटोस्तीत्यनयोः पर्यायतया युगपत्प्रयोगायोगात्। नास्तीति प्रयोगविरोधाच्च।
units.english: Moreover, suppose that the question to be asked is this: "Is being or non-being the real nature of the thing?" The real nature of the thing cannot be being, for then you could not properly use the phrase, "It is a pot" (ghaṭósti), as the two words "is" and "pot" would be tautological; nor ought you to say, "It is not a pot," as the words thus used would imply a direct contradiction; and the same argument is to be used in other questions.[57] As it has been declared—

units.sanskrit: यथोक्तम् - घटोस्तीति न वक्तव्यं सन्नेव हि यतो घटः।
units.english: "It must not be said 'It is a pot,' since the word 'pot' implies 'is;'

units.sanskrit: नास्तीत्यपि न वक्तव्यं विरोधात्सदसत्त्वयोः॥ इत्यादि॥
units.english: "Nor may you say 'it is not a pot,' for existence and non-existence are mutually exclusive," &c.

units.sanskrit: तस्मादित्थं वक्तव्यं सदसत्सदसदनिर्वचनीयवादभेदेन प्रतिवादिनश्चतुर्विधाः। पुनरप्यनिर्वचनीयमतेन मिश्रितानि सदसदादिमतानीति त्रिविधाःतान्प्रति किं वस्त्वस्तीत्यादिपर्यनुयोगे कथंचिदस्तीत्यादिप्रतिवचनसंभवेन ते वादिनः सर्वे निर्विण्णाः सन्तस्तूष्णीमासत इति संपूर्णार्थविनिश्चायिनः स्याद्वादमङ्गीकु र्वतस्तत्र तत्र विजय इति सर्वमुपपन्नम्।
units.english: The whole is thus to be summed up. Four classes of our opponents severally hold the doctrine of existence, non-existence, existence and non-existence successively, and the doctrine that everything is inexplicable (anirvacanīyatā);[58] three other classes hold one or other of the three first theories combined with the fourth.[59] Now, when they meet us with the scornful questions, "Does the thing exist?" &c., we have an answer always possible, "It exists in a certain way," &c., and our opponents are all abashed to silence, and victory accrues to the holder of the Syād-vāda, which ascertains the entire meaning of all things.

units.sanskrit: यदबोचदाचार्यः स्याद्वादमञ्जर्याम् अनेकान्तात्मकं वस्तु गोचरः सर्वसंविदाम्। एकदेशाविशिष्टोर्थों नयस्य विषयो मतः। न्यायानामेकनिष्ठानां प्रवृत्तौ श्रुतवर्त्मनि। संपूर्णार्थविनिश्चायि स्याद्वस्तु श्रुतमुच्यते॥इति॥
units.english: "A thing of an entirely indeterminate nature is the object only of the omniscient; a thing partly determined is held to be the true object of scientific investigation.[60] When our reasonings based on one point proceed in the revealed way, it is called the revealed Syād-vāda, which ascertains the entire meaning of all things."

units.sanskrit: अन्योन्यपक्षप्रतिपक्षभावाद्यथापरे मत्सरिणः प्रवादाः। नयानशेषानविशेषमिच्छन् न पक्षपाती समयस्तथार्हतः॥
units.english: "All other systems are full of jealousy from their mutual propositions and counter-propositions; it is only the doctrine of the Arhat which with no partiality equally favours all sects."

units.sanskrit: अन्तरायस्तथा निद्रा भीरज्ञानं जुगुप्सितम्॥
units.english: The Jaina doctrine has thus been summed up by Jinadatta-sūri—

units.sanskrit: हिंसा रत्यरती रागद्वेषावविरतिः स्मरः। शोको मिथ्यात्वमेतेष्टादश दोषा न यस्य सः॥२॥ जिनो देवो गुरुः सम्यक् तत्त्वज्ञानोपदेशकः।
units.english: "The hindrances belonging to vigour, enjoyment, sensual pleasure, giving and receiving,—sleep, fear, ignorance, aversion, laughter, liking, disliking, love, hatred, want of indifference, desire, sorrow, deceit, these are the eighteen 'faults' (doṣa) according to our system.[61] The divine Jina is our Guru, who declares the true knowledge of the tattvas.

units.sanskrit: ज्ञानदर्शनचारित्राण्यपवर्गस्य वर्तनी॥३॥
units.english: The path[62] of emancipation consists of knowledge, intuition, and conduct.

units.sanskrit: स्याद्वादस्य प्रमाणे द्वे प्रत्यक्षमनुमापि च।
units.english: There are two means of proof (pramāṇa) in the Syād-vāda doctrine,—sense-perception and inference.

units.sanskrit: नित्यानित्यात्मकं सर्वं नव तत्त्वानि सप्त वा॥४॥
units.english: All consists of the eternal and the non-eternal; there are nine or seven tattvas.

units.sanskrit: जीवाजीवौ पुण्यपापे चास्रवः संवरोपि च। बन्धो निर्जरणं मुक्तिरेषां व्याख्याधुनोच्यते॥५॥
units.english: The jīva, the ajīva, merit and demerit, āsrava, saṃvara, bandha, nirjarā, mukti,—we will now explain each.

units.sanskrit: चेतनालक्षणो जीवः स्यादजीवस्तदन्यकः। सत्कर्मपुद्गलाः पुण्यं पापं तस्य विपर्ययः॥६॥ आस्रवः स्त्रोतसो द्वारं संवृणोतीति संवरः। प्रवेशः कर्मणां बन्धो निर्जरस्तद्वियोजनम्॥ अष्टकर्मक्षयान्मोक्षोथान्तर्भावश्च कै श्चन।
units.english: Jīva is defined as intelligence; ajīva is all other than it; merit means bodies which arise from good actions, demerit the opposite; āsrava is the bondage of actions,[63] nirjarā is the unloosing thereof; mokṣa arises from the destruction of the eight forms of karman or "action".

units.sanskrit: पुण्यस्य संवरे पापस्यास्रवे क्रियते पुनः॥८॥
units.english: But by some teachers "merit" is included in saṃvara,[64] and "demerit" in āsrava.

units.sanskrit: लब्धानन्तचतुष्कस्य लोकागूढस्य चात्मनः। क्षीणाष्टकर्मणो मुक्तिǔâर्नव्यावृत्तिर्जिनोदिता॥९॥
units.english: "Of the soul which has attained the four infinite things[65] and is hidden from the world, and whose eight actions are abolished, absolute liberation is declared by Jina.

units.sanskrit: सरजोहरणा भैक्षभुजो लुञ्चितमूर्धजाः। श्वेताम्बराः क्षमाशीला निःसङ्गा जैनसाधवः॥१०॥
units.english: The Śvetāmbaras are the destroyers of all defilement, they live by alms,[66] they pluck out their hair, they practise patience, they avoid all association, and are called the Jaina Sādhus.

units.sanskrit: लुञ्चिताः पिच्छिकाहस्ताः पाणिपात्रा दिगम्बराः। ऊर्ध्वाशिनो गृहे दातुर्द्वितीयाः स्युर्जिनर्षयः॥११॥
units.english: The Digambaras pluck out their hair, they carry peacocks' tails in their hands, they drink from their hands, and they eat upright in the giver's house,—these are the second class of the Jaina Ṛṣis.

units.sanskrit: भुङ्क्ते न के वली न स्त्री मोक्षमेति दिगम्बरः। प्राहुरेषामयं भेदो महाञ्श्वेताम्बरैः सह॥१२॥इति॥
units.english: "A woman attains not the highest knowledge, she enters not Mukti,—so say the Digambaras; but there is a great division on this point between them and the Śvetāmbaras."[67]

units.sanskrit: तदेतदार्हतमतं प्रामाणिकगर्हणमर्हति। न ह्येकस्मिन्वस्तुनि परमार्थे सति परमार्थसतां युगपत्सदसत्त्वादिधर्माणां समावेशः संभवति।
units.english: This doctrine of the Ārhatas deserves a rational condemnation, for whereas there is only one thing really existent, the simultaneous co-existence of existence, non-existence and other modes in a plurality of really existing things is an impossibility.

units.sanskrit: न च सदसत्त्वयोः परस्परविरुद्धयोः समुच्चयासंभवे विकल्पः किं न स्यादिति वदितव्यम्। क्रिया हि विकल्प्यते न वस्त्विति न्यायात्।
units.english: Nor should any one say: Granting the impossibility of the co-existence of existence and non-existence, which are reciprocally contradictory, why should there not be an alternation between existence and non-existence? there being the rule that it is action, not Ens, that alternates.

units.sanskrit: न च एनकान्तं जगत्सर्वं हेरम्बनरसिंहवत्। इति दृष्टान्तावष्टम्भवशादेष्टव्यम्। एकस्मिन्देशे गजत्वं सिंहत्वं वा'परस्मिन्नरत्वमिति देशभेदेन विरोधाभावेन तस्यैकस्मिन्देश एव सत्त्वासत्त्वादिनानेकान्तत्वाभिधाने दृष्टान्तानुपपत्तेः।
units.english: Nor let it be supposed that the whole universe is multiform, in reliance upon the examples of the elephant-headed Gaṇeśa and of the incarnation of Viṣṇu as half man, half lion; for the elephantine and the leonine nature existing in one part, and the human in another, and consequently there being no contradiction, those parts being different, these examples are inapplicable to the maintenance of a nature multiform as both existent and non-existent in one and the same part (or place).

units.sanskrit: ननु द्रव्यात्मना सत्वं पर्यायात्मना तदभाव इत्युभयमप्युपपन्नमिति चैन्मैवम्। कालभेदेन हि कस्याचित्सत्त्वमसत्त्वं च स्वभाव इति न कश्चिद्दोषः।
units.english: Again, if any one urge: Let there be existence in one form, and non-existence in another, and thus both will be compatible; we rejoin: Not so, for if you had said that at different times existence and non-existence may be the nature of anything, then indeed there would have been no vice in your procedure.

units.sanskrit: न चैकस्य ह्रस्वत्वदीर्घत्ववदनेकान्तत्वं जगतः स्यादिति वाच्यम्। प्रतियोगिभेदेन विरोधाभावात्।
units.english: Nor is it to be contended: Let the multiformity of the universe be like the length and shortness which pertain to the same thing (in different relations); for in these (in this length and shortness) there is no contrariety, inasmuch as they are contrasted with different objects.

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्प्रमाणाभावाद्युगपंत्सत्त्वासत्त्वे परस्परविरुद्धे नैकस्मिन्वस्तुनि वस्तुं युक्ते ।
units.english: Therefore, for want of evidence, existence and non-existence as reciprocally contradictory cannot reside at the same time in the same thing.

units.sanskrit: एवमन्यासामपिभङ्गीनां भङ्गोवगन्तव्यः।
units.english: In a like manner may be understood the refutation of the other bhaṅgas (Ārhata tenets).

units.sanskrit: किं च सर्वस्यास्य मूलभूतः सप्तभङ्गिनयः स्वयमेकोन्तोनेकान्तो वा। आद्ये सर्वमनेकान्तमिति प्रतिज्ञाव्याघातः।
units.english: Again, we ask, is this doctrine of the seven bhaṅgas, which lies at the base of all this, itself uniform (as excluding one contradictory), or multiform (as conciliating contradictories).

units.sanskrit: द्वितीये विवक्षितार्थासिद्धिः। अनेकान्तत्वेनासाधकत्वात्। तथा चेयमुभयतःपाशा रज्जुः स्याद्वादिनः स्यात्।
units.english: If it is uniform, there will emerge a contradiction to your thesis that all things are multiform; if it is multiform, you have not proved what you wished to prove, a multiform statement (as both existent and non-existent) proving nothing.[1] In either case, there is rope for a noose for the neck of the Syād-Vādin.

units.sanskrit: अपि च नवत्वसप्तत्वादिनिर्धारणस्य फलस्य तन्निर्धारयितुः प्रमातुश्च तत्करणस्य प्रमाणस्य प्रमेयस्य च नवत्वादेरनियमे साधु समर्थितमात्मनस्तीर्थकरत्वं देवानांप्रियेणार्हतमतप्रवर्तके न।
units.english: An admirable author of institutes has the founder of the Ārhata system, dear to the gods (uninquiring pietist), proved himself to be, when he has not ascertained whether his result is the settling of nine or of seven principles, nor the investigator who settles them, nor his organon, the modes of evidence, nor the matter to be evidenced, whether it be ninefold or not!

units.sanskrit: तथा जीवस्य देहानुरूपपरिमाणत्वाङ्गीकारे योगबलादनेकदेहपरिग्राहकयोगिशरीरेषु प्रतिशरीरं जीवविच्छेदः प्रसज्येत।
units.english: In like manner if it be admitted that the soul has (as the Ārhatas say), an extension equal to that of the body, it will follow that in the case of the souls of ascetics, who by the efficacy of asceticism assume a plurality of bodies, there is a differentiation of the soul for each of those bodies.

units.sanskrit: मनुजशरीरपरिमाणो जीवो मतङ्गजदेहं कृत्स्नं प्रवेष्टुं न प्रभवेत्। किं च गजादिशरीरं परित्यज्य पिपीलिकाशरीरं विशतः प्राचीनशरीरसंनिवेशविनाशोपि प्राप्नुयात्।
units.english: A soul of the size of a human body would not (in the course of its transmigrations) be able to occupy the whole body of an elephant; and again, when it laid aside its elephantine body to enter into that of an ant, it would lose its capacity of filling its former frame.

units.sanskrit: न च यथा प्रदीपप्रभाविशेषः प्रपाप्रासादाद्युदरवर्तिसंकोचविकाशवांस्तथाजीवोपि मनुजमतङ्गजादिशरीरेषु स्यादित्येषितव्यम्। प्रदीपवदेव सविकारत्वेनानित्यत्वप्राप्तौ कृतप्रणाशाकृताभ्यागमप्रसङ्गात्। एवं प्रधानमल्लनिवर्हणन्यायेन जीवपदार्थद्रूषणाभिधानदिशान्यत्रापि दूषणमुत्प्रेक्षणीयम्।
units.english: And it cannot be supposed that the soul resides successively in the human, elephantine, and other bodies, like the light of a lamp which is capable of contraction and expansion, according as it occupies the interior of a little station on the road-side in which travellers are supplied with water, or the interior of a stately mansion; for it would follow (from such a supposition) that the soul being susceptible of modifications and consequently non-eternal, there would be a loss of merits and a fruition of good and evil unmerited.

units.sanskrit: तस्मान्नित्यनिर्दोंषश्रुतिविरुद्धत्वादिदमुपादेयं न भवति।
units.english: Their doctrine, therefore, as repugnant to the eternal, infallible revelation, cannot be adopted.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं भगवता व्यासेननैकस्मिन्नसंभवात् (ब्र.सू.२/२/३१) इति। रामानुजेन च जैनमतनिराकरणपरत्वेन तदिदं सूत्रं व्याकारि।
units.english: The venerated Vyāsa accordingly propounded the aphorism (ii. 2, 33), "Nay, because it is impossible in one;" and this same aphorism has been analysed by Rāmānuja with the express purpose of shutting out the doctrine of the Jainas.

units.sanskrit: एष हि तस्य सिद्धान्तः चिदचिदीश्वरभेदेन भोक्तृभोग्यनियामकभेदेन च व्यवस्थितास्त्रयः पदार्था इति।
units.english: The tenets of Rāmānuja are as follows:—Three categories are established, as soul, not-soul, and Lord; or as subject, object, and supreme disposer.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तम् - ईश्वरश्चिदचिश्चेति पदार्थत्रितयं हरिः।
units.english: Thus it has been said— "Lord, soul, and not-soul are the triad of principles: Hari (Viṣṇu)

units.sanskrit: ईश्वरश्चिदिति प्रोक्तो जीवो दृश्यमचित्पुनः।इति।
units.english: "Is Lord; individual spirits are souls; and the visible world is not-soul."

units.sanskrit: अपरे पुनरशेषविशेषप्रत्यनीकं चिन्मात्रं ब्रह्मैव परमार्थः। तच्च नित्यशुद्धबुद्धमुक्तस्वभावमपि तत्त्वमसि (छा.६/८/७) इत्यादिसामानाधिकरण्याधिगतजीवैक्यं बध्यते मुच्यते च।
units.english: Others, again (the followers of Śaṅkarācārya), maintain that pure intelligence, exempt from all differences, the absolute, alone is really existent; and that this absolute whose essence is eternal, pure, intelligent, and free, the identity of which with the individuated spirit is learnt from the "reference to the same object" (predication), "That art thou," undergoes bondage and emancipation.

units.sanskrit: तदतिरिक्तनानाविधभोक्तृभोक्तव्यादिभेदप्रपञ्चः सर्वोंपि तस्मिन्नविद्यया परिकल्पितः सदेव सोम्येदमग्र आसीदेकमेवाद्वितीयम् ( छा.६/२/१) इत्यादि वचननिचयप्रामाण्यादिति ब्रुवणा तरति शोकमात्मवित् ( छ.७/१/३) इत्यादिश्रुतिशिरः शतवशेन निर्विशेषब्रह्मात्मैकत्वविद्ययानाद्यविद्यानिवृत्तिमङ्गीकु र्वाणाः। मृत्योः स मृत्युमाप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति (का.२.१) इति भेदनिन्दाश्रवणेन पारमार्थिकं भेदं निराचक्षाणां विचक्षणंमन्यास्तमिमं विभागं न सहन्ते।
units.english: Maintaining this, and acknowledging a suppression of this beginningless illusion by knowledge of the unity (and identity) of individuated spirits and the undifferenced absolute, in conformity with hundreds of texts from the Upaniṣads, such as He that knows spirit passes beyond sorrow; rejecting also any real plurality of things, in conformity with the text condemnatory of duality, viz., Death after death he undergoes who looks upon this as manifold; and thinking themselves very wise, the Śāṅkaras will not tolerate this division (viz., the distribution of things into soul, not-soul, and Lord).

units.sanskrit: तत्रायं समाधिरभिधीयते। भवेदेतदेवं यद्यविद्यायां प्रमाणं विद्येत।
units.english: To all this the following counterposition is laid down:—This might be all well enough if there were any proof of such illusion.

units.sanskrit: नन्विदमनादि भावरूपं ज्ञाननिवर्त्यमज्ञानमहमज्ञो मानन्यं च न जानामीति प्रत्यक्षप्रमाणसिद्धम्।
units.english: But there is no such ignorance (or illusion), an unbeginning entity, suppressible by knowledge, testified in the perceptions, I am ignorant, I know not myself and other things.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तम् - अनादि भावरूपं यद्विज्ञानेन विलीयते।
units.english: Thus it has been said (to explain the views of the Śāṅkara)—

units.sanskrit: तदज्ञानमिति प्राज्ञा लक्षणं संप्रचक्षते॥
units.english: "Entitative from everlasting, which is dissolved by knowledge,
"Such is illusion.

units.sanskrit: न चैतज्ज्ञानाभावविषयमित्याशङ्कनीयम्।
units.english: This perception (they would further contend) is not conversant about the absence of knowledge.

units.sanskrit: को ह्येवं ब्रूयात्प्रभाकरकरावलम्बी भट्टदत्तहस्तो वा।
units.english: For who can maintain this, and to whom? One who leans on the arm of Prabhākara, or one to whom Kumārila-bhaṭṭa gives his hand? Not the former, for in the words—

units.sanskrit: नाद्यः - स्वरूपपररूपाभ्यां नित्यं सदसदात्मके ।
units.english: "By means of its own and of another's form, eternal in the existent and non-existent,

units.sanskrit: वस्तुनि ज्ञायते किं चित्कैश्चिद्रूपं कदाचन।
units.english: "Thing is recognised something by some at certain times.

units.sanskrit: भावान्तरादभावोन्यो न कश्चिदनिरूपणात्। इति वदता भावव्यतिरिक्तस्याभावस्यानभ्युपगमात्।
units.english: "Non-entity is but another entity by some kind of relation. Non-entity is but another entity, naught else, for naught else is observed."

units.sanskrit: न द्वितीयः।
units.english: They deny any non-entity ulterior to entity.

units.sanskrit: अभावस्य षष्ठप्रमाणगोचरत्वेन ज्ञानस्य नित्यानुमेयत्वेन च तदभावस्य प्रत्यक्षविषयत्वानुपपत्तेः।
units.english: Non-entity being cognisable by the sixth instrument of knowledge (anupalabdhi), and knowledge being always an object of inference, the absence of knowledge cannot be an object of perception.

units.sanskrit: यदि पुनः प्रत्यक्षाभाववादी कश्चिदेवमाचक्षीत तं प्रत्याचक्षीत। अहमज्ञ इत्यस्मिन्ननुभवेहमित्यात्मनोऽभावधर्मितया ज्ञानस्य प्रतियोगितया चावगतिरस्ति न वा।
units.english: If, again, any one who maintains non-entity to be perceptible should employ the above argument (from the perceptions, I am ignorant, I know not myself, and other things); it may be replied: "Is there, or is there not, in the consciousness, I am ignorant, an apprehension of self as characterised by an absence, and of knowledge as the thing absent or non-existent? If there is such apprehension, consciousness of the absence of knowledge will be impossible, as involving a contradiction.

units.sanskrit: अस्ति चेद्विरोधादेव न ज्ञानाभावानुभवः। न चेद्धर्मिप्रतियोगिज्ञानसापेक्षो ज्ञानाभावानुभवः सुतरां न संभवति। तस्याज्ञानस्य भावरूपत्वे प्रागुक्तदषणाभावादूयमनुभवो भावरूपाज्ञानगोचर एवाभ्युपगन्तव्य इति। तदेतद्गगनरोमन्थायितम्। भावरूपस्याज्ञानस्य ज्ञानाभावेन समानयोगक्षेमत्वात्। तथा हिविषयत्वेनाश्रयत्वेन चाज्ञानस्य व्यावर्तकतया प्रत्यगर्थः प्रतिपन्नो न वा। प्रतिपन्नश्चेत्स्वरूपज्ञाननिवर्त्यं तदज्ञानमिति तस्मिन्प्रतिपन्ने कथंकारमवतिष्ठते। अप्रतिपन्नश्चेद्वयावर्त्तकाश्रयविषयशून्यमज्ञानं कथमनुभूयेत। अथ विशदः स्वरूपावभास एवाज्ञानविरोधी नाज्ञानेन सह भासत इत्याश्रयविषयज्ञाने सत्यपि नाज्ञानानुभवविरोध इति हन्त तर्हि ज्ञानाभावेपि समानमेतदन्यत्राभिनिवेशात्।
units.english: If there is not, consciousness of the absence of knowledge, which consciousness presupposes a knowledge of the subject and of the thing absent, will not readily become possible." Inasmuch (the Śāṅkaras continue) as the foregoing difficulties do not occur if ignorance (or illusion) be entitative, this consciousness (I am ignorant, I know not myself, and other things) must be admitted to be conversant about an entitative ignorance. All this (the Rāmānuja replies) is about as profitable as it would be for a ruminant animal to ruminate upon ether; for an entitative ignorance is not more supposable than an absence of knowledge. For (we would ask), is any self-conscious principle presented as an object and as a subject (of ignorance) as distinct from cognition? If it is presented, how, since ignorance of a thing is terminable by knowledge of its essence, can the ignorance continue? If none such is presented, how can we be conscious of an ignorance which has no subject and no object? If you say: A pure manifestation of the spiritual essence is revealed only by the cognition opposed to ignorance (or illusion), and thus there is no absurdity in the consciousness of ignorance accompanied with a consciousness of its subject and object; then we rejoin:—Unfortunately for you, this (consciousness of subject) must arise equally in the absence of knowledge (for such we define illusion to be), notwithstanding your assertion to the contrary.

units.sanskrit: तस्मादुभयाभ्युपगतज्ञानाभाव एवाहमज्ञो मानन्यं च न जानामीत्यनुभवगोचर इत्यभ्युपगन्तव्यम्।
units.english: It must, therefore, be acknowledged that the cognition, I am ignorant, I know not myself and other things, is conversant about an absence of cognition allowed by us both.

units.sanskrit: अस्तु तर्ह्यनुमानं मानंविवादास्पदं प्रमाणज्ञानं स्वप्रागभावव्यतिरिक्तस्वविषयावरणस्वनिवर्त्यस्वदेशगतवस्त्वन्तरपूर्वकप्रकाशितार्थप्रकाशकत्वादन्धकारे प्रथमोत्पन्नप्रदीपप्रभावदिति।
units.english: illusion), an entity different from mere prior non-existence of knowledge, which envelops the objects of knowledge, which is terminable by knowledge, which occupies the place of knowledge, inasmuch as it (the right knowledge) illuminates an object not before illuminated, like the light of a lamp springing up for the first time in the darkness.

units.sanskrit: तदपि न क्षोदक्षमम्।
units.english: We dismiss further prolixity.

units.sanskrit: न हि प्रदीपप्रभाया अप्रकाशितार्थप्रकाशकत्वं संभवति। ज्ञानस्यैव प्रकाशकत्वात्। सत्यपि प्रदीपे ज्ञानेन विषयप्रकाशसंभवात्।
units.english: The counterposition (of the Rāmānujas) is as follows:—The illusion under dispute does not reside in Brahman, who is pure knowledge, because it is an illusion, like the illusion about nacre, &c.

units.sanskrit: प्रतिप्रयोगश्च विवादाध्यासितमज्ञानं न ज्ञानमात्रब्रह्माश्रितम् अज्ञानत्वाच्छु क्तिकाद्यज्ञानवदिति। ननु शुक्तिकाद्यज्ञानस्याश्रयस्य प्रत्यगर्थस्य ज्ञानमात्रस्वभावत्वमेवेति चेन्मैवं शङ्किष्ठाः। अनुभूतिर्हि स्वसद्भावेनैव कस्यचिद्वस्तुनो व्यवहारानुगुणत्वापादनस्वभावो ज्ञानावगतिसंविदाद्यपरनामा सकर्मकोनुभवितुरात्मनो धर्माविशेषः।
