units.english: If any one ask: Has not the self-conscious entity that underlies the illusion about nacre, &c., knowledge only for its nature? they reply: Do not start such difficulties; for we suppose that consciousness by its bare existence has the nature of creating conformity to the usage about (i.e., the name and notion of) some object; and such consciousness, also called knowledge, apprehension, comprehension, intelligence, &c., constitutes the soul, or knowledge, of that which acts and knows.

units.sanskrit: ननु ज्ञानरूपस्यात्मनः कथं ज्ञानगुणकत्वमिति चेत्तदसारम।यथा हि मणिद्युमणिप्रभृति तेजोद्रव्यं प्रभावद्रूपेणवतिष्ठमानं प्रभारूपगुणाश्रयः। स्वाश्रयादन्यत्रापि वर्तमानत्वेन रूपवत्त्वेन च प्रभा द्रव्यरूपापि तच्छेषत्वनिबन्धनगुणव्यवहारा। एवमयमात्मा स्वप्रकाशचिद्रूप एव चैतन्यगुणः। तथा च श्रुतिःस यथा सैन्धवघनोनन्तरोऽबाह्यः कृत्स्नाः प्रज्ञानधन एव।
units.english: If any one ask: How can the soul, if it consists of cognition, have cognition as a quality? they reply: This question is futile; for as a gem, the sun, and other luminous things, existing in the form of light, are substances in which light as a quality inheres—for light, as existing elsewhere than in its usual receptacle, and as being a mode of things though a substance, is still styled and accounted a quality derived from determination by that substance,—so this soul, while it exists as a self-luminous intelligence, has also intelligence as its quality.

units.sanskrit: अत्रायं पुरुषः स्वयंज्योतिर्भवति (बृ.४/३/९)। न हि विज्ञातुर्विज्ञातेर्विपरिलोपो विद्यते (बृ.४/३/३०) अथ यो वेदेदं जिघ्राणीति स आत्मा (छा.८/१२/४) योयं विज्ञानमयः प्राणेषु हृद्यन्तर्ज्योंतिः पुरुषः (बृ.४/३/७)। एष हि द्रष्टा स्प्रष्टा श्रोता घ्राता रसयिता मन्ता बोद्धा कर्ता विज्ञानात्मा पुरुषः (प्र.४/९) इत्यादिका।
units.english: Accordingly the Vedic texts: A lump of salt is always within and without one entire mass of taste, so also this soul is within and without an entire mass of knowledge; Herein this person is itself a light; Of the knowledge of that which knows there is no suspension; He who knows, smells this; and so also, This is the soul which, consisting of knowledge, is the light within the heart; For this person is the seer, the hearer, the taster, the smeller, the thinker, the understander, the doer; The person is knowledge, and the like texts.

units.sanskrit: न च अनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः (छा.८/३/२) इति श्रुतिरविद्यायां प्रमाणमित्याश्रयितुं शक्यम्। ऋतेतरविषयो ह्यनृतशब्दः।
units.english: It is not to be supposed that the Veda also affords evidence of the existence of the cosmical illusion, in the text, Enveloped in untruth (anṛta); for the word untruth (anṛta) denotes that which is other than truth (ṛta).

units.sanskrit: ऋतं पिबन्तौ (का.३/१) इति वचनात्।
units.english: The word ṛta has a passive sense, as appears from the words, Drinking ṛta.

units.sanskrit: ऋतं तद्वयतिरिक्तं सांसारिकाल्पफलं कर्मानृतं ब्रह्मप्राप्तिविरोधि।
units.english: Ṛta means works done without desire of fruit; having as its reward the attainment of the bliss of the Supreme Spirit through his propitiation.

units.sanskrit: य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्ति अनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः (छा.८/३/२) इति वचनात्।
units.english: In the text in question, untruth (anṛta) designates the scanty fruit enjoyed during transmigratory existence as opposed to that (which results from propitiation of the Supreme Spirit), which temporal fruit is obstructive to the attainment of supreme existence (brahman); the entire text (when the context is supplied) being: They who find not this supreme sphere (brahma-loka) are enveloped in untruth.

units.sanskrit: मायां तु प्रकृतिं विद्यात् ( श्वे.४/१०) इत्यादौ माया शब्दो विचित्रार्थसर्गकरत्रिगुणात्मकप्रकृत्यभिधायको नानिर्वचनीयाज्ञानवचनः।
units.english: In such texts, again, as Let him know illusion (māyā) to be the primary emanative cause (prakṛti), the term (māyā) designates the emanative cause, consisting of the three "cords" (guṇa), and creative of the diversified universe.

units.sanskrit: तेन मायासहस्रं तच्छम्बरस्याशुगामिना। बालस्य रक्षता देहमेकै कांशेन सूदितम्॥ (वि.पु.१/१९/२०) इत्यादौ विचित्रार्थसर्गसमर्थस्य पारमार्थिकसैवासुराद्यस्त्रविशेषस्यैव मायाशब्दाभिधेयत्वोपलम्भात्।
units.english: In such passages as, By him the defender of the body of the child, moving rapidly, the thousand illusions (māyā) of the barbarian were swooped upon as by a hawk, we observe that the word "illusion" (māyā) designates the really existent weapon of a Titan, capable of projective diversified creation.

units.sanskrit: अतो न कदाचिदपि श्रुत्या अनर्वचनीयाज्ञानप्रतिपादनम्।
units.english: The Veda, then, never sets out an inexplicable illusion.

units.sanskrit: नाप्यैक्योपदेशान्यथानुपपत्त्या। तत्त्वंपदयोः सविशेषब्रह्माभिधेयत्वेन विरुद्धयोर्जीवपरयोः स्वरूपैक्यस्य प्रतिपत्तुमशक्यतयार्थापत्तेरनुदयदोषदूषितत्वात्।
units.english: Nor (is the cosmical illusion to be inferred from the "grand text," That art thou), inasmuch as the words, That art thou, being incompetent to teach unity, and indicating a conditionate Supreme Spirit, we cannot understand by them the essential unity of the mutually exclusive supreme and individual spirits; for such a supposition (as that they are identical) would violate the law of excluded middle.

units.sanskrit: तथा हितत्पदं निरस्तसमस्तदोषमनवधिकातिशयासंख्येयकल्याणगुणास्पदं जगदुदयविभवलयलीलं ब्रह्म प्रतिपादयति। तदैक्षत बहु स्यां प्रजायेय (छा.६/२/३) इत्यादिषु तस्यैव प्रकृतत्वात्।
units.english: The term That denotes the Supreme Spirit exempt from all imperfections, of illimitable excellence, a repository of innumerable auspicious attributes, to whom the emanation, sustentation, retractation of the universe is a pastime;[2] such being the Supreme Spirit, spoken of in such texts as, That desired, let me be many, let me bring forth.

units.sanskrit: तत्समानाधिकरणं त्वंपदं चाचिद्विशिष्टजीवशरीरकं ब्रह्माचष्टे। प्रकारद्वयविशिष्टैकवस्तुपरत्वात्सामानाधिकरण्यस्य।
units.english: Perhaps the word Thou, referring to the same object (as the word That), denotes the Supreme Spirit characterised by consciousness, having all individual spirits as his body; for a "reference to the same object" designates one thing determined by two modes.

units.sanskrit: ननु सोयं देवदत्त इतिवत्तत्त्वमिति पदयोर्विरुद्धभागत्यागलक्षणया निर्विशेषस्वरूपमात्मैक्यं सामानाधिकरण्यार्थः किं न स्यात्। यथा सोयमित्यत्र तच्छब्देन देशान्तरकालान्तरसंबन्धी पुरुषः प्रतीयते। इदंशब्देन च संनिहितदेशवर्तमानकालसंबन्धी।
units.english: Here, perhaps, an Advaita-vādin may reply: Why may not the purport of the reference to the same object in the words, That art thou, be undifferenced essence, the unity of souls, these words (That and thou) having a (reciprocally) implicate power by abandonment of opposite portions of their meaning; as is the case in the phrase, This is that Devadatta. In the words, This is that Devadatta, we understand by the word That, a person in relation to a different time and place, and by the word This, a person in relation to the present time and place.

units.sanskrit: तयोः सामानाधिकरण्येनैक्यमवगम्यते।
units.english: That both are one and the same is understood by the form of predication ("reference to the same object").

units.sanskrit: तत्रैकस्य युगपद्विरुद्धदेशकालप्रतीतिर्न संभवतीति द्वयोरपि पदयोः स्वरूपपरत्वे स्वरूपस्य चैक्यं प्रतिपत्तुं शक्यम्।
units.english: Now as one and the same thing cannot at the same time be known as in different times and places, the two words (This and That) must refer to the essence (and not to the accidents of time and place), and unity of essence can be understood.

units.sanskrit: एवमत्रापि किं चिञ्जत्वसर्वज्ञत्वादिविरुद्धांशप्रहाणेनाखण्डस्वरूपंलक्ष्यत इति चेत् - विषमोयमुपन्यासः।
units.english: Similarly in the text, That art thou, there is implicated an indivisible essence by abandonment of the contradictory portions (of the denotation), viz., finite cognition (which belongs to the individual soul or Thou), and infinite cognition (which belongs to the real or unindividual soul).

units.sanskrit: दृष्टान्तेपि विरोधवैधुर्येण लक्षणागन्धासंभवात्। एकस्य तावद् भूतवर्तमानकालद्वयसंबंन्धो न विरुद्धः। देशान्तरस्थितिर्भूता संनिहितदेशस्थितिर्वर्तत इति देशभेदसंबन्धविरोधश्च कालभेदेन परिहरणीयः। लक्षणापाक्षेप्येकस्यैव पदस्य लक्षणत्वाश्रयणेन विरोधपरिहारे पदद्वयस्य लाक्षणिकत्वस्वीकारो न संगच्छते। इतरथैकस्य वस्तुनस्तत्तेदंताविशिष्टत्वावगाहनेन प्रत्यभिज्ञायाः प्रामाण्यानङ्गीकारे स्थायित्वासिद्धौ क्षणभङ्गवादी बौद्धो विजयेत।
units.english: This suggestion (the Rāmānujas reply) is unsatisfactory, for there is no opposition (between This and That) in the example (This is that Devadatta), and consequently not the smallest particle of "implication" (lakṣaṇā, both This and That being used in their denotative capacity). The connection of one object with two times past and present involves no contradiction. And any contradiction supposed to arise from relation to different places may be avoided by a supposed difference of time, the existence in the distant place being past, and the existence in the near being present. Even if we concede to you the "implication," the (supposed) contradiction being avoidable by supposing one term (either That or Thou) to be implicative, it is unnecessary to admit that both words are implicative. Otherwise (if we admit that both words are implicative), if it be granted that the one thing may be recognised, with the concomitant assurance that it differs as this and as that, permanence in things will be inadmissible, and the Buddhist assertor of a momentary flux of things will be triumphant.

units.sanskrit: एवमत्रापि जीवपरमात्मनोः शरीरात्मभावेन तादात्म्यं न विरुद्धमिति प्रतिपादितम्।
units.english: We have, therefore (the Rāmānujas continue), laid it down in this question that there is no contradiction in the identity of the individual and the Supreme Spirit, the individual spirits being the body and the Supreme Spirit the soul.

units.sanskrit: जीवात्मा हि ब्रह्मणः शरीरतया प्रकारत्वाद्रह्यात्मकः। य आत्मनि तिष्ठन्नात्मनोन्तरो यमात्मा न वेद यस्यात्मा शरीरम् ( बृ.भा.३/७/२२) इति श्रुत्यन्तरात्।
units.english: For the individual spirit as the body, and therefore a form, of the Supreme Spirit, is identical with the Supreme Spirit, according to another text, Who abiding in the soul, is the controller of the soul, who knows the soul, of whom soul is the body.

units.sanskrit: अत्यल्पमिदमुच्यते।
units.english: Your statement of the matter, therefore, is too narrow.

units.sanskrit: सर्वे शब्दाः परमात्मन एव बाचकाः।
units.english: All words are designatory of the Supreme Spirit.

units.sanskrit: न च पर्यायत्वम्। द्वारभेदसंभवात्। यथा हि जीवस्य शरीरतया प्रकारभूतानि देवमनुष्यादिसंस्थानानीव सर्वाणि वस्तूनीति ब्रह्मात्मकानि तानि सर्वाणि।
units.english: They are not all synonymous, a variety of media being possible; thus as all organised bodies, divine, human, &c., are forms of individual spirits, so all things (are the body of Supreme Spirit), all things are identical with Supreme Spirit.

units.sanskrit: अतः - देवो मनुष्यो यक्षो वा पिशाचोरगराक्षसाः। पक्षी वृक्षो लता काष्ठं शिला तृणं घटः पटः। इत्यादयः सर्वे शब्दाः प्रकृतिप्रत्यययोगेनाभिधायकतया प्रसिद्धा लोके तद्वाच्चतया प्रतीयमानतत्तत्संस्थानवद्वस्तुमुखेन तदभिमानिजीवतदन्तर्यामिपरमात्मपर्यन्तसंघातस्य वाचकाः।
units.english: Hence— God, Man, Yakṣa, Piśāca, serpent, Rākṣasa, bird, tree, creeper, wood, stone, grass, jar, cloth,—these and all other words, be they what they may, which are current among mankind as denotative by means of their base and its suffixes, as denoting those things, in denoting things of this or that apparent constitution, really denote the individual souls which assumed to them such body, and the whole complexus of things terminating in the Supreme Spirit ruling within.

units.sanskrit: देवादिशब्दानां परमात्मपर्यन्तत्वमुक्तं तत्त्वमुक्तावल्यां चतुर्थसरे - जीवं देवादिशब्दो वदति तदपृथक्सिद्धाभावाभिधानान्निष्कर्षाभावयुक्ताद् बहुरिह च दृढो लोकवेदप्रयोगः।
units.english: That God and all other words whatsoever ultimately denote the Supreme Spirit is stated in the Tattva-muktāvalī and in the Caturantara— "God, and all other words, designate the soul, none else than That, called the established entity, "Of this there is much significant and undoubted exemplification in common speech and in the Veda;

units.sanskrit: आत्मासंबन्धकाले स्थितिरनवगता देवमर्त्यादिमूर्तेर्जीवात्मानुप्रवेशाज्जगति विभुरपि व्याकरोन्नामरूपे॥
units.english: "Existence when dissociated from spirit is unknown; in the form of gods, mortals, and the rest "When pervading the individual spirit, the infinite has made a diversity of names and forms in the world."

units.sanskrit: अनेन देवादिशब्दानां शरीरविशिष्टजीवपर्यन्तत्वं प्रतिपाद्य संस्थानैक्याद्यभावे (तत्त्वमु.४/८३) इत्यादिना शरीरलक्षणं दर्शयित्वा शब्दैस्तन्वंशरूपप्रभृतिभिः (तत्त्वमु. ४/८४) इत्यादिना विश्वस्येश्वरादपृथक्सिद्धत्वमुपपाद्य निष्कर्षाकू त (तत्त्वमु.४/८५) इत्यादिना पद्येन सर्वेषां शब्दानां परमात्मपर्यन्तत्वं प्रतिपादितं तत्सर्वं तत एवावधार्यम्।
units.english: In these words the author, setting forth that all words, God, and the rest, designate the body, and showing in the words, "No unity in systems," &c., the characteristic of body, and showing in the words, "By words which are substitutes for the essence of things," &c., that it is established that nothing is different from the universal Lord, lays down in the verses, Significant of the essence, &c., that all words ultimately designate the Supreme Spirit. All this may be ascertained from that work.

units.sanskrit: अयमेवार्थः समर्थितो वेदार्थसंग्रहे नामरूपश्रुतिव्याकरणसमये रामानुजेन।
units.english: The same matter has been enforced by Rāmānuja in the Vedārtha-saṅgraha, when analysing the Vedic text about names and forms.

units.sanskrit: किं च सर्वप्रमाणस्य सविशेषविषयतया निर्विशेषवस्तुनि न किमपि प्रमाणं समस्ति।
units.english: Moreover, every form of evidence having some determinate object, there can be no evidence of an undetermined (unconditionate) reality.

units.sanskrit: निर्विकल्पप्रत्यक्षेपि सविशेषमेव वस्तु प्रतीयते।
units.english: Even in non-discriminative perception it is a determinate (or conditioned) thing that is cognised.

units.sanskrit: अन्यथा सविकल्पके सोयमिति पूर्वप्रतिपन्नप्रकारविशिष्टप्रतीत्यनुपपत्तेः।
units.english: Else in discriminative perception there could not be shown to be a cognition characterised by an already presented form.

units.sanskrit: किं च तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यं न प्रपञ्चस्य बाधकम्। भ्रान्तिमूलकत्वात् भ्रान्तिप्रयुक्तरज्जुसर्पवाक्यवत्। नापि ब्रह्मात्मैक्यज्ञानं निवर्तकम्।
units.english: Again, that text, That art thou, is not sublative of the universe as rooted in illusion, like a sentence declaratory that what was illusorily presented, as a snake is a piece of rope; nor does knowledge of the unity of the absolute and the soul bring (this illusory universe) to an end; for we have already demonstrated that there is no proof of these positions.

units.sanskrit: न च प्रपञ्चस्य सत्यत्वप्रतिष्ठापनपक्ष एकविज्ञानेन सर्वविज्ञानप्रतिज्ञाव्याकोपः। प्रकृतिपुरुषमहदहंकारतन्मात्रभूतेन्द्रियचतुर्दशभुवनात्मकब्रह्माण्डतदन्तरवर्तिदेवतिर्यङ्गमनुष्यस्थावरादिसर्वप्रकारसंस्थान संस्थितं कार्यमपि सर्वं ब्रह्मैवेति कारणभूतब्रह्मात्मज्ञानादेव सर्वविज्ञानं भवतीत्येकविज्ञानेन सर्वविज्ञानस्योपपन्नतरत्वात्।
units.english: Nor is there an absurdity (as the Śāṅkaras would say), on the hypothesis enunciatory of the reality of the universe, in affirming that by a cognition of one there is a cognition of all things: for it is easily evinced that the mundane egg, consisting of the primary cause (prakṛti), intellect, self-position, the rudimentary elements, the gross elements, the organs (of sense and of action), and the fourteen worlds, and the gods, animals, men, immovable things, and so forth, that exist within it, constituting a complex of all forms, is all an effect, and that from the single cognition of absolute spirit as its (emanative) cause, when we recognise that all this is absolute spirit (there being a tautology between cause and effect), there arises cognition of all things, and thus by cognition of one cognition of all.

units.sanskrit: अपि च ब्रह्मव्यतिरिक्तस्य सर्वस्य मिथ्यात्वे सर्वस्यासत्त्वादेवैकविज्ञानेन सर्वविज्ञानप्रतिज्ञा वाध्येत।
units.english: Besides, if all else than absolute spirit were unreal, then all being non-existent, it would follow that by one cognition all cognition would be sublated.

units.sanskrit: नामरूपविभागानर्हसूक्ष्मदशावत्प्रकृतिपुरुषशरीरं ब्रह्म कारणावस्थम्। जगतस्तदापत्तिरेव प्रलयः। नामरूपविभागविभक्तस्थूलचिदचिद्वस्तुशरीरं ब्रह्म कार्यावस्थम्। ब्रह्मणस्तथाविधस्थूलभावश्च सृष्टिरित्यभिधीयते एवं च कार्य कारणयोरनन्यत्वमप्यारम्भणाधिकरणे प्रतिपादितमुपपन्नतरं भवति।
units.english: It is laid down (by the Rāmānujas) that retractation into the universe (pralaya) is when the universe, the body whereof consists of souls and the originant (prakṛti), returns to its imperceptible state, unsusceptible of division by names and forms, existing as absolute spirit the emanative cause; and that creation (or emanation) is the gross or perceptible condition of absolute spirit, the body whereof is soul and not soul divided by diversity of names and forms, in the condition of the (emanative) effect of absolute spirit.

units.sanskrit: निर्गुणवादाश्चप्राकृतहेयगुणनिषेधविषयतया व्यवस्थिताः।
units.english: The statements that the Supreme Spirit is void of attributes, are intended (it is shown) to deny thereof phenomenal qualities which are to be escaped from by those that desire emancipation.

units.sanskrit: नानात्वनिषेधवादाश्चैकस्यैव ब्रह्मणः शरीरतया प्रकारभूतं सर्वं चेतनाचेतनात्मकं वस्त्विति सर्वस्यात्मतया सर्वप्रकारं ब्रह्मैवावस्थितमिति सर्वात्मकब्रह्मपृथग्भूतवस्तुसद्भावनिषेधपरत्वाभ्युपगमेन प्रतिपादिताः।
units.english: The texts which deny plurality are explained as allowed to be employed for the denial of the real existence of things apart from the Supreme Spirit, which is identical with all things, it being Supreme Spirit which subsists under all forms as the soul of all, all things sentient and unsentient being forms as being the body of absolute Spirit.[3]

units.sanskrit: किमत्र तत्त्वं भेदोऽभेद उभयात्मकं वा। सर्वं तत्त्वम्। तत्र सर्व शरीरतया सर्वप्रकारं ब्रह्मैवावस्थितमित्यभेदोभ्युपेयते। एकमेव ब्रह्म नानाभूतचिदचित्प्रकारान्नानात्वेनावस्थितमिति भेदाभेदौ। चिदचिदीश्वराणां स्वरूपस्वभाववैलक्षण्यादसंकराच्च भेदः।
units.english: What is the principle here involved, pluralism or monism, or a universe both one and more than one? Of these alternatives monism is admitted in saying that Supreme Spirit alone subsists in all forms as all is its body; both unity and plurality are admitted in saying that one only Supreme Spirit subsists under a plurality of forms diverse as soul and not-soul; and plurality is admitted in saying that the essential natures of soul, not-soul, and the Lord, are different, and not to be confounded.

units.sanskrit: तत्र चिद्रपाणां ऊ जीवात्मनामसंकु चितापरिच्छिन्ननिर्मलज्ञानरूपाणामनादिकर्मरूपाविद्यावेष्टितानां तत्तत्कर्मानुरूपज्ञानसंकोचविकासौ भोग्यभूताचित्संसर्गस्तदनुगुणसुखदुःखोपभोगद्वयरूपा भोक्तृता भगवत्प्रतिपत्तिर्भगवत्पदप्राप्तिरित्यादयः स्वभावाः।
units.english: Of these (soul, not-soul, and the Lord), individual spirits, or souls, consisting of uncontracted and unlimited pure knowledge, but enveloped in illusion, that is, in works from all eternity, undergo contraction and expansion of knowledge according to the degrees of their merits. Soul experiences fruition, and after reaping pleasures and pains proportionate to merits and demerits, there ensues knowledge of the Lord, or attainment of the sphere of the Lord.

units.sanskrit: अचिद्वस्तूनां तु भोग्यभूतानामचेतनत्वमपुरुषार्थत्वं विकारास्पदत्वमित्यादयः।
units.english: Of things which are not-soul, and which are objects of fruition (or experience of pleasure and pain), unconsciousness, unconduciveness to the end of man, susceptibility of modification, and the like, are the properties.

units.sanskrit: परस्येश्वरस्य भोक्तृभोग्ययोरन्तर्यामिरूपेणावस्थानमपरिच्छे द्यज्ञानैश्वर्यवीर्यशक्तितेजः प्रभृत्यनवधिकातिशयासंख्येयकल्याणगुणगणता स्वसंकल्पप्रवृत्तस्वेतरसमस्तचिदचिद्वस्तुजाततास्वाभिमतस्वानुरूपैकरूपदिव्यरूपनिरतिशयविविधानन्तभूषण तेत्यादयः।
units.english: Of the Supreme Lord the attributes are subsistence, as the internal controller (or animator) of both the subjects and the objects of fruition; the boundless glory of illimitable knowledge, dominion, majesty, power, brightness, and the like, the countless multitude of auspicious qualities; the generation at will of all things other than himself, whether spiritual or non-spiritual; various and infinite adornment with unsurpassable excellence, singular, uniform, and divine.

units.sanskrit: वेङ्कटनाथेन त्वित्थं निरटङ्कि पदार्थविभागः - द्रव्याद्रव्यप्रभेदान्मितमुभयविधं तद्विदस्तत्त्वमाहुः द्रव्यं द्वेधा विभक्तं जडमिति प्राच्यमव्यक्तकालो।
units.english: Veṅkaṭa-nātha has given the following distribution of things:— "Those who know it have declared the principle to be twofold, substance and non-substance; "Substance is dichotomised as unsentient and sentient; the former being the unevolved (avyakta), and time.

units.sanskrit: अन्त्यं प्रत्यक्पराक्च प्रथममुभयथा तत्र जीवेशभेदान्नित्या भूतिर्मतिच्चेत्यपरमिह जडामादिमां के चिदाहुः॥
units.english: "The 'distant' is eternal glory and intelligence; the other principle some have called the unsentient primary." Of these—

units.sanskrit: (तत्त्वमु. १/६) तत्र द्रव्यं दशावत्प्रकृतिरिह गुणैः सत्त्वपूर्वैरुपेता कालोब्दाद्याकृतिः स्यादणुरवगतिमाञ्जीव ईशोन्य आत्मा।
units.english: "Substance undergoes a plurality of conditions; the originant is possessed of goodness and the other cords; "Time has the form of years, &c.; soul is atomic and cognisant; the other spirit is the Lord;

units.sanskrit: संप्रोक्ता नित्यभूतिस्त्रिगुणसमधिका सत्त्वयुक्ता तथैव ज्ञातुर्ज्ञेयावभासो मतिरिति कथितं संग्रहाद् द्रव्यलक्ष्म॥ (तत्त्वमु. १/७) इत्यादिना।
units.english: "Eternal bliss has been declared as transcending the three cords (or modes of phenomenal existence), and also as characterised by goodness; "The cognisable manifestation of the cognisant is intelligence; thus are the characteristics of substance summarily recounted."

units.sanskrit: तत्र चिच्छब्दवाच्या जीवात्मानः परमात्मनः सकाशद्भिन्ना नित्याश्च।
units.english: Of these (soul, not-soul, and the Lord), individual spirits, called souls, are different from the Supreme Spirit and eternal.

units.sanskrit: तथा च श्रुतिःद्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया (मु.३/१/१।,श्वे,४/६) इत्यादिका।
units.english: Thus the text: Two birds, companions, friends, &c. (Rig-Veda, i.

units.sanskrit: अत एवोक्तं नानात्मानो व्यवस्थातः (वैःसू.३/२/२०) इति।
units.english: Accordingly it is stated (in the aphorisms of Kaṇāda, iii. 2, 20), Souls are diverse by reason of diversity of conditions.

units.sanskrit: तन्नित्यत्वमपिश्रुतिप्रसिद्धम्न जायते म्रियते वा विपश्चिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
units.english: The eternity of souls is often spoken of in revelation— "The soul is neither born, nor dies, nor having been shall it again cease to be;

units.sanskrit: अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे॥ (का.२.१८) इति।
units.english: "Unborn, unchanging, eternal, this ancient of days is not killed when the body is killed" (Bhagavad-gītā, ii.

units.sanskrit: अपरथा कृतप्रणाशाकृताभ्यागमप्रसङ्गः।
units.english: Otherwise (were the soul not eternal) there would follow a failure of requital and a fruition (of pleasures and pains) unmerited.

units.sanskrit: अत एवोक्तं वीतरागजन्मादर्शनात् ( न्या.सू.३/१/२५) इति।
units.english: It has accordingly been said (in the aphorisms of Gautaṃa, iii.

units.sanskrit: तदणुत्वमपि श्रुति प्रसिद्धम् - बालाग्रशतभागस्य शतधा कल्पितस्य च।
units.english: "If the hundredth part of a hair be imagined to be divided a hundred times,

units.sanskrit: भागो जीवः स विज्ञेयः स चानन्त्याय कल्यते॥
units.english: "The soul may be supposed a part of that, and yet it is capable of infinity."
And again—

units.sanskrit: आराग्रमात्रः पुरुषः (श्वे.५/८) अणुरात्मा चेतसा वेदितव्यः (मु.३/१/९) इति च।
units.english: "Soul is of the size of the extremity of the spoke of a wheel. Spirit is to be recognised by the intelligence as atomic."

units.sanskrit: अचिच्छब्दवाच्यं दृश्यं जडं जगत्त्रिविधं भोग्यभोगोपकरणभोगायतनभेदात्।
units.english: The visible, unsentient world, designated by the term not-soul, is divided into three, as the object, the instrument, or the site of fruition.

units.sanskrit: तस्य जगतः कâर्तोंपादानं चेश्वरपदार्थः पुरुषोत्तमो वासुदेवादिपदवेदनीयः।
units.english: Of this world the efficient and substantial cause is the Deity, known under the names Puruṣottama (best of spirits), Vāsudeva (a patronymic of Kṛṣṇa), and the like.

units.sanskrit: तदुप्युक्तम् - वासुदेवः परं ब्रह्म कल्याणगुणसंयुतः।
units.english: "Vāsudeva is the supreme absolute spirit, endowed with auspicious attributes,

units.sanskrit: भुवनानामुपादानं कर्ता जीवनियामकः॥इति॥
units.english: "The substantial cause, the efficient of the worlds, the animator of spirits."

units.sanskrit: स एव वासुदेवः परमकारुणिको भक्तवत्सलः परमपुरुषस्तदपासकानुगुणत्तत्फलप्रदानाय उ स्वलीलावशादर्चाविभवव्यूह सूक्ष्मान्तर्यामिभेदेन पञ्चधावतिष्ठते।
units.english: This same Vāsudeva, infinitely compassionate, tender to those devoted to him, the Supreme Spirit, with the purpose of bestowing various rewards apportioned to the deserts of his votaries in consequence of pastime, exists under five modes, distinguished as "adoration" (arcā), "emanation" (vibhava), "manifestation" (vyūha), "the subtile" (sūkṣma), and the "internal controller." (1.) "Adoration" is images, and so forth.

units.sanskrit: तत्रार्चा नाम प्रतिमादयः। रामाद्यवतारो विभवः।
units.english: (2.) "Emanation" is his incarnation, as Rāma, and so forth.

units.sanskrit: व्यूहश्चुर्विधो वासुदेवसंकर्षणप्रद्युम्नानिरुद्धसंज्ञकः।
units.english: (3.) His "manifestation" is fourfold, as Vāsudeva, Saṅkarshaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha.

units.sanskrit: सूक्ष्मं संपूर्णषड्गुणं वासुदेवाख्यं परं ब्रह्म।
units.english: (4.) "The subtile" is the entire Supreme Spirit, with six attributes, called Vāsudeva.

units.sanskrit: गुणा अपहतपाप्मत्वादयः।
units.english: His attributes are exemption from sin, and the rest.

units.sanskrit: सोपहतापाप्मा विजरो विमृत्युर्विशोको विजिघत्सोऽपिपासः सत्यकामः सत्यसंकल्पः (छा.८/७/३) इति श्रुतेः।
units.english: That he is exempt from sin is attested in the Vedic text: Passionless, deathless, without sorrow, without hunger, desiring truth, true in purpose.

units.sanskrit: अन्तर्यामी सकलजीवनियामकः। य आत्मनि तिष्ठन्नात्मानमन्तरो यमयति (बृ.मा.३/७/२२) इति श्रुतेः।
units.english: (5.) The "internal controller," the actuator of all spirits, according to the text: Who abiding in the soul, rules the soul within.

units.sanskrit: तत्र पूर्वपूर्वमूत्युपासनया पुरुषार्थपरिपन्थिदुरितनिचयक्षये सत्युत्तरोत्तरमूत्युपास्त्यधिकारः।
units.english: When by worshipping each former embodiment a mass of sins inimical to the end of the soul (i.e., emancipation) have been destroyed, the votary becomes entitled to practise the worship of each latter embodiment.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तम् - वासुदेवः स्वभक्ते षु वात्सल्यात्तत्तदीहितम्।
units.english: It has, therefore, been said— "Vāsudeva, in his tenderness to his votaries, gives, as desired by each,

units.sanskrit: अधिकार्यानुगुण्येन प्रयच्छति फलं बहु॥
units.english: "According to the merits of his qualified worshippers, large recompense.

units.sanskrit: तदर्थं लीलया स्वीयाः पञ्चर मूत्तीः करोति वै।
units.english: "For that end, in pastime he makes to himself his five embodiments;

units.sanskrit: प्रतिमादिकमर्चा स्यादवतारास्तु वैभवाः।
units.english: "Images and the like are 'adoration;' his incarnations are 'emanations;'

units.sanskrit: संकर्षणो वासुदेवः प्रद्युम्नश्चानिरुद्धकः। व्यूहश्चतुर्विधो ज्ञेयः सूक्ष्मं संपूर्णषड्गुणम्॥
units.english: "As Saṅkarshaṅa, Vāsudeva, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, his manifestation is to be known to be fourfold; 'the subtile' is the entire six attributes;

units.sanskrit: तेदव वासुदेवाख्यं परं ब्रह्म निगद्यते।
units.english: "That self-same called Vāsudeva is styled the Supreme Spirit;

units.sanskrit: अंतर्यामी जीवसंस्थो जीवप्रेरक ईरितः॥ य आत्मनीति वेदान्तवाक्यजालैर्निरूपितः।
units.english: "The internal controller is declared as residing in the soul, the actuator of the soul, "Described in a multitude of texts of the Upaniṣads, such as 'Who abiding in the soul.'

units.sanskrit: अर्चोंपासनया क्षिप्ते कल्मषेधिकृतो भवेत्॥
units.english: "By the worship of 'adoration,' a man casting off his defilement becomes a qualified votary;

units.sanskrit: विभवोपासने पश्चाद्वयूहोपास्तौ ततः परम्।
units.english: "By the subsequent worship of 'emanation,' he becomes qualified for the worship of 'manifestation;' next,

units.sanskrit: सूक्ष्मे तदनु शक्तः स्यादन्तर्यामिणमीक्षितुम्॥
units.english: "By the worship thereafter of 'the subtile,' he becomes able to behold the 'internal controller.'"

units.sanskrit: तदुपासनं च पञ्चविधमभिगमनमुपादानमिज्या स्वाध्यायो योग इति श्रीपञ्चरात्रेभिहितम्।
units.english: The worship of the Deity is described in the Pañca-rātra as consisting of five elements, viz., (1.) the access, (2.) the preparation, (3.) oblation, (4.) recitation, (5.) devotion.

units.sanskrit: तत्राभिगमनं नाम देवतास्थानमार्गस्य संमार्जनोपलेपनादि।
units.english: Of these, access is the sweeping, smearing, and so forth, of the way to the temple.

units.sanskrit: उपादानं गन्ध्पुष्पादिपूजासाधनसंपादनम्।
units.english: The preparation is the provision of perfumes, flowers, and the like appliances of worship.

units.sanskrit: इज्या नाम देवतापूजनम्।
units.english: Oblation is worship of the deities.

units.sanskrit: स्वाध्यायो नाम अर्थानुसंधानपूर्वको मन्त्रजपो वैष्णवसूक्तस्तोत्रपाठो नामसंकीर्तनं तत्त्वप्रतिपादकशास्त्राभ्यासश्च।
units.english: Recitation is the muttered ejaculation of sacred texts, with attention to what they mean, the rehearsal of hymns and lauds of Viṣṇu, the commemoration of his names, and study of institutes which set forth the truth.

units.sanskrit: योगो नाम देवतानुसंघानम्।
units.english: Devotion is meditation on the Deity.

units.sanskrit: एवमुपासनाकर्मसमुच्चीतेन विज्ञानेन द्रष्टृदर्शने नष्टे भगवद्भक्तस्य तन्निष्ठस्य भक्तवत्सलः परमकारुणिकः पुरुषोत्तमः स्वयाथात्म्यानुभवानुगुणनिरवधिकानन्दरूपं पुनरावृत्तिरहितं स्वपदं प्रयच्छति।
units.english: When the vision of the visible world has been brought to a close by knowledge accumulated by the merit of such worship, the infinitely compassionate Supreme Spirit, tender to his votaries, bestows upon the votary devoted to his lord and absorbed in his lord, his own sphere infinite and endless, marked by consciousness of being like him, from which there is no future return (to the sorrows of transmigratory existence).

units.sanskrit: तथा च स्मृतिः - मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम्। नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिंद्धिं परमां गताः॥ (भ.गी.८/१५) इति।
units.english: So the traditionary text— "When they have come to me, the high-souled no longer undergo future birth, a receptacle of pain, transitory, having attained to the supreme consummation.

units.sanskrit: स्वभक्तं वासुदेवोपि संप्राप्यानन्दमक्षयम्। पुनरावृत्तिरहितं स्वीयं धाम प्रयच्छति॥
units.english: "Vāsudeva, having found his votary, bestows upon him his own mansion, blissful, undecaying, from whence there is no more return."

units.sanskrit: तदेतत्सर्वं हृदि निधाय महोपनिषन्मतावलम्बनेन भगवद्धौधायनाचार्यकृतां ब्रह्मसूत्रबृत्तिं विस्तीर्णामालक्ष्य रामानुजः शारीरकमीमांसाभाष्यमकार्षीत्।
units.english: After laying up all this in his heart, leaning upon the teaching of the great Upaniṣad, and finding the gloss on the Vedānta aphorisms by the venerated Bodhāyanacārya too prolix, Rāmānuja composed a commentary on the Śārīrakamīmānsā (or Vedānta theosophy).

units.sanskrit: तत्राथातो ब्रह्मजिज्ञासा (ब्र.सू.१/१/१) इति प्रथमसूत्रस्यायमर्थः अत्राथशब्दः पूर्ववृत्तकर्माधिगमनानन्तर्यार्थः।
units.english: In this the sense of the first aphorism, "Then hence the absolute must be desired to be known," is given as follows:—The word then in this aphorism means, after understanding the hitherto-current sacred rites.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं वृत्तिकारेणवृत्तात्कर्माधिगमादनन्तरं ब्रह्म विविदिषतीति।
units.english: Thus the glossator writes: "After learning the sacred rites," he desires to know the absolute.

units.sanskrit: अतःशब्दो हेत्वर्थः। अधीतसाङ्गवेदस्याधिगततदर्थस्य विनश्वरफलात्कर्मणो विरक्तत्वाद्धेतोः स्थिरमोक्षाभिलाषुकस्य तदुपायभूत - ब्रह्मजिज्ञासा भवति।
units.english: The word hence states the reason, viz., because one who has read the Veda and its appendages and understands its meaning is averse from sacred rites, their recompense being perishable. The wish to know the absolute springs up in one who longs for permanent liberation, as being the means of such liberation.

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मशब्देन स्वभावतो निरस्तसमस्तदोषानवधिकातिशयासंख्येयकल्याणगुणः पुरुषोत्तमोभिधीयते।
units.english: By the word absolute is designated the Supreme Spirit, from whom are essentially excluded all imperfections, who is of illimitable excellence, and of innumerable auspicious attributes.

units.sanskrit: एवं च कर्मज्ञानस्य तदनुष्ठानस्य च वैराग्योत्पादनद्वारा चित्तकल्मषापनयद्वारा च ब्रह्मज्ञानं प्रति साधनत्वेन तयोः कार्यकारणत्वेन पूर्वोंत्तरमीमांसयोरेकशास्त्रत्वम्।
units.english: Since then the knowledge of sacred rites and the performance of those rites is mediately through engendering dispassionateness, and through putting away the defilement of the understanding, an instrument of the knowledge of the absolute; and knowledge of sacred rites and knowledge of the absolute being consequently cause and effect, the former and the latter Mīmānsā constitute one system of institutes.

units.sanskrit: अतएव वृत्तिकारा एकमेवेदं शास्त्रं जैमिनीयेन षोडशलक्षणेनेत्याहुः।
units.english: On this account the glossator has described this system as one with the sixteenfold system of Jaimini.

units.sanskrit: कर्मफलस्य क्षयित्वं ब्रह्मज्ञानफलस्य चाक्षयित्वं परीक्ष्य लोकान्कर्मचितान्ब्राह्मणो निर्वेदमायान्नास्त्यकृतः कृतेन (मु.१/२/१२) इत्यादिश्रुतिभिरनुमानार्थापत्त्युपबृंहिताभिः प्रत्यपादि।
units.english: That the fruit of sacred rites is perishable, and that of the knowledge of the absolute imperishable, has been laid down in virtue of Vedic texts, such as: Scanning the spheres gained by rites, let him become passionless; Not wrought by the rite performed, accompanied with inference and disjunctive reasoning.

units.sanskrit: एकै कनिन्दया कर्मविशिष्टस्य ज्ञानस्य मोक्षसाधनत्वं दर्शयति श्रुतिःअन्धं तमः प्रविशन्ति येऽविद्यामुपासते। ततो भूय इव ते तमो य उ विद्यायां रताः॥ (बृ.४/४/१०,ई.९) विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह। अविद्यया मृत्युं तीत्वा विद्ययामृतमश्र्नुते।
units.english: Revelation, by censuring each when unaccompanied by the other, shows that it is knowledge together with works that is efficacious of emancipation, in the words: Blind darkness they enter who prefer illusion, and a greater darkness still do they enter who delight in knowledge only; knowledge and illusion, he who knows these both, he passing beyond death together with illusion, tastes immortality by knowledge.

units.sanskrit: (ई.११) इत्यादि। तदुक्तं पाञ्चरात्ररहस्येस एव करुणासिन्धुर्भगवान् भक्तवत्सलः।
units.english: Conformably it is said in the Pañcarātra-rahasya— "That ocean of compassion, the Lord, tender to his votaries,

units.sanskrit: उपासकानुरोधेन भजते मूर्तिपञ्चकम्॥
units.english: "For his worshipper's sake takes five embodiments upon him.

units.sanskrit: तदर्चाविभवव्यूहसूक्ष्मान्तर्यामिसंज्ञकम्।
units.english: "These are styled Adoration, Emanation, Manifestation, the Subtile, the Internal Controller,

units.sanskrit: यदाश्रित्यैव चिद्वर्गस्तत्तज्ज्ञेयं प्रपद्यते॥
units.english: "Resorting whereto souls attain to successive stages of knowledge.

units.sanskrit: पूर्वपूर्वोंदितोपास्तिविशेषक्षीणकल्मषः।
units.english: "As a man's sins are worn away by each successive worship,

units.sanskrit: उत्तरोत्तर्रमूत्तीनामुपास्त्यधिकृतो भवेत्।
units.english: "He becomes qualified for the worship of each next embodiment.

units.sanskrit: एवं ह्यरहरः श्रौतस्मार्तधर्मानुसारतः।
units.english: "Thus day by day, according to religion, revealed and traditional,

units.sanskrit: उक्तोपासनया पुंसां वासुदेवः प्रसीदति।
units.english: "By the aforesaid worship Vāsudeva becomes propitious to mankind.

units.sanskrit: प्रसन्नात्मा हरिर्भक्त्या निदिध्यासनरूपया।
units.english: "Hari, when propitiated by devotion in the form of meditation,

units.sanskrit: अविद्यां कर्मसंघातरूपां सद्यो निवर्तयेत्।
units.english: "At once brings to a close that illusion which is the aggregate of works.

units.sanskrit: ततः स्वाभाविकाः पुंसां ते संसारतिरोहिताः।
units.english: "Then in souls the essential attributes, from which transmigration has vanished,

units.sanskrit: आविर्भवन्ति कल्याणाः सर्वज्ञत्वादयो गुणाः।
units.english: "Are manifested, auspicious, omniscience, and the rest.

units.sanskrit: एवं गुणाः समानाः स्युर्मुक्तानामीश्वरस्य च।
units.english: "These qualities are common to the emancipated spirits and the Lord,

units.sanskrit: सर्वकर्तृत्वमेवैकं तेभ्यो देवे विशिष्यते॥
units.english: "Universal efficiency alone among them is peculiar to the Deity.

units.sanskrit: मुक्तास्तु शेषिणि ब्रह्मण्यशेषे शेषरूपिणः।
units.english: "Emancipated spirits are ulterior to the infinite absolute, which is unsusceptible of aught ulterior;

units.sanskrit: सर्वानश्नुवते कामान् सह तेन विपश्चिता॥इति॥
units.english: "They enjoy all beatitudes together with that Spirit."

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्तापत्रयातुरैरमृतत्वाय पुरुषोत्तमादिपदवेदनीयं ब्रह्म जिज्ञासितव्यमित्युक्तं भवति।
units.english: It is therefore stated that those who suffer the three kinds of pain must, for the attainment of immortality, investigate the absolute spirit known under such appellations as the Highest Being.

units.sanskrit: प्रकृतिप्रत्ययौ प्रत्ययार्थं प्राधान्येन सह ब्रूत इतः सनोन्यत्रेति वचनबलादिच्छाया इष्यमाणप्रधानत्वादिष्यमाणं ज्ञानमिह विधेयम्।
units.english: According to the maxim: The base and the suffix convey the meaning conjointly, and of these the meaning of the suffix takes the lead, the notion of desire is predominant (in the word jijñāsitavya), and desired knowledge is the predicate (in the aphorism, Then hence the absolute must be desired to be known).

units.sanskrit: तच्च ध्यानोपासनादिशब्दवाच्यं वेदनं न तु वाक्यजन्यमापातज्ञानम्। पदसंदर्भश्राविणो व्युत्पन्नस्य विधानमन्तरेणापि प्राप्तत्वात्। आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः (बृ.२/४/५) आत्मेत्यवोपासीत (बृ.१/४/७) विज्ञाय प्रज्ञां कु र्वीत (बृ.४/४/२१) अनुविद्य विजानाति छा.८/७/१) इत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः।
units.english: Knowledge is cognition designated by such terms as meditation, devotion; not the merely superficial knowledge derived from verbal communication, such being competent to any one who hears a number of words and understands the force of each, even without any predication; in conformity with such Vedic texts as: Self indeed it is that is to be seen, to be heard, to be thought, to be pondered; He should meditate that it is self alone; Having known, let him acquire excellent wisdom; He should know that which is beyond knowledge.

units.sanskrit: अत्र श्रोतव्य इत्यनुवादः। अध्ययनविधिना साङ्गस्य स्वाध्यायस्य ग्रहणेधीतवेदस्य पुरुषस्य प्रयोजन वदर्थदर्शनात्तान्निर्णयाय स्वरसत एव श्रवणे प्रवर्तमानतया तस्य प्राप्तत्वात्।
units.english: In these texts "to be heard" is explanatory, hearing being understood (but not enounced) in the text about sacred study (viz., ṣaḍaṅgena vedo'dhyeyo jñeyaśca, the Veda, with its six appendages, is to be studied and known); so that a man who has studied the Veda must of his own accord, in acquiring the Veda and its appendages, engage in "hearing," in order to ascertain the sense by examining it and the occasion of its enouncement.

units.sanskrit: मन्तव्य इति चानुवादः। श्रवणप्रतिष्ठार्थत्वेन मननस्यापि प्राप्तत्वात्। अप्राप्ते शास्त्रमर्थवदिति न्यायात्।
units.english: The term "to be thought" (or "to be inferred") is also explanatory, cogitation (or inference) being understood as the complementary meaning of hearing, according to the aphorism: Before its signification is attained the system is significant.

units.sanskrit: ध्यानं च तैलधारावदविच्छिन्नस्मृतिसंतानरूपम्। ध्रुवा स्मृतिः स्मृतिप्रतिलम्भे सर्वग्रन्थीनां विप्रमोक्ष इति ध्रुवायाः स्मृतेरेव मोक्षोपायत्वश्रवणात्।
units.english: Meditation is a reminiscence consisting of an unbroken succession of reminiscences like a stream of oil, it being revealed in the text, in continuity of reminiscence there is a solution of all knots,—that it is unintermittent reminiscence that is the means of emancipation.

units.sanskrit: सा च स्मृतिर्दर्शनसमानाकारा।
units.english: And this reminiscence is tantamount to intuition.

units.sanskrit: भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः।
units.english: "Cut is his heart's knot, solved are all his doubts,

units.sanskrit: क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्टे परावरे॥
units.english: "And exhausted are all his works, when he has seen the Highest and Lowest,"

units.sanskrit: (मु. २/२/८) इत्यनेनैकवाक्यत्वात्।
units.english: because he becomes one with that Supreme.

units.sanskrit: तथा च आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः (वृ.२/४/५) इत्यनेनास्यादर्शनरूपता विधीयते।
units.english: So also in the words, Self indeed is to be seen, it is predicated of this reminiscence that it is an intuition.

units.sanskrit: भवति च भावना प्रकर्षात्स्मृतेर्दर्शनरूपत्वम्।
units.english: Reminiscence becomes intuitional through the vivacity of the representations.

units.sanskrit: वाक्यकारेणैतत्सर्वं प्रपञ◌आइ◌◌चतं वेदनमुपासनं स्यादित्यादिना।
units.english: The author of the Vākya has treated of all this in detail in the passage beginning Cognition is meditation.

units.sanskrit: तदेव ध्यानं विशिनष्टि श्रुतिः - नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन।
units.english: The characters of this meditation are laid out in the text: This soul is not attainable by exposition, nor by wisdom, nor by much learning; Whom God chooses by him God may be attained.

units.sanskrit: यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लम्भस्तस्यैव आत्मा विवृणुते तनूंस्वाम्॥
units.english: To him this self unfolds its own nature.

units.sanskrit: प्रियतम एव हि वरणीयो भवति। यथायं प्रियतम आत्मानं प्राप्नोति तथा स्वयमेव भगवान्प्रयतत इति भगवतैवाभिहितम् - तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम्।
units.english: For it is that which is dearest which is choice-worthy, and as the soul finds itself most dear, so the Lord is of Himself most dear, as was declared by the Lord Himself— "To them always devoted, who worship me with love,

units.sanskrit: ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते॥ (भ.गी.१०.१०) इति। पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लम्यस्त्वनन्यया।
units.english: "I give the devotion of understanding whereby they come to me." And again— "That Supreme Spirit, Arjuna, is attainable by faith unwavering."

units.sanskrit: भक्तिस्तु निरतिशयानन्दप्रियानन्यप्रयोजनसकलेतरवैतृष्ण्यवज्जानविशेष एव।
units.english: But devotion (or faith) is a kind of cognition which admits no other motive than the illimitable beatitude, and is free from all other desires; and the attainment of this devotion is by discrimination and other means.

units.sanskrit: तत्सिद्धिश्च विवेकादिभ्यो भवतीति वाक्यकारेणोक्तं तल्लब्धिर्विवेकविमोकाभ्यासक्रियाकल्याणानवसादानुद्धर्षेभ्यः संभवान्निर्वचनाच्चेति।
units.english: As is said by the author of the Vākya: Attainment thereof results from discrimination (viveka), exemption (vimoka), practice (abhyāsa), observance (kriyā), excellence (kalyāṇa), freedom from despondency (anavasāda), satisfaction (anuddharsha), according to the equivalence (of the definition), and the explication (of these terms).

units.sanskrit: तत्र विवेको नामादष्टादन्नात्सत्त्वशुद्धि उः। अत्र निर्वचनम - आहारशुद्धेः सत्त्वशुद्धिः सत्त्वशुद्धया ध्रुवा स्मृतिरिति।
units.english: Of these means, discrimination is purity of nature, resultant from eating undefiled food, and the explication (of discrimination) is From purity of diet, purity of understanding, and by purity of understanding the unintermittent reminiscence.

units.sanskrit: विमोकः कामानभिष्वङ्गः। शान्त उपासीतेति निर्वचनम्।
units.english: Exemption is non-attachment to sensuous desires; the explication being, Let the quietist meditate.

units.sanskrit: पुनः पुनः संशीलनमभ्यासः। निर्वचनं च स्मार्तमुदाहृतं भाष्यकारेण ऽसदा तद्भावनावितः (गी.८/६) इति।
units.english: Practice is reiteration; and of this a traditionary explication is quoted (from the Bhagavad-gītā) by (Rāmānuja) the author of the commentary: For ever modified by the modes thereof.

units.sanskrit: श्रौतस्मार्तकर्मानुष्ठानं शक्तितः क्रिया। क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठ इति निर्वचनम्।
units.english: Observance is the performance of rites enjoined in revelation and tradition according to one's ability; the explication being (the Vedic text), He who has performed rites is the best of those that know the supreme.

units.sanskrit: सत्यार्जवदयादानादीनि कल्याणानि। सत्येन लभ्यत इत्यादि निर्वचनम्।
units.english: The excellences are veracity, integrity, clemency, charity (alms-giving), and the like; the explication being, It is attained by veracity.

units.sanskrit: दैन्यविपर्ययोनवसादः। नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यः (मु.३/२/४) इति निर्वचनम्।
units.english: Freedom from despondency is the contrary of dejection; the explication being, This soul is not attained by the faint-hearted.

units.sanskrit: तद्विपर्ययजातुष्टिरुद्धर्षः। तद्विपर्ययोनुद्धर्षः। शान्तो दान्त इति निर्वचनम्।
units.english: Satisfaction is the contentment which arises from the contrary of dejection; the explication being, Quiescent, self-subdued.

units.sanskrit: तदेववंविधनियमविशेषसमासादितपुरुषोत्तमप्रसादविध्वस्ततमःस्वान्तस्यानन्यप्रयोजनानवरतनिरतिशयप्रियविशदात्मप्रत्ययावभासतापन्नध्यानरूपया भक्त्या पुरुषोत्तमपदं लभ्यत इति सिद्धम्।
units.english: It has thus been shown that by the devotion of one in whom the darkness has been dispelled by the grace of the Supreme Spirit, propitiated by certain rites and observances, which devotion is meditation transformed into a presentative manifestation of soul, without ulterior motive, as incessantly and illimitably desired, the sphere of the Supreme Spirit (Vaikuṇṭha) is attained.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं यामुनेन उभयपरिकर्मितस्वान्तस्यैकान्तिकात्यन्तिकभक्तियोगो लभ्य इति। ज्ञानकर्मयोगसंस्कृतान्तःकरणस्येत्यर्थः।
units.english: Thus Yāmuna says: Attainable by the final and absolute devotion of faith in one internally purified by both (works and knowledge); that is, in one whose internal organ is rectified by the devotion of works and knowledge.

units.sanskrit: किं पुनर्ब्रह्म जिज्ञासितव्यमित्यपेक्षायां लक्षणमुक्तं ऽजन्माद्यस्य यतः' (व्र.सू.१/१/२) इति।
units.english: In anticipation of the inquiry, But what absolute is to be desired to be known? the definition is given (in the second aphorism). From which the genesis, and so forth, of this.

units.sanskrit: जन्मादीति सृष्टिस्थितिप्रलयम्।
units.english: The genesis, and so forth, the creation (emanation), sustentation, and retractation (of the universe).

units.sanskrit: तद्गुणसंविज्ञानो बहुव्रीहिः। अस्याचिन्त्यविविधविचित्ररचनस्य नियतदेशकालभोगब्रह्यादिस्तम्बपर्यन्तक्षेत्रज्ञमिश्रस्य जगतो यतो यस्मात्सर्वेश्वरान्निखिलहेयप्रत्यनीकस्वरूपात्सत्यसंकल्पाद्यनवधिकातिशयासंख्येयकल्याणगुणात्सर्वज्ञात्सर्वशक्तेः पुंसः सृष्टिस्थितिप्रलयाः प्रवर्तन्त इति सूत्रार्थः।
units.english: The purport of the aphorism is that the emanation, sustentation, and retractation of this universe, inconceivably multiform in its structure, and interspersed with souls, from Brahmā to a tuft of grass, of determinate place, time, and fruition, is from this same universal Lord, whose essence is contrary to all qualities which should be escaped from, of illimitable excellences, such as indefeasible volition, and of innumerable auspicious attributes, omniscient, and omnipotent.

units.sanskrit: इत्थंभूते ब्रह्मणि किं प्रमाणमिति जिज्ञासायां शास्त्रमेव प्रमाणमित्युक्तं शास्त्रयोनित्वात् (व्र.सू.१/१/३) इति।
units.english: In anticipation of the further inquiry, What proof is there of an absolute of this nature? It is stated that the system of institutes itself is the evidence (in the third aphorism): Because it has its source from the system.

units.sanskrit: शास्त्रं योनिः कारणं प्रमाणं यस्य तच्छास्त्रयोनि।
units.english: To have its source from the system is to be that whereof the cause or evidence is the system.

units.sanskrit: तस्य भावस्तत्त्वं तस्मात्। ब्रह्मज्ञानकारणत्वाच्छास्त्रस्य तद्योनित्वं ब्रह्मण इत्यर्थः।
units.english: The system, then, is the source (or evidence) of the absolute, as being the cause of knowing the self, which is the cause of knowing the absolute.

units.sanskrit: न च ब्रह्मणः प्रमाणन्तरगम्यत्वं शङ्कितुं शक्यम्। अतीन्द्रियत्वेन प्रत्यक्षस्य तत्र प्रवृत्त्यनुपपत्तेः।
units.english: Nor is the suspicion possible that the absolute may be reached by some other form of evidence. For perception can have no conversancy about the absolute since it is supersensible.

units.sanskrit: नापि महार्णवादिकं सकर्तृकं कार्यत्वाद्धटवदित्यनुमानम्। तस्य पूतिकू ष्माण्डायमानत्वात्।
units.english: Nor can inference, for the illation, the ocean, and the rest, must have a maker, because it is an effect like a water-pot, is worth about as much as a rotten pumpkin.

units.sanskrit: तल्लक्षणं ब्रह्म ऽयतो वा इमानि भूतानिऽ (तढ.२/१/१) इत्यादिवाक्यं प्रतिपादयतीति स्थितम्।
units.english: It is evinced that it is such texts as, Whence also these elements, that prove the existence of the absolute thus described.

units.sanskrit: यद्यपि ब्रह्म प्रमाणन्तरगोचरतां नावतरति तथापि प्रवृत्ति निवृत्तिपरत्वाभावे सिद्धरूपं ब्रह्म न शास्त्रं प्रतिपादयितुं प्रभवतीत्यतत्पर्यनुयोगपरिहायोक्तं - तत्तु समन्वयात् ( ब्र.सू. १/१/४) इति।
units.english: Though the absolute (it may be objected) be unsusceptible of any other kind of proof, the system, did it not refer to activity and cessation of activity, could not posit the absolute aforesaid. To avoid by anticipation any queries on this point, it is stated (in the fourth aphorism): But that is from the construction.

units.sanskrit: तुशब्दः प्रसक्ताशङ्काव्यावृत्त्यर्थः।
units.english: This is intended to exclude the doubt anticipated.

units.sanskrit: तच्छास्त्रप्रमाणकत्वं ब्रह्मणः संभवत्येव। कु तः समन्वयात्। परमपुरुषार्थभूतस्यैव ब्रह्मणोभिधेयतयान्वयादित्यर्थः न च प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्त्योरन्यतरविरहिणः प्रयोजनशून्यत्वम्। स्वरूपपरेष्वपि पुत्रस्ते जातो नायं सर्प इत्यादिषु हर्षप्राप्तिभयनिवृत्तिरूपप्रयोजनवत्त्वं दृष्टमेवेति न किं चिदनुपपन्नम्।
units.english: The evidence, then, of the system is the only evidence that can be given of the absolute. Why? Because of the construction, that is because the absolute, that is, the highest end for man, is construed as the subject (of the first aphorism, viz., Then thence the absolute is to be desired to be known). Moreover, a sentence which has nothing to do either with activity or with cessation of activity is not therefore void of purpose, for we observe that sentences merely declaratory of the nature of things, such as, A son is born to you, This is not a snake, convey a purpose, viz., the cessation of joy or of fear. Thus there is nothing unaccounted for.

units.sanskrit: दिङ्मात्रमत्र प्रदर्शितम्।
units.english: We have here given only a general indication.

units.sanskrit: विस्तरस्त्वाकरादेवावगन्तव्य इति विस्तारभीरुणोदास्यत इति सर्वमनाकु लम्॥ अथ पूर्णप्रज्ञदर्शनम् ॥५॥
units.english: The details may be learnt from the original (viz., Rāmānuja's Bhāṣya on the Vedānta aphorisms); we therefore decline a further treatment, apprehensive of prolixity; and thus all is clear.[4]

units.sanskrit: तदेतद्रामानुजमतं जीवाणुत्वदासत्व् -वेदापौरुषेयत्वसिद्धार्थबोधकत्वस्वतःप्रमाणत्वप्रमाणत्रित्वपञ्चरात्रोपजीव्यत्वप्रपञ्चभेदसत्यत्वादिसाम्येऽपि परस्पर विरुद्धभेदादिपक्षत्रयकक्षीकारेण क्षपणकपक्षनिक्षिप्तमित्युपेक्षमाणः, ऽस आत्मा तत्त्व मसिऽ (छा०६।८।७) इत्यादिवेदान्तवाक्यजातस्य भङ्ग्यन्तरेणर्थान्तरपरत्वमुपपाद्य ब्रह्ममीमांसाविवरणव्याजेन आनन्दतीर्थः प्रस्थनान्तरमास्थिषत।
units.english: Ānanda-tīrtha (Pūrṇa-prajña, or Madhva) rejected this same Rāmānuja system, because, though like his own views, it teaches the atomic size of the soul, the servitude of the soul, the existence of the Veda without any personal author, the authenticity of the Veda, the self-evidence of the instruments of knowledge, the triad of evidences, dependency upon the Pañca-rātra, the reality of plurality in the universe, and so forth,—yet, in accepting three hypotheses as to reciprocally contradictory divisions, &c., it coincides with the tenets of the Jainas.

units.sanskrit: तन्मते हि द्विविधं तत्त्वं स्वतन्त्रपरतन्त्रभेदात्। तदुक्तं तत्त्वविवेके - स्वतन्त्रं परतन्त्रं च द्विविधं तत्त्वमिष्यते।
units.english: For in his doctrine ultimate principles are dichotomised into independent and dependent; as it is stated in the Tattva-viveka:— "Independent and dependent, two principles are received;

units.sanskrit: स्वतन्त्रो भगवान्विष्णुर्निर्दोंषोऽशेषसद्गुणः॥इति।
units.english: "The independent is Viṣṇu the Lord, exempt from imperfections, and of inexhaustible excellences."

units.sanskrit: ननु सजातीयविजातीयस्वगतनानात्वशून्यं ब्रह्म तत्तवमिति प्रतिपादके षु वेदान्तेषु जागरुके षु कथमशेषसद्गुणत्वं कथ्यत इति चेत्, मैवम्। भेदुप्रमापकबहप्रमाणविरोधेन तेषां तत्र प्रामाण्यानुपपत्तेः। तथा हि, प्रत्यक्षं तावदिदमस्माद्भिन्नम् इति नीलपीतादेर्भेदमध्यक्षयति।
units.english: Here it will be urged (by the Advaita-vādins): Why predicate of the absolute these inexhaustible excellences in the teeth of the Upaniṣads, which lay down that the absolute principle is void of homogeneity and heterogeneity, and of all plurality in itself? To this be it replied: Not so, for these texts of the Upaniṣads, as contradictory of many proofs positive of duality, cannot afford proof of universal unity; perception, for example, in the consciousness, This is different from that, pronounces a difference between things, blue and yellow, and so forth.

units.sanskrit: अथ मन्येथाः - किं प्रत्यक्षं भेदमेवावगाहते किं वा धर्मिप्रतियोगिघटितम् ? न प्रथमः, धर्मिप्रतियोगिप्रतिप्रत्तिमन्तरेण तत्सापेक्षस्य भेदस्याशक्याध्यवसायात्वात्। द्वितीयेऽपि धर्मिप्रतियोगिग्रहणपुरःसरं भेदग्रहणमथवा युगपत्तत्सर्वग्रहणम् ? न पूर्वः, बुद्धेर्विरम्य व्यापाराभावात्। अन्योन्याश्रयप्रसङ्गाच्च।
units.english: On the latter alternative it must be asked, Is the apprehension of the difference preceded by an apprehension of the thing and its contrary, or are all the three (the thing, its contrary, and the contrariety) simultaneously apprehended? It cannot be thus preceded, for the operation of the intellect is without delay (or without successive steps), and there would also result a logical seesaw (apprehension of the difference presupposing apprehension of the thing and its contrary, and apprehension of the thing and its contrary presupposing apprehension of the difference).

units.sanskrit: नापि चरमः, कार्यकारणबुद्धयोयौंगपद्याभावात्। धर्मिप्रतीतिर्हि भेदप्रत्ययस्य कारणम्। एवं प्रतियोगिप्रतीतिरपि। संनिहितेऽपि धर्मिण व्यवहितप्रतियोगिज्ञानमन्तरेण भेदस्याज्ञातत्त्वेनान्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां कार्यकारणभावावगमात्।
units.english: Nor can there be a simultaneous apprehension (of the thing, its contrary, and the difference); for cognitions related as cause and effect cannot be simultaneous, and the cognition of the thing is the cause of the recognition of the difference; the causal relation between the two being recognised by a concomitance and non-concomitance (mutual exclusion), the difference not being cognised even when the thing is present, without a cognition of its absent contrary.

units.sanskrit: तस्मान्न भेदप्रत्यक्षं सुप्रसरमिति चेत्।
units.english: The perception of difference, therefore (the opponent concludes), is not easily admissible.

units.sanskrit: किं वस्तुस्वरूपभेदवादिनं प्रति इमानि दूषणानि उद्धुष्य न्ते, किं वा धर्मभेदवादिनं प्रति ? प्रथमे चोरापराधान्माण्डव्यनिग्रहन्यायापातः।
units.english: To this let the reply be as follows:—Are these objections proclaimed against one who maintains a difference identical with the things themselves, or against one who maintains a difference between things as the subjects of attributes? In the former case, you will be, as the saying runs, punishing a respectable Brāhman for the offence of a thief, the objections you adduce being irrelevant.

units.sanskrit: ननु वस्तुस्वरूपस्यैव भेदत्वे प्रतियोगिसापेक्षत्वं न घटते घटवत्। प्रतियोगिसापेक्ष एव सर्वत्र भेदः प्रथत इति चेन्न। प्रथमं सर्वतो विलक्षणतया वस्तुस्वरूपे ज्ञायमाने प्रतियोग्यपेक्षया विशिष्टव्यवहारोपपत्तेः। तथा हिपरिमाणघटितं वस्तुस्वरूपं प्रथममवगम्यते। पश्चात्प्रतियोगि विशेषापेक्षया ह्रस्वं दीर्घमिति तदेव विशिष्य व्यवहारभाजनं भवति।
units.english: If it be urged that if it is the essence of the thing that is the difference, then it will no longer require a contrary counterpart; but if difference presuppose a contrary counterpart, it will exist everywhere; this statement must be disallowed, for while the essence of a thing is first known as different from everything else, the determinate usage (name and notion) may be shown to depend upon a contrary counterpart; for example, the essence of a thing so far as constituted by its dimensions is first cognised, and afterwards it becomes the object of some determinate judgment, as long or short in relation to some particular counterpart (or contrasted object).

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं विष्णुतत्त्वनिर्णये- ऽन च विशेषणविशेष्यतया भेदसिद्धिः। विशेषणविशेष्यभावश्च भेदापेक्षः। धर्मिप्रतियोग्यपेक्षया भेदसिद्धिः। भेदापेक्षं च धर्मिप्रतियोगित्वमित्यन्योन्याश्रयतया भेदस्यायुक्तिः।
units.english: Accordingly, it is said in the Viṣṇu-tattva-nirṇaya: "Difference is not proved to exist by the relation of determinant and determinate; for this relation of determinant and determinate (or predicate and subject) presupposes difference; and if difference were proved to depend upon the thing and its counterpart, and the thing and its counterpart to presuppose difference, difference as involving a logical circle could not be accounted for; but difference is itself a real predicament (or ultimate entity).

units.sanskrit: पदार्थस्वरूपत्वाद्भेदस्यऽ- इत्यादिना। अत एव गवार्थिनो गवयदर्शनान्न प्रवर्तन्ते, गो शब्दं च न स्मरन्ति।
units.english: For this reason (viz., because difference is a thing) it is that men in quest of a cow do not act (as if they had found her) when they see a gayal, and do not recall the word cow.

units.sanskrit: न च नीरक्षीरादौ स्वरूपे गृह्यमाणे भेदप्रतिभासोऽपि स्यादिति भणनीयम्। समानाभिहारादिप्रतिबन्धकबलाद् भेदभानव्यवहाराभावोपपत्तिः। तदुक्तम् - अतिदूरात्सामीप्यादिन्द्रियघातान्मनोऽनवस्थानात्।
units.english: Nor let it be objected that (if difference be a real entity and as such perceived) on seeing a mixture of milk and water, there would be a presentation of difference; for the absence of any manifestation of, and judgment about, the difference, may be accounted for by the force of (the same) obstructives (as hinder the perception of other things), viz., aggregation of similars and the rest." Thus it has been said (in the Sāṅkhya-kārikā, v.

units.sanskrit: सौक्ष्म्याद् व्यवधानादभिभवात्समानाभिहाराच्च॥
units.english: "From subtilty, from interposition, from being overpowered, and from aggregation of similars."

units.sanskrit: सां.का.७) अतिदूरात् - गिरिशिखरवर्तिपर्वतादौ, अतिसामीप्यात्लोचनाञ्जानदौ, इन्द्रियघातात्विद्युदादौ, मनोऽनवस्थानात्कामाद्युप्लुतमनस्कस्य स्फीतालोकवर्तिनि घटादौ, सौक्ष्म्यात्परमाण्वादौ, व्यवधानात्कु डयान्तर्हिते, अभिभवात्दिवा प्रदीपप्रभादौ, समानाभिहारात्नीरक्षीरादौ यथावत् ग्रहणं नास्तीत्यर्थः।
units.english: There is no perception respectively of a tree and the like on the peak of a mountain, because of its too great remoteness; of collyrium applied to the eyes, and so forth, because of too great proximity; of lightning and the like, because of a defect in the organs; of a jar or the like in broad daylight, by one whose common sensory is bewildered by lust and other passions, because of instability of the common sensory; of an atom and the like, because of their subtility; of things behind a wall, and so forth, because of interposition; of the light of a lamp and the like, in the day-time, because of its being overpowered; of milk and water, because of the aggregation of similars.

units.sanskrit: भवतु वा धर्मभेदवादस्तथापि न कश्चिद्दोषः। धर्मिप्रतियोगिग्रहणे सति पश्चात्तद्धटितभेदग्रहणोपपत्तेः।
units.english: Or let the hypothesis of difference in qualities be granted, and no harm is done; for given the apprehension of a subject of attributes and of its contrary, the presentation of difference in their modes is possible.

units.sanskrit: न च परस्पराश्रयप्रसङ्गः। पराननपेक्ष्य प्रभेदशालिनो वस्तुनो ग्रहणे सति धर्मभेदभानसंभवात्। न च धर्मभेदवादे तस्य तस्य भेदस्य भेदान्तरभेद्यत्वेनानवस्था दुरवस्था स्यादित्यास्थेयम्।
units.english: Nor let it be supposed that on the hypothesis of difference in the modes of things, as each difference must be different from some ulterior difference, there will result an embarrassing progression to infinity, there being no occasion for the occurrence of the said ulterior difference, inasmuch as we do not observe that men think and say that two things are different as differenced from the different.

units.sanskrit: भेदभेदिनौ भिन्नाविति व्यवहारादर्शनात्। न चैकभेदबलेनान्यभेदानुमानम्। दृष्टान्तभेदाविघातेनोत्थाने दोषाभावात्।
units.english: Nor can an ulterior difference be inferred from the first difference, for there being no difference to serve as the example in such inference, there cannot but be a non-occurrence of inference.

units.sanskrit: सोऽयं पिण्याकयाचनार्थं गतस्य खारिकातैलदातृत्वाभ्युपगम इव।
units.english: And thus it must be allowed that in raising the objection you have begged for a little oil-cake, and have had to give us gallons of oil.

units.sanskrit: दृष्टान्तभेदविमर्दे त्वनुत्थानमेव।
units.english: If there be no difference for the example the inference cannot emerge.

units.sanskrit: न हि वरविघाताय कन्योद्वाहः।
units.english: The bride is not married for the destruction of the bridegroom.

units.sanskrit: तस्मान्मूलक्षयाभावादनवस्था न दोषाय।
units.english: There being, then, no fundamental difficulty, this infinite progression presents no trouble.

units.sanskrit: अनुमानेनापि भेदोऽवसीयते।
units.english: Difference (duality) is also ascertained by inference.

units.sanskrit: परमेश्वरो जीवाद् भिन्नः। तं प्रति सेव्यत्वात्। यो यं प्रति सेव्यः स तस्माद् भिन्नः। यथा भृत्याद्राजा।
units.english: Thus the Supreme Lord differs from the individual soul as the object of its obedience; and he who is to be obeyed by any person differs from that person, a king, for instance, from his attendant.

units.sanskrit: न हि सुखं मे स्याद् दुःखं मे न मनागपिइति पुरुषार्थमर्थयमानाः पुरुषाः स्थपतिपदं कामयमानाः सत्कारभाजो भवेयुः। प्रत्युत सर्वानर्थभाजनं भवन्ति।
units.english: For men, desiring as they do the end of man, Let me have pleasure, let me not have the slightest pain, if they covet the position of their lord, do not become objects of his favour, nay, rather, they become recipients of all kinds of evil.

units.sanskrit: यः स्वस्यात्मनो हीनत्वं परस्य गुणोत्कर्षं च कययति स स्तुत्यः प्रीतः स्तावकस्य तस्याभीष्टं प्रयच्छति।
units.english: He who asserts his own inferiority and the excellence of his superior, he it is who is to be commended; and the gratified superior grants his eulogist his desire.

units.sanskrit: तदाह - घातयन्ति हि राजानो राजाहमिति वादिनः।
units.english: Therefore it has been said:— "Kings destroy those who assert themselves to be kings,

units.sanskrit: ददत्यखिलमिष्टं च स्वगुणोत्कर्षवादिनाम्॥
units.english: "And grant to those who proclaim their kingly pre-eminence all that they desire."

units.sanskrit: एवं च परमेश्वराभेदतृष्णया विष्णोर्गुणोत्कर्षस्य मृगतृष्णिकासमत्वाभिधानं विपुलकदलीफललिप्सया जिह्वाच्छे दनमनुहरति। एतादृशविष्णुविद्वेषणादन्धतमसप्रवेशप्रसङ्गात्।
units.english: Thus the statement of those (Advaita-vādins) in their thirst to be one with the Supreme Lord, that the supreme excellence of Viṣṇu is like a mirage, is as if they were to cut off their tongues in trying to get a fine plantain, since it results that through offending this supreme Viṣṇu they must enter into the hell of blind darkness (andha-tamasa).

units.sanskrit: तदेतत्प्रतिपादितं मध्यमन्दिरेण महाभारततात्पर्यनिर्णयेअनादिद्वेषिणो दैत्या विष्णौ द्वेषो विवर्धितः।
units.english: The same thing is laid down by Madhya-mandira in the Mahābhārata-tātparya-nirṇaya:— "O Daityas, enemies of the eternal, Viṣṇu's anger is waxed great;

units.sanskrit: तमस्यन्धे पातयति दैत्यानन्ते विनिश्चयात्॥ (म.भा.ता.१/१११) इति।
units.english: "He hurls the Daityas into the blind darkness, because they decide blindly."

units.sanskrit: सा च सेवा अङ्कननामकरणभजनभेदात् त्रिविधा।
units.english: This service (or obedience of which we have spoken) is trichotomised into (1.) stigmatisation, (2.) imposition of names, (3.) worship.

units.sanskrit: तत्राङ्कनं नारायणायुधादीनां तद्रपस्मरणार्थमपेक्षितार्थसिद्धूयर्थं च।
units.english: Of these, (1.) stigmatisation is (the branding upon oneself) of the weapons of Nārāyaṇa (or Viṣṇu) as a memorial of him, and as a means of attaining the end which is needful (emancipation).

units.sanskrit: तथा च शाकल्यसंहितापरिशिष्टम् - चक्रं बिभर्त्ति पुरुषोऽभितप्तं बलं देवानाममृतस्य विष्णोः।
units.english: Thus the sequel of the Sākalya-samhitā:— "The man who bears branded in him the discus of the immortal Viṣṇu, which is the might of the gods,

units.sanskrit: स याति नाकं दुरिताबधूय विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः।
units.english: "He, shaking off his guilt, goes to the heaven (Vaikuṇṭha) which ascetics, whose desires are passed away, enter into:

units.sanskrit: देवासो येन विधृतेन बाहुना सुदर्शनेन प्रयातास्तमायन्।
units.english: "The discus Sudarśana by which, uplifted in his arm, the gods entered that heaven;

units.sanskrit: येनाङ्किता मनवो लोकसृष्टिं वितन्वन्ति ब्राह्मणास्तद्वहन्ति॥
units.english: "Marked wherewith the Manus projected the emanation of the world, that weapon Brāhmans wear (stamped upon them);

units.sanskrit: तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं येन गच्छन्ति लाञ्छिताः।
units.english: "Stigmatised wherewith they go to the supreme sphere of Viṣṇu;

units.sanskrit: उरुक्रमस्य चिह्नैरङ्किता लोके सुभगा भवामः॥इति।
units.english: "Marked with the stigmas of the wide-striding (Viṣṇu), let us become beatified."

units.sanskrit: ऽअतप्ततनूर्न तदामो अश्नुते श्रितास इद्वहन्तस्तत्समासत' (तै.आ.१/११) इति तैत्तिरीयकोपनिषच्च। स्थानविशेषश्चाग्नेयपुराणे प्रदर्शितः - दक्षिणे तु करे विप्रो बिभृयाच्च सुदर्शनम्। सव्येन शङ्खं बिभृयादिति ब्रह्मविदो विदुः ॥
units.english: Again, the Taittirīyaka Upaniṣad says: "He whose body is not branded, is raw, and tastes it not: votaries bearing it attain thereto." The particular parts to be branded are specified in the Āgneya-purāṇa:— "On his right hand let the Brāhman wear Sudarśana, "On his left the conch-shell: thus have those who know the Veda declared."

units.sanskrit: अन्यत्र चक्रधारणे मन्त्रविशेषश्च दर्शितः - सुदर्शन महाज्वाल कोटिसूर्यसमप्रभः ! अज्ञानान्धस्य मे नित्यं विष्णोमार्गं प्रदर्शय॥
units.english: In another passage is given the invocation to be recited on being branded with the discus:— "Sudarśana, brightly blazing, effulgent as ten million suns, "Show unto me, blind with ignorance, the everlasting way of Viṣṇu.

units.sanskrit: त्वं पुरा सागरोत्पन्नो विष्णुना विधृतः करे।
units.english: "Thou aforetime sprangest from the sea, brandished in the hand of Viṣṇu,

units.sanskrit: नमितः सर्वदेवैश्च पाञ्चजन्य नमोऽस्तु ते॥
units.english: "Adored by all the gods; O Pāṅcajanya, to thee be adoration."

units.sanskrit: नामकरणं पुत्रादीनां के शवादिनाम्ना व्यवहारः, सर्वदा तन्नामानुस्मरणार्थम्।
units.english: (2.) Imposition of names is the appellation of sons and others by such names as Keśava, as a continual memorial of the name of the Supreme Lord.

units.sanskrit: भजनं दशविधंवाचा सत्यं हितं प्रियं स्वाध्यायः, कायेन दानं परित्राणं परिरक्षणं, मनसा दया स्पृहा श्रद्धा चेति।
units.english: (3.) Worship is of ten kinds, viz., with the voice, (1.) veracity, (2.) usefulness, (3.) kindliness, (4.) sacred study; with the body, (5.) alms-giving, (6.) defence, (7.) protection; with the common sensory, (8.) mercy, (9.) longing, and (10.) faith.

units.sanskrit: अत्रैकै कं निष्पाद्य नारायणे समर्पणं भजनम्।
units.english: Worship is the dedication to Nārāyaṇa of each of these as it is realised.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तम्।
units.english: Thus it has been said:—

units.sanskrit: अङ्कनं नामकरणं भजनं दशधा च तत्।
units.english: "Stigmatisation, imposition of names, worship; the last is of ten kinds."

units.sanskrit: एवं ज्ञेयत्वादिनापि भेदोऽनुमातव्यः। तथा श्रुत्यापि भेदोऽवगन्तव्यः।
units.english: Difference (or duality between the Supreme Being and the universe) may also be inferred from cognisability and other marks.

units.sanskrit: ऽसत्यमेनमनु विश्वे मदन्ति, रातिं देवस्य गृह्णतो मघोनः।ऽ सत्यः सो अस्य महिमा गृणे शवो, यज्ञेषु विप्रराज्ये।ऽ ऽसत्य आत्मा, सत्यो जीवः, सत्यं भिदा सत्यं भिदा सत्यं भिदा, मैवारुवण्यो मैवारुवण्य मैवारुवण्य' इति मोक्षानन्दभेदप्रतिपादक श्रुतिभ्यः।
units.english: So also difference (or duality) may be understood from revelation, from texts setting out duality in emancipation and beatitude, such as: "All rejoice over truth attained; truthful, and celebrating the gift of the divine Indra, they recount his glory;" "Sarva, among those that know the truth, O Brāhman, is in the universe, true spirit; true is individual spirit; truth is duality, truth is duality, in me is illusion, in me illusion, in me illusion."

units.sanskrit: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः।
units.english: "After attaining this knowledge, becoming like unto me,

units.sanskrit: सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च॥
units.english: "In creation they are not born again, in retractation they perish not" (Bhagavad-gītā, xiv.

units.sanskrit: (गी.१४/२) ऽजगद्व्यापारवर्जम्ऽ ऽ प्रकरणादसंनिहितत्वाच्च' (ब्र.सू.४/४/१७-१८) इत्यादिभ्यश्च।
units.english: According also to such aphorisms as, "Excepting cosmical operation because of occasion, and because of non-proximity."

units.sanskrit: न च ऽब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवतिऽ (मु.३/२/९) इति श्रुतिबलाज्जीवस्य पारमैश्वर्यं शक्यशङ्कम्। ऽसंपूज्य ब्राह्मणं भकत्या शूद्रोऽपि ब्राह्मणो भवेत्ऽ- इतिवद् वृंहितो भवतीत्यर्थपरत्वात्।
units.english: Nor should suggestion be made that individual spirit is God in virtue of the text, He that knows the absolute becomes the absolute; for this text is hyperbolically eulogistic, like the text, Worshipping a Brāhman devoutly a Śūdra becomes a Brāhman, i.e., becomes exalted.

units.sanskrit: ननुप्रपञ्चो यदि विद्येत निवर्तेत न संशयः।
units.english: "If the universe existed it would doubtless come to an end,"

units.sanskrit: मायामात्रमिदं द्वैतमद्वैतं परमार्थतः॥ (माण्डू क्यकारिका १/१७) इति वचनाद् द्वैतस्य कल्पितत्वमवगम्यत इति चेत्सत्यम्। भावमनभिसंघायाभिधानात्। तथा हियद्ययमुत्पद्येत तर्हि निवर्तेत न संशयः। तस्मादनादिरेवायं प्रकृष्टः पञ्चविधो भेदप्रपञ्चः।
units.english: this duality is merely illusory, and in reality a unity, and that duality is learnt to be illusorily imagined; it may be replied: What you say is true, but you do not understand its meaning; for the real meaning is, If this world had been produced, it would, without doubt, come to an end; therefore this universe is from everlasting, a fivefold dual universe; and it is not non-existent, because it is mere illusion.

units.sanskrit: मायामात्रत्वात्। मायेति भगवदिच्छोच्यते।
units.english: Illusion is defined to be the will of the Lord, in virtue of the testimony of many such passages as:—

units.sanskrit: महामायेत्यविद्येति नियतिर्मोंहिनीति च।
units.english: "The great illusion, ignorance, necessity, the bewilderment,

units.sanskrit: प्रकृतिर्वासनेत्येव तवेच्छानन्त कथ्यते॥
units.english: "The originant, ideation,—thus is thy will called, O Infinite.

units.sanskrit: प्रकृतिः प्रकृष्टकरणाद्वासना वासयेद्यतः।
units.english: "The originant, because it originates greatly; ideation, because it produces ideas;

units.sanskrit: अ इत्युक्तो हरिस्तस्य मायाविद्येति संज्ञिना॥
units.english: "The illusion of Hari, who is called a, is termed (avidyā) ignorance:

units.sanskrit: मायेत्युक्ता प्रकृष्टत्वात्प्रकृष्टे हि मयाभिधा।
units.english: "Styled (māyā) illusion, because it is pre-eminent, for the name māyā is used of the pre-eminent;

units.sanskrit: विष्णोः प्रज्ञप्तिरेवैका शब्देरेतैरुदीर्यते॥
units.english: "The excellent knowledge of Viṣṇu is called, though one only, by these names;

units.sanskrit: प्रज्ञाप्तिरूपो हि हरिः सा च स्वानन्दलक्षणा।
units.english: "For Hari is excellent knowledge, and this is characterised by spontaneous beatitude."

units.sanskrit: सैव प्रज्ञा मानत्राणकर्त्री च यस्य तन्मायामात्रम्। ततश्च परमेश्वरेण ज्ञानत्वाद्रक्षितत्वाच्च न द्वैतं भ्रान्तिकल्पितम्।
units.english: That in which this excellent knowledge produces knowledge and effects sustentation thereof, that is pure illusion, as known and sustained, therefore by the Supreme Lord duality is not illusorily imagined.

units.sanskrit: न हीश्वरे सर्वस्य भ्रान्तिः संभवति। विशेषदर्शननिबन्धनत्वाद् भ्रान्तेः।
units.english: For in the Lord illusory imagination of the universe is not possible, illusory imagination arising from non-perception of differences (which as an imperfection is inconsistent with the divine nature).

units.sanskrit: तर्हि तद्व्यपदेशः कथमित्यत्रोत्तरमद्वैतं परमार्थत इति। परमार्थत इति परमार्थापेक्षया। तेन सर्वस्मादुत्तमस्य विष्णुतत्त्वस्य समभ्यधिकशून्यत्वमुक्तं भवति।
units.english: If it be asked how then that (illusory duality) is predicated, the answer is that in reality there is a non-duality, that is in reality, Viṣṇu being better than all else, has no equal and no superior.

units.sanskrit: तथा च परमा श्रुतिः - जीवेश्वरभिदा चैव जडेश्वरभिदा तथा।
units.english: Accordingly, the grand revelation:— "A difference between soul and the Lord, a difference between the unsentient and the Lord,

units.sanskrit: जीवभेदो मिथश्चैव जडजीवभिदा तथा॥ मिथश्च जडभेदो यः प्रपञ्चो भेदपञ्चकः।
units.english: "A difference among souls, and a difference of the unsentient and the soul each from the other. "Also the difference of unsentient things from one another, the world with its five divisions.

units.sanskrit: सोऽयं सत्योऽप्यनादिश्च सादिश्चेन्नाशमाप्नुयात्॥
units.english: "This same is real and from all eternity; if it had had a beginning it would have an end:

units.sanskrit: न च नाशं प्रयात्येष न चासौ भ्रान्तिकल्पितः।
units.english: "Whereas it does not come to an end; and it is not illusorily imagined:

units.sanskrit: कल्पितश्चेन्निवर्तेत न चासौ विनिवर्तते॥
units.english: "For if it were imagined it would cease, but it never ceases.

units.sanskrit: द्वैतं न विद्यत इति तस्मादज्ञानिनां मतम्।
units.english: "That there is no duality is therefore the doctrine of those that lack knowledge;

units.sanskrit: मतं हि ज्ञानिनामेतन्मितं त्रातं हि विष्णुना॥
units.english: "For this the doctrine of those that have knowledge is known and sustained by Viṣṇu."

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्विष्णोः सर्वोंत्कर्ष एव तात्पर्यं सर्वागमानाम्।
units.english: The purpose, then, of all revelations is to set out the supreme excellence of Viṣṇu.

units.sanskrit: एतदेवाभिसंघायाभिहितं भगवता - द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च।
units.english: With this in view the Lord declared:— "Two are these persons in the universe, the perishable and the imperishable;

units.sanskrit: क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कू टस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते॥
units.english: "The perishable is all the elements, the imperishable is the unmodified.

units.sanskrit: उत्तम पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः।
units.english: "The other, the most excellent person, called the Supreme Spirit,

units.sanskrit: यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य विभर्त्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः॥
units.english: "Is the undecaying Lord, who pervading sustains the three worlds.

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः।
units.english: "Since transcending the perishable, I am more excellent than the imperishable (soul),

units.sanskrit: अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः।
units.english: "Hence I am celebrated among men and in the Veda as the best of persons (Puruṣottama);

units.sanskrit: यो मामेवमसंमूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम्। स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत॥
units.english: "He who uninfatuated knows me thus the best of persons, he all-knowing worships me in every wise.

units.sanskrit: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ।
units.english: "Thus this most mysterious institute is declared, blameless (Arjuna):

units.sanskrit: एतद् बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत॥
units.english: "Knowing this a man may be wise, and may have done what he has to do, O Bhārata" (Bhagavad-gītā, xv.
So in the Mahā-varāha—

units.sanskrit: महावराहेऽपि - मुख्यं च सर्ववेदानां तात्पर्यं नीपतौ परे।
units.english: "The primary purport of all the Vedas relates to the supreme spouse of Śrī;

units.sanskrit: उत्कर्षे तु तदन्यत्र तात्पर्यं स्यादवान्तरम॥इति।
units.english: "Its purport regarding the excellence of any other deity must be subordinate."

units.sanskrit: युक्तं च विष्णोः सर्वोंत्कर्षे महातात्पर्यम्।
units.english: It is reasonable that the primary purport should regard the supreme excellence of Viṣṇu.

units.sanskrit: मोक्षो हि सर्वपुरुषार्थोंत्तमः। धर्मार्थकामाः सर्वेऽपि न नित्या मोक्ष एव हि। नित्यस्तस्मात्तदर्थाय यतेत मतिमान्नरः। इति भाल्लवेयश्रुतेः।
units.english: For emancipation is the highest end of all men, according to the text of the Bhāllaveya Upaniṣad: While merit, wealth, and enjoyment are transitory, emancipation is eternal; therefore a wise man should strive unceasingly to attain thereto.

units.sanskrit: मोक्षश्च विष्णुप्रसादमन्तरेण न लभ्यते। यस्य प्रसादात्परर्मात्तिरूपादस्मात्संसारन्मुच्यते नापरेण। नारायणोऽसौ परमो विचिन्त्यो मुमुक्षुभिः कर्मपाशादमुष्मात्॥ इति नारायणश्रुतेः।
units.english: And emancipation is not won without the grace of Viṣṇu, according to the text of the Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad: Through whose grace is the highest state, through whose essence he is liberated from transmigration, while inferior men propitiating the divinities are not emancipated; the supreme object of discernment to those who desire to be liberated from this snare of works. According also to the words of the Viṣṇu-purāṇa—

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्प्रसन्ने किमिहास्त्यलभ्यं धर्मार्थकामैरलमल्पकास्ते।
units.english: "If he be propitiated, what may not here be won? Enough of all wealth and enjoyments.

units.sanskrit: समाश्रिताद् ब्रह्मतरोरनन्तात् निःसंशयं युक्तिफलं प्रयान्ति॥
units.english: On climbing the tree of the supreme essence, without doubt a man attains to the fruit of emancipation."

units.sanskrit: (वि.पु.१/१७/६१) इति विष्णुपुराणोक्ते श्च। प्रसादश्च गुणोत्कर्षज्ञानादेव नाभेदज्ञानादित्युक्तम्।
units.english: And it is declared that the grace of Viṣṇu is won only through the knowledge of his excellence, not through the knowledge of non-duality.

units.sanskrit: न च तत्त्वमस्यादितादात्म्यव्याकोपः। श्रुतितात्पर्यापरिज्ञानविजृम्भणात्।
units.english: Nor is there in this doctrine any confliction with texts declaratory of the identity (of personal and impersonal spirit) such as, That art thou (for this pretended identity) is mere babbling from ignorance of the real purport.

units.sanskrit: आह नित्यपरोक्षं तु त्वच्छब्दो ह्यविशेषतः।
units.english: "The word That, when undetermined, designates the eternally unknown,

units.sanskrit: त्वंशब्दश्चापरोक्षार्थं तयोरैक्यं कथं भवेत्॥
units.english: "The word Thou designates a knowable entity; how can these be one?"

units.sanskrit: आदित्यो यूप इतिवत्सादृश्यार्था तु सा श्रुतिः।
units.english: And this text (That art thou) indicates similarity (not identity) like the text, The sun is the sacrificial post.

units.sanskrit: तथा च परमा श्रुतिः - जीवस्य परमैक्यं तु बुद्धिसारुप्यमेव तु।
units.english: Thus the grand revelation:— "The ultimate unity of the individual soul is either similarity of cognition,

units.sanskrit: एकस्थाननिवेशो वा व्यक्तिस्थानमपेक्ष्य सः॥
units.english: "Or entrance into the same place, or in relation to the place of the individual;

units.sanskrit: न स्वरूपैकता तस्य युक्तस्यापि विरुपतः।
units.english: "Not essential unity, for even when it is emancipated it is different,

units.sanskrit: स्वातन्त्र्यपूर्णतेऽल्पत्वपारतन्त्र्ये विरुपते॥
units.english: "The difference being independence and completeness (in the Supreme Spirit), and smallness and dependence (in the individual spirit)."

units.sanskrit: अथवा तत्त्वमसीत्यत्र स एवात्मा स्वातन्त्र्यादिगुणोपेतत्वात्। अतत्त्वमसि त्वं तत्र भवसि तद्रहितत्वादित्येकत्वमतिशयेन निराकृतम्।
