units.english: Or to propose another explanation of the text, Ātmā tat tvam asi, That art thou, it may be divided, ātmā tat tvam asi. He alone is soul as possessing independence and other attributes, and thou art not-that (atat) as wanting those attributes; and thus the doctrine of unity is utterly expelled.

units.sanskrit: तदाहअतत्वमिति वा छे दस्तेनैक्यं सुनिराकृतम्।
units.english: "Or the division may be Atat tvam, and thus unity will be well got rid of."

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् दृष्टान्तनवकेऽपि, स यथा शकु निः सूत्रेण प्रबद्धः' )छा.६/८/३) इयादिना भेद एव दृष्टान्ताभिघानान्नायमभेदोपदेश इति तत्त्ववादरहस्यम्।
units.english: According, therefore, to the Tattva-vāda-rahasya, the words in the nine examples (in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad), He like a bird tied with a string, &c., teach unity with the view of giving an example of non-duality.

units.sanskrit: तथा च महोपनिषद्यथा पक्षी च सूत्रं च नानावृक्षरसा यथा।
units.english: Accordingly the Mahopaniṣad:— "Like a bird and the string; like the juices of various trees;

units.sanskrit: यथा नद्यः समुद्राश्च यथा जीवमहीरुहौ॥
units.english: "Like rivers and the sea; like fresh and salt water;

units.sanskrit: चोरापहार्यौ च यथा यथा पुंविषयावपि॥
units.english: "Like a robber and the robbed; like a man and his energy;

units.sanskrit: तथा जीवेश्वरौ भिन्नौ सर्वदैव विलक्षणौ॥ तथापि सूक्ष्मरूपत्वान्न जीवात्परमो हरिः।
units.english: "So are soul and the Lord diverse, for ever different. "Nevertheless from subtilty (or imperceptibility) of form, the supreme Hari

units.sanskrit: भेदेन मन्ददृष्टीनां दृश्यते प्रेरकोऽपि सन्॥
units.english: "Is not seen by the dim-sighted to be other than the individual spirit, though he is its actuator;

units.sanskrit: वैलक्षण्यं तयोज्ञात्वा मुच्यते बध्यतेऽन्यथा।इति।
units.english: "On knowing their diversity a man is emancipated: otherwise he is bound."

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मा शिवः सुराद्याश्च शरीरक्षरणत्क्षराः।
units.english: "Brahmā, Śiva, and the greatest of the gods decay with the decay of their bodies;

units.sanskrit: लक्ष्मीरक्षरदेहत्वादक्षरा तत्परो हरिः॥
units.english: "Greater than these is Hari, undecaying, because his body is for the sustentation of Lakṣmī.

units.sanskrit: स्वातन्त्र्यशक्तिविज्ञानसुखाद्यैरखिलैर्गुणैः।
units.english: "By reason of all his attributes, independence, power, knowledge, pleasure, and the rest,

units.sanskrit: निःसीमत्वेन ते सर्वे तद्वशाः सर्वदैव च॥
units.english: "All they, all the deities, are in unlimited obedience to him."

units.sanskrit: विष्णुं सर्वगुणैः पूर्णं ज्ञात्वा संसारवर्जितः।
units.english: "Knowing Viṣṇu, full of all excellences, the soul, exempted from transmigration,

units.sanskrit: निर्दुःखानन्दभुङ् नित्यं तत्समीपे स मोदते॥
units.english: "Rejoices in his presence for ever, enjoying painless bliss.

units.sanskrit: मुक्तानां चाश्रयो विष्णुरधिकोऽधिपतिस्तथा।
units.english: "Viṣṇu is the refuge of liberated souls, and their supreme ruler.

units.sanskrit: तद्वशा एव ते सर्वे सर्वदैव स ईश्वरः॥ इति च।
units.english: "Obedient to him are they for ever; he is the Lord."

units.sanskrit: एकविज्ञानेन सर्वविज्ञानं च प्रधानत्वकारणत्वादिना युज्यते न तु सर्व मिथ्यात्वेन।
units.english: That by knowledge of one thing there is knowledge of all things may be evinced from its supremacy and causality, not from the falsity of all things.

units.sanskrit: न हि सत्यज्ञानेन मिथ्याज्ञानं संभवति।
units.english: For knowledge of the false cannot be brought about by knowledge of real existence.

units.sanskrit: यथा प्रधानपुरुषाणां ज्ञानाज्ञानाभ्यां ग्रामो ज्ञातोऽज्ञात इत्येवमादिव्यपदेशो दृष्ट एव। यथा च कारणे पितरि ज्ञाते जानात्यस्य पुत्रमिति। यथा वा सादृश्यादेकस्त्रीज्ञानाद् अन्यस्त्रीज्ञानमिति।
units.english: As we see the current assurance and expression that by knowing or not knowing its chief men a village is known or not known; and as when the father the cause is known, a man knows the son; (so by knowing the supreme and the cause, the inferior and the effect is known).

units.sanskrit: अन्यथा ऽसोम्यैके न मृत्पिण्डेन सर्वं मृन्मयं विज्ञातम्ऽ इत्यत्र एकपिण्डशब्दौ वृथा प्रसज्येयाताम्। मृदा विज्ञातया' इत्येतावतैव वाक्यस्य पूर्णत्वात्।
units.english: Otherwise (on the doctrine of the Advaita-vādins that the world is false and illusory) the words one and lump in the text, By one lump of clay, fair sir, all that is made of clay is recognised, would be used to no purpose, for the text must be completed by supplying the words, By reason of clay recognised.

units.sanskrit: न च ऽवाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं मृत्तिके त्येव सत्यम्ऽ (छा.६/१/५) इत्येतत्कार्यस्य मिथ्यात्वमाचष्टं इत्येष्टव्यम्। वाचारम्भणं विकारो यस्य तदविकृतं नित्यं नामधेयं मृत्तिके त्यादिकमित्येतद्वचनं सत्यमित्यर्थस्य स्वीकारात्।
units.english: For the text, Utterance with the voice, modification, name, clay (or other determinate object),—these alone are real, cannot be assumed to impart the falsity of things made; the reality of these being admitted, for what is meant is, that of which utterance with the voice is a modification, is unmodified, eternal; and a name such as clay, such speech is true.

units.sanskrit: अपरथा नामधेयमितिशब्दयोर्वैयर्थ्य प्रसज्येत।
units.english: Otherwise it would result that the words name and alone would be otiose.

units.sanskrit: अतो न कु त्रापि जगतो मिथ्यात्वसिद्धिः।
units.english: There is no proof anywhere, then, that the world is unreal.

units.sanskrit: किं च प्रपञ्चो मिथ्येत्यत्र मिथ्यात्वं तथ्यमतथ्यं वा प्रथमे सत्याद्वैतभङ्ग प्रसङ्गः।
units.english: Besides (we would ask) is the statement that the world is false itself true or false. If the statement is true, there is a violation of a real non-duality.

units.sanskrit: चरमे प्रपञ्चसत्यत्वापातः।
units.english: If the statement is untrue, it follows that the world is true.

units.sanskrit: नन्वनित्यंत्वं नित्यमनित्यं वा। उभयथाप्यनुपपत्तिरित्याक्षेपवदयमपि नित्यसम जातिभेदः स्यात्।
units.english: Perhaps it may be objected that this dilemma is a kind of fallacious reasoning, like the dilemma: Is transitoriness permanent or transitory? There is a difficulty in either case.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं न्यायनिर्माणवेधसानित्यमनित्यभावादनित्ये नित्यत्वोपपत्तेर्नित्यसमः' (न्या०सू०५/३/३५) इति।
units.english: As it is said by the author of the Nyāya-nirvāṇa: The proof of the permanence of the transitory, as being both permanent and transitory, is a paralogism.

units.sanskrit: तार्कि करक्षायां च - धर्मस्य तदूतद्रपविकल्पानुपपत्तितः।
units.english: And in the Tārkika-rakṣā— "When a mode cannot be evinced to be either such and such, or not such and such,

units.sanskrit: धर्मिणस्तद्विशिष्टत्वभङ्गो नित्यसमो भवेत॥इति।
units.english: "The denial of a subject characterised by such a mode is called Nitya-sama."

units.sanskrit: अस्याः संज्ञाया उपलक्षणत्वमभिप्रेत्याभिहितं प्रवोधसिद्धावन्वर्थित्वात्तूपरञ्जकधर्मसमेति।
units.english: With the implied mention of this same technical expression it is stated in the Prabodha-siddhi: Equality of characteristic modes results from significancy.

units.sanskrit: तस्मादसदुत्तरमिति चेत् - अशिक्षितत्रासनमेतत्। दुष्टत्वमूलानिरूपणात्।
units.english: If it be said, This then is a valid rejoinder, we reply, This is a mere scaring of the uninstructed, for the source of fallacy has not been pointed out.

units.sanskrit: तद् द्विविधं साधारणमसाधारणं च। तत्राद्यं स्वव्याघातकम्। द्वितीयं त्रिबिधं युक्ताङ्गहीनत्वमयुक्ताङ्गाधिकत्वमविषयवृत्तित्वं चेति।
units.english: This is twofold, general and particular: of these, the former is self-destructive, and the latter is of three kinds, defect of a requisite element, excess of an element not requisite, and residence in that which is not the subjicible subject.

units.sanskrit: तत्र साधारणमसंभवितमेव। उक्तस्याक्षेपस्य स्वात्मव्यापनानुलम्भात्। एवमसाधारणमपि। घटस्य नास्तितायां नास्तितोक्तौ अस्तित्ववत्प्रकृतेऽप्युपपत्तेः।
units.english: Of these (two forms of the fallacy), the general form is not suspected, no self-pervasion being observed in the dilemma in question (viz., Is the statement that the world is unreal itself true or false? &c.) So likewise the particular; for if a water-jar be said to be non-existent, the affirmation of its non-existence is equally applicable to the water-jar as that of its existence.

units.sanskrit: ननु प्रपञ्चस्य मिथ्यात्वमभ्युपेयते नासत्त्वमिति चेत्, तदेतत्सोऽयं शिरश्छे देऽपि शतं न ददाति, विंशतिपञ्चकं तु प्रयच्छतीति शाकटिकवृत्तान्तमनुहरेत्। मिथ्यात्वासत्त्वयोः पर्यायत्वादित्यलमतिप्रपञ्चेन।
units.english: If you reply: We accept the unreality (or falsity) of the world, not its non-existence; this reply is about as wise as the procedure of the carter who will lose his head rather than pay a hundred pieces of money, but will at once give five score; for falsity and non-existence are synonymous. We dismiss further prolixity.

units.sanskrit: तत्र ऽअथातो ब्रह्मजिज्ञासा' (ब्र०सू०१/१/१) इति प्रथमसूत्रस्यायमर्थः। तत्राथशब्दो मङ्गलार्थों'धिकारानन्तर्यार्थश्च स्वीक्रियते।
units.english: The meaning of the first aphorism, viz., Then hence the absolute is to be desired to be known, is as follows:—The word then is allowed to purport auspiciousness, and to designate subsequency to the qualification (of the aspirant).

units.sanskrit: अतःशब्दो हेत्वर्थः।
units.english: The word hence indicates a reason.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं गारुडेअथातःशब्दपूर्वाणि सूत्राणि निखिलान्यपि।
units.english: Accordingly it is stated in the Gāruḍa-purāṇa:—

units.sanskrit: प्रारभ्यन्ते नियत्यैव तत्किमत्र नियामकम्॥ कश्चार्थस्तु तयोर्विद्वन्कथमुत्तमता तयोः।
units.english: "All the aphorisms begin with the words Then and Hence regularly; what then is the reason of this? "And what is the sense of those words, O sage? Why are those the most excellent?

units.sanskrit: एतदाख्याहि मे ब्रह्मन्यथा ज्ञास्यामि तत्त्वतः॥
units.english: "Tell me this, Brahmā, that I may know it truly."

units.sanskrit: एवमुक्तो नारदेन ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच सत्तमः।
units.english: Thus addressed by Nārada, the most excellent Brahmā replied:—

units.sanskrit: आनन्तर्याधिकारे च मङ्गलार्थे तथैव च॥
units.english: "The word Then is used of subsequency and of competency, and in an auspicious sense,

units.sanskrit: अथशब्दस्त्वतःशब्दो हेत्वर्थे समुदीरितः।
units.english: "And the word Thence is employed to indicate the reason."

units.sanskrit: यतो नारायणप्रसादमन्तरेण न मोक्षो लभ्यते प्रसादश्च ज्ञानमन्तरेण, अतो ब्रह्मजिज्ञासा कर्तव्येति सिद्धम्।
units.english: It is laid down that we must institute inquiries about the absolute, because emancipation is not attained without the grace of Nārāyana, and his grace is not attained without knowledge.

units.sanskrit: जिज्ञास्यब्रह्मणो लक्षणमुक्तं ऽजन्माद्यस्य यतः' (ब्र.सू.१.१.२) इति। सृष्टिस्थित्यादि यतो भवति तद् ब्रह्मेति वाक्यार्थः। तथा च स्कान्दं वचः - उत्पत्तिस्थितिसंहारा नियतिर्ज्ञानमावृतिः।
units.english: The absolute, about which the inquiry is to be instituted, is described in the words (of the second aphorism): From which the genesis, and so forth, of this. The meaning of the sentence is that the absolute is that from which result emanation, sustentation, and retractation; according to the words of the Skanda-purāṇa—

units.sanskrit: वन्धमोक्षौ च पुरुषाद्यस्मात्स हरिरेकराट्॥
units.english: "He is Hari the sole ruler, the spirit from whom are emanation, sustentation, retractation, necessity, knowledge, involution (in illusion), and bondage and liberation;"

units.sanskrit: यतो वा इमानीत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यश्च।
units.english: and according to such Vedic texts, From which are these.

units.sanskrit: तत्र प्रमाणमप्युक्तं ऽशास्त्रयोनित्वात्ऽ (ब्र०सू०१/१/३) इति।
units.english: The evidence adducible for this is described (in the third aphorism): Because it has its source from the system.

units.sanskrit: ऽनावेदविन्मनुते तं बृहन्तम्ऽ (तै०ब्रा० ३/१२/९/७) ऽतं त्वौपनिषदम्ऽ (बृ० ३/९/२६) इत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यस्तस्यानुमानिकत्वं निराक्रियते।
units.english: That the absolute should be reached by way of inference is rejected by such texts as, He that knows not the Veda cogitates not that mighty one; Him described in the Upaniṣads.

units.sanskrit: च चानुमानस्य स्वातन्त्र्येण प्रामाण्यमस्ति। तदुक्तं कौर्मे - श्रुतिसाहाय्यरहितमनुमानं न कु त्रचित्।
units.english: Inference, moreover, is not by itself authoritative, as is said in the Kaurma-purāṇa— "Inference, unaccompanied by revelation, in no case

units.sanskrit: निश्चयात्साधयेदर्थं प्रमाणान्तरमेव च॥
units.english: "Can definitely prove a matter, nor can any other form of evidence;

units.sanskrit: श्रुतिस्मृतिसहायं यत्प्रमाणन्तरमुत्तमम्।
units.english: "Whatsoever other form of evidence, companioned by revelation and tradition,

units.sanskrit: प्रमाणपदवीं गच्छेन्नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥
units.english: "Acquires the rank of probation, about this there can be no hesitation."

units.sanskrit: शास्त्रस्वरुपमुक्तं स्कान्दे - ऋग्यजुःसामाथर्वा च भारतं पाञ्चरात्रकम्। मूलरामायणं चैव शास्त्रमित्यभिधीयते॥
units.english: What a Śāstra (or system of sacred institutes) is, has been stated in the Skanda-purāṇa:— "The Rig-veda, the Yajur-veda, the Sāma-veda, the Atharva-veda, the Mahābhārata, the Pañca-rātra, and the original Rāmāyaṇa, are called Śāstras.

units.sanskrit: यच्चानुकू लमेतस्य तच्च शास्त्रं प्रकीर्तितम्।
units.english: "That also which is conformable to these is called Śāstra.

units.sanskrit: अतोऽन्यो ग्रन्थविस्तारो नैव शास्त्रं कु वर्त्म तत॥इति। तदनेन, ऽअनन्यलभ्यः शास्त्रार्थः' इति न्यायेन भेदस्य प्राप्तत्वेन तत्र न तात्पर्यं किन्तु अद्वैत एव वेदवाक्यानां तात्पर्यम् इत्यद्वैतवादिनां प्रत्याशा प्रतिक्षिप्ता। अनुमानादीश्वरस्य सिद्धयभावेन तद्भेदस्यापि ततः सिद्धयभावात्।
units.english: According, then, to the rule that the sense of the sacred institutes is not to be taken from other sources than these, the Monist view, viz., that the purport of the texts of the Veda relates not to the duality learnt from those but to non-duality, is rejected: for as there is no proof of a God from inference, so there is no proof of the duality between God and other things from inference.

units.sanskrit: तस्मान्न भेदानुवादकत्वमिति तत्परत्वमवगम्यते। अत एवोक्तम् - सदागमैकविज्ञेयं मतीतक्षराक्षरम्।
units.english: Therefore there can be in these texts no mere explanation of such duality, and the texts must be understood to indicate the duality. Hence it is that it has said:—

units.sanskrit: नारायणं सदा वन्दे निर्दोंषाशेषसद्गुणम्॥ (वि.त.१) इति।
units.english: "I ever laud Nārāyaṇa, the one being to be known from genuine revelation, who transcends the perishable and the imperishable, without imperfections, and of inexhaustible excellences."

units.sanskrit: शास्त्रस्य तत्र प्रामाण्यमुपपादितं ऽतत्तु समन्वयात्ऽ (ब्र०सू०१/१/४) इति।
units.english: It has thus been evinced that the sacred institutes are the evidence of (the existence of) this (ultimate reality, Brahman).

units.sanskrit: समन्वय उपक्रमादिलङ्गम्।
units.english: (The fourth aphorism is): But that is from the construction.

units.sanskrit: उक्तं च बृहत्संहितायाम् - उपक्रमोपसंहारावभ्यासोऽपूर्वता फलम्। अर्थवादोपपत्ती च लिङ्गं तात्पर्यनिर्णये॥इति।
units.english: In regard to this, the commencement and other elements are stated to be the marks of the construction, in the Bṛhat-saṃhitā:— "Commencement, conclusion, reiteration, novelty, profit, eulogy, and demonstration, are the marks by which the purport is ascertained."

units.sanskrit: एवं वेदान्ततात्पर्यवशात् तदेव ब्रह्म शास्त्रगम्यमित्युक्तं भवति।
units.english: It is thus stated that in accordance with the purport of the Upaniṣads the absolute is to be apprehended only from the sacred institutes.

units.sanskrit: दिङ्मात्रमत्र प्रादर्शि।
units.english: We have here given merely a general indication.

units.sanskrit: शिष्टमानन्दतीर्थभाष्यव्याख्यानादौ द्रष्टव्यम्।
units.english: What remains may be sought from the Ānandatīrtha-bhāṣya-vyākhyāna (or exposition of the Commentary of Ānanda-tīrtha).

units.sanskrit: ग्रन्थबहुत्वभियोप रम्यत इति।
units.english: We desist for fear of giving an undue prolixity to our treatise.

units.sanskrit: एतच्च रहस्यं पूर्णप्रज्ञेन मध्यमन्दिरेण वायोस्तृतीयावतारम्यन्येन निरुपितम्।
units.english: This mystery was promulgated by Pūrṇa-prajña Madhya-mandira, who esteemed himself the third incarnation of Vāyu:—

units.sanskrit: प्रथमस्तु हनूमान्स्याद् द्वितीयो भीम एव च।
units.english: "The first was Hanumat, the second Bhīma,

units.sanskrit: पूर्णप्रज्ञस्तृतीयश्च भगवत्कार्यसाधकः॥
units.english: "The third Pūrṇa-prajña, the worker of the work of the Lord."

units.sanskrit: एतदेवाभिप्रेत्य तत्र तत्र ग्रन्थसमाप्ताविदं पद्यं लिख्यते - यस्य त्रीण्युदितानि वेदवचने दिव्यानि रुपाण्यलं बट् तद्दर्शतमित्थमेव निहितं देवस्य भर्गों महत्।
units.english: After expressing the same idea in various passages, he has written the following stanza at the conclusion of his work:— "That whereof the three divine forms are declared in the text of the Veda, sufficiently "Has that been set forth; this is the whole majesty in the splendour of the Veda;

units.sanskrit: वायो रामवचोनयं प्रथमकं पृक्षो द्वितीयं वपु र्मध्वो यत्तु तृतीयमेतदमुना ग्रन्थः कृतः के शवे॥ (म० भा० ता० ३२/१८१) एतत्पद्यार्थस्तु ऽबलित्था तद्वपुषे धायि दर्शतं देवस्य भर्गः सहसो यतोऽजनिऽ (ऋ०१/१४१/१) इत्यादिश्रुतिपर्यालोचनया-'वगम्यत इति। तस्मात्सर्वस्य शास्त्रस्य विष्णुतत्त्वं सर्वोंत्तममित्यत्र तात्पर्यमिति सर्वं निरवद्यम्।
units.english: "The first incarnation of the Wind-god was he that bowed to the words of Rāma (Hanumat); the second was Bhīma; "By this Madhva, who is the third, this book has been composed in regard to Keśava." The import of this stanza may be learnt by considering various Vedic texts. The purport of this is that Viṣṇu is the principle above all others in every system of sacred institutes.

units.sanskrit: (गणकारिका, ८) इति।
units.english: Thus all is clear.[1]

units.sanskrit: साधकस्य शुद्धिहेतुरुपायो वासचर्यादिभेदात्पञ्चविधः तदप्याह - वासचर्या जपो ध्यानं सदा रुद्रस्मृतिस्तथा।
units.english: [The seventh system in Mādhava's Sarva-darśana-saṅgraha is the Śaiva-darśana.

units.sanskrit: येनार्थानुसंधानपूर्वकं ज्ञानतपोवृद्धी प्राप्नोति स देशो गुरुजनादिः। यदाहगुरुर्जनो गुहादेशः श्मशानं रुद्र एव च।
units.english: This sect is very prevalent in the South of India, especially in the Tamil country; it is said to have arisen there about the eleventh century a.d.

units.sanskrit: आ लाभप्राप्तेरेकमर्यादावस्थितस्य यदवस्थानं सावस्था व्यक्तादिविशेषणविशिष्टा। बलपञ्चकं चगुरुभक्तिः प्रसादश्च मतेर्द्वन्द्वनयस्तथा। पञ्चमललघूकरणार्थमागमाविरोधिनोऽन्नार्जनोपाया वृत्तयो भैक्ष्योत्सृष्टयथालब्धाभिधा इति। शेषमशेषमाकर एवावगन्तव्यम्।
units.english: Several valuable contributions have been lately made to our knowledge of its tenets in the publications of the Rev. H. R. Hoisington and the Rev. T. Foulkes. The former especially, by his excellent articles in the American Oriental Society's Journal, has performed a great service to the students of Hindu philosophy.

units.sanskrit: आध्यात्मिकादिदुःखत्रयव्यपोहप्रश्नार्थत्वात्तस्य। पशुशब्देन कार्यस्य परतन्त्रवचनत्वात्तस्य। पतिशब्देन कारणस्य। ईश्वरः पतिरीशिता' इति जगत्कारणीभूतेश्वरवचनत्वात्तस्य। योगविधी तु प्रसिद्धौ।
units.english: He has there translated the Tattuva-Kaṭṭalei, or law of the Tattvas, the Śiva-Gnānapotham, or instruction in the knowledge of God, and the Śiva-Pirakāsam, or light of Śiva, and the three works shed immense light on the outline as given by Mādhava.

units.sanskrit: तत्र सूक्ष्मव्यवहितविप्रकृष्टाशेषचाक्षुषस्पर्शादिविषयं ज्ञानं दर्शनम्। अशेषशब्दविषयं सिद्धिज्ञानं श्रवणम्।
units.english: One great use of the latter is to enable us to recognise the original Sanskrit names in their Tamil disguise, no easy matter occasionally, as aṛul for anugraha and tīḍcei for dīkṣā may testify.

units.sanskrit: समस्तचिन्ताविषयं सिद्धिज्ञानं मननम्। निरवशेषशास्त्रविषयं ग्रन्थतोर्थतश्च सिद्धिज्ञानं विज्ञानम्। स्वशास्त्रं येनोच्चते। उक्तानुक्ताशेषार्थेषु समासविस्तरविभागविशेषतश्च तत्त्वव्याप्तसदोदितसिद्धिज्ञानं सर्वज्ञत्वमिति।
units.english: The Śaivas have considerable resemblance to the Theistic Sānkhya; they hold that God, souls, and matter are from eternity distinct entities, and the object of philosophy is to disunite the soul from matter and gradually to unite it to God.

units.sanskrit: एषा धीशक्तिः। क्रियाशक्तिरेकापि त्रिविधोपचर्यतेमनोजवित्वं कामरूपित्वं विकरण धर्मित्वं चेति।
units.english: Śiva is the chief deity of the system, and the relation between the three is quaintly expressed by the allegory of a beast, its fetters, and its owner.

units.sanskrit: एषा क्रियाशक्तिः। अस्वतन्त्रं सर्वं कार्यम्।
units.english: Paśupati is a well-known name of Śiva, as the master or creator of all things.

units.sanskrit: एतेषां ज्ञानात्संशयादिनिवृत्तिः।
units.english: There seem to be three different sets of so-called Saiva sūtras.

units.english: Certain, however, of the Māheśvara sect receiving the system of truth authoritatively laid down in the Śaiva Āgama,[1] reject the foregoing opinion that "the Supreme Being is a cause as independent of our actions, &c.," on the ground of its being liable to the imputation of partiality and cruelty. They, on the contrary, hold the opinion that "the Supreme Being is a cause in dependence on our actions, &c.;" and they maintain that there are three categories distinguished as the Lord, the soul, and the world (or literally "the master," "the cattle," and "the fetter").

units.sanskrit: यदुक्तसाधनं तदुक्तसाध्यं यथार्थादि।

units.english: Nor may we say with the Vedāntin that it is only one, since the apportionment of different fruits proves that there are many individual souls; nor with the Sānkhyas that it is devoid of action, since, when all the various "fetters" are removed, Śruti informs us of a state of identity with Śiva, which consists in intelligence in the form of an eternal and infinite vision and action.[21] This has been declared in the Śrīmat Mṛgendra—

units.sanskrit: क्लेशयुक्तोऽसर्वज्ञः परिमितशक्तिं प्राप्नुयादिति चेत्मैवं मंस्था।
units.english: "It is revealed that identity with Śiva results when all fetters are removed."

units.english: Now the souls are threefold, as denominated vijñānākalāḥ, pralayākalāḥ, and sakalāḥ.[22] (a.) The first are those who are under the influence of mala only, since their actions are cancelled by receiving their proper fruits, or by abstraction, contemplation, and knowledge, and since they have no "fetters" in the form of enjoyments, such as kalā, &c.

units.sanskrit: द्वितीयस्तु प्रलयेन कलादेरुपसंहारान्मलकर्मयुक्तः ऽप्रलयाकल' इति व्यवह्रियते।
units.english: (b.) The second are those who are under the influence of mala and karman, since in their case kalā, &c., are destroyed by mundane destructions, hence their name pralayākala.

units.english: (c.) The third are those who are bound in the three fetters of mala, māyā, and karman, hence their name sakala.

units.english: The following is the full meaning of this passage:—The word "internal organ," which properly includes "mind," "intelligence," "egoism," and "reason,"[28] includes also the seven tattvas which enter into the production of enjoyment [or experience], viz., those called kalā, time, fate, knowledge, concupiscence, nature, and quality;[29] the words "thought" (dhī) and karman signify the five cognisable gross elements, and their originators, the subtile rudiments.

units.english: It is also said in the Srīmad Mṛgendra— "He removes from that infinitesimal soul all the bonds which previously exerted a contrary influence over it."[32]

units.sanskrit: व्याकृतं च नारायणकण्ठेन। तत्सर्वं तत एवावधार्यम्। अस्माभिस्तु विस्तरभिया न प्रस्तूयते।
units.english: All this has been explained at great length by Nārāyaṇa-Kaṇṭha, and there it is to be studied; but we are obliged to pass on through fear of prolixity.

units.sanskrit: अपक्वकलुषान्बद्धानणूनभोगभाजो विधत्ते परमेश्वरः कर्मवशात्। तदप्युक्तम् - बद्धाञ्छे षानपरान् विनियुङ्क्ते भोगभुक्तये पुंसः। तत्कर्मणामनुगमादित्येवं कीर्तिताः पशवः॥
units.english: But as for the second class, or those called apakvakaluṣa, the Supreme Being, as impelled by the desert of their respective actions, appoints them, as bound and endued with infinitesimal bodies, to enjoy the rewards of their previous actions.[33] As has been said—

units.sanskrit: अस्यार्थःप्रावृणोति प्रकर्षेणाच्छादयत्यात्मनः स्वाभाविक्यौ दृक्क्रिये इति प्रावृत्तिरशुचिर्मलः। स च ईष्टे स्वातन्त्र्येणेति ईशः।
units.english: (4.) "Māyā," because herein as an energy of the Divine Being all the world is potentially contained (māti) at a mundane destruction, and again at a creation it all comes (yāti) into manifestation, hence the derivation of the name.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तम् तासामहं वरा शक्तिः सर्वानुग्राहिका शिवा।
units.english: This has been said in the Śrīmat Saurabheya—

units.sanskrit: धर्मानुवर्तनादेव पाश इत्युपचर्यते॥(२)। क्रियते फलार्थिभिरिति कर्म धर्माधर्मात्मकं बीजाङ्कु रवत्प्रवाहरूपेणानादि।
units.english: "The effects, as a form of the Divine energy, are absorbed therein at a mundane destruction, "And again at a renovation it is manifested anew in the form of effects as kalā, &c."[38]

units.sanskrit: (४) यद्यप्यत्र बहु वक्तव्यमस्ति तथापि ग्रन्थभूयस्त्वभयादुपरम्यते।
units.english: Although much more might be added on this topic, yet we stop here through fear of extending this treatise too far.

units.sanskrit: तदित्थं पति पशुपाशपदार्थास्त्रयः पदर्शिताः।
units.english: Thus have the three categories been declared,—the Lord, the soul, and matter.

units.sanskrit: पतिविद्ये तथाविद्या पशुः पाशश्च कारणम्।
units.english: "The Lord, knowledge, ignorance, the soul, matter, and the cause

units.sanskrit: तन्निवृत्ताविति प्रोक्ताः पदार्थाः षट् समासतः॥
units.english: "Of the cessation thereof,—these are collectively the six categories."

units.sanskrit: सर्वं तत एवागन्तव्यमिति सर्वं समञ्जसम्॥ अथ प्रत्यभिज्ञादर्शनम् ॥८॥
units.english: But our readers must seek for full information from the work itself. Thus our account of the system is complete.

units.sanskrit: अत्रापेक्षाविहीनानां जडानां कारणत्वं दुष्यतीत्यपरितुष्यन्तो , मतान्तरमन्विष्यन्तः, परमेश्वरेच्छावशादेव जगन्निर्माणं परिघुषयन्तः, स्वसंवेदनोपपत्त्या आगमसिद्धप्रत्यगात्मतादात्म्ये नानाविधमानमेयादिभेदाभेदशालिपरमेश्वरोऽनन्यमुखप्रेक्षित्वलक्षणस्वातन्त्र्यभाक् स्वात्मदर्पणे भावान्प्रतिबिम्बवद् अवभासयतीति भणन्तो, बाह्याभ्यन्तरचर्याप्राणायामादिक्लेशप्रयासकलापवैधुर्येण संर्वसुलभमभिनवं प्रत्यभिज्ञामात्रं परापरसिद्धयुपायमभ्युपगच्छन्तः, परे माहेश्वराः प्रत्यभिज्ञाशास्त्रमभ्यस्यन्ति।
units.english: They pronounce that this Supreme Lord, who is at once other than and the same with the several cognitions and cognita, who is identical with the transcendent self posited by one's own consciousness, by rational proof, and by revelation, and who possesses independence, that is, the power of witnessing all things without reference to aught ulterior, gives manifestation, in the mirror of one's own soul, to all entities[1] as if they were images reflected upon it. Thus looking upon recognition as a new method for the attainment of ends and of the highest end, available to all men alike, without any the slightest trouble and exertion, such as external and internal worship, suppression of the breath, and the like, these Māheśvaras set forth the system of recognition (pratyabhijñā).

units.sanskrit: तस्येयत्तापि न्यरूपि परीक्षकैः - सूत्रं वृत्तिर्विवृत्तिर्लध्वी बृहतीत्युभे विमर्शिन्यौ।
units.english: The extent of this system is thus described by one of their authorities— "The aphorisms, the commentary, the gloss, the two explications, the greater and the less,

units.sanskrit: प्रकरणविवरणपञ्चकमिति शास्त्रं प्रत्यभिज्ञायाः॥
units.english: "The five topics, and the expositions,—such is the system of recognition."

units.sanskrit: तत्रेदं प्रथमं सूत्रम् - कथंचिदासाद्य महेश्वरस्य दास्यं जनस्याप्युपकारमिच्छन्।
units.english: The first aphorism in their text-book is as follows[2]:— "Having reached somehow or other the condition of a slave of Maheśvara, and wishing also to help mankind,

units.sanskrit: समस्तसंपत्समवाप्तिहेतुं तत्प्रत्यभिज्ञामुपपादयामि॥इति॥
units.english: "I set forth the recognition of Maheśvara, as the method of attaining all felicity."

units.sanskrit: कथंचिदितिपरमेश्वराभिन्नगुरुचरणारविन्दयुगलसमाराधनेन परमेश्वरघटितेन एवेत्यर्थः। आसाद्येतिआ समन्तात्परिपूर्णतया सादयित्वा, स्वात्मोपभोग्यतां निरर्गलां गमयित्वा।
units.english: [This aphorism may be developed as follows]:— "Somehow or other," by a propitiation, effected by God, of the lotus feet of a spiritual director identical with God, "having reached," having fully attained, this condition, having made it the unintercepted object of fruition to myself.

units.sanskrit: तदनेन विदितवेद्यत्वेन परार्थशास्त्रकरणेऽधिकारो दर्शितः। अन्यथा प्रतारणमेव प्रसज्येत।
units.english: Thus knowing that which has to be known, he is qualified to construct a system for others: otherwise the system would be a mere imposture.

units.sanskrit: मायोत्तीर्णा अपि महामायाधिकृता विष्णुविरिञयाद्या यदीयैश्वर्यलेशेन ईश्वरीभूताः स भगवानानवच्छिन्नप्रकाशानन्दस्वातन्त्र्यपरमार्थों महेश्वरः।
units.english: Maheśvara is the reality of unintermitted self-luminousness, beatitude, and independence, by portions of whose divine essence Viṣṇu, Viriñci, and other deities are deities, who, though they transcend the fictitious world, are yet implicated in the infinite illusion.

units.sanskrit: तस्य दास्यम्। दीयतेऽस्मै स्वामिना सर्वं यथाभिलषितमिति दासः। परमेश्वरस्वरूपस्वातन्त्र्यपात्रमित्यर्थः।
units.english: The condition of being a slave to Maheśvara is the being a recipient of that independence or absoluteness which is the essence of the divine nature, a slave being one to whom his lord grants all things according to his will and pleasure (i.e., dāsya, from dā).

units.sanskrit: जनशब्देनाधिकारिविषयनियमाभावः प्रादर्शि।
units.english: The word mankind imports that there is no restriction of the doctrine to previously qualified students.

units.sanskrit: यस्य यस्य हीदं स्वरूपकथनं तस्य तस्य महाफलं भवति। प्रज्ञानस्यैव परमार्थफलत्वात्।
units.english: Whoever he may be to whom this exposition of the divine nature is made, he reaps its highest reward, the emanatory principium itself operating to the highest end of the transmigrating souls.

units.sanskrit: तथोपदिष्टं शिवदृष्टौ परमगुरुभिर्भगवत्सोमानन्दनाथपादैः - एकवारं प्रमाणेन शास्त्राद्वा गुरुवाक्यतः। ज्ञाते शिवत्वे सर्वस्थे प्रतिपत्या दृढात्मना॥
units.english: It has been accordingly laid down in the Śiva-dṛṣṭi by that supreme guide the revered Somānandanātha— "When once the nature of Śiva that resides in all things has been known with tenacious recognition, whether by proof or by instruction in the words of a spiritual director,

units.sanskrit: करणेन नास्ति कृत्यं क्वापि भावनयापि वा।
units.english: "There is no further need of doing aught, or of any further reflection.

units.sanskrit: ज्ञाते सुवर्णे करणं भावानां वा परित्यजेत्॥
units.english: When he knows Suvarṇa (or Śiva) a man may cease to act and to reflect."

units.sanskrit: अपिशब्देन स्वात्मनस्तदभिन्नतामाविष्कु र्वता पूर्णत्वेन स्वात्मनि परार्थसंपत्त्यतिरिक्तप्रयोजनान्तरावकाशश्च पराकृतः। परार्थश्च प्रयोजनं भवत्येव।
units.english: The word also excludes the supposition that there is room in self which has recognised the nature of Maheśvara, and which manifests to itself its own identity with him, and is therefore fully satisfied, for any other motive than felicity for others.

units.sanskrit: तल्लक्षणयोगात्। न ह्ययं देवशापः ऽस्वार्थ एव प्रयोजनं न परार्थ' इति।
units.english: The well-being of others is a motive, whatever may be said, for the definition of a motive applies to it: for there is no such divine curse laid upon man that self-regard should be his sole motive to the exclusion of a regard for others.

units.sanskrit: अत एवोक्तमक्षपादेन-'यमर्थमधिकृत्य प्रवर्तते तत्प्रयोजनम्ऽ (गौ०सू० १/१/२४) इति।
units.english: Thus Akṣapāda (i. 24) defines a motive: A motive is that object towards which a man energises.

units.sanskrit: उपशब्दः सामीप्यार्थः। तेन जनस्य परमेश्वरसमीपताकरणमात्रं फलम्।
units.english: The preposition upa in upapādayami (I set forth) indicates proximity: the result is the bringing of mankind near unto God.

units.sanskrit: अत एवाह - समस्तेति।
units.english: Hence the word all in the phrase the method of attaining all felicities.

units.sanskrit: परमेश्वरतालाभे हि सर्वाः संपदस्तन्निष्यन्दमय्यः संपन्ना एव, रोहणाचललाभे रत्नसंपद इव।
units.english: For when the nature of the Supreme Being is attained, all felicities, which are but the efflux thereof, are overtaken, as if a man acquired the mountain Rohaṇa (Adam's Peak), he would acquire all the treasures it contains.

units.sanskrit: एवं परमेश्वरतालाभे किमन्यत्प्रार्थनीयम् ? तदुक्तमुत्पलाचार्यैः - भक्तिलक्ष्मीसमृद्धानां किमन्यदुपयाचितम्। एतया वा दरिद्राणां किमन्यदपयाचितम्॥
units.english: If a man acquire the divine nature, what else is there that he can ask for? Accordingly Utpalācārya says— "What more can they ask who are rich in the wealth of devotion? What else can they ask who are poor in this?"

units.sanskrit: इत्थं षष्ठीसमासपक्षे प्रयोजनं निर्दिष्टम्।
units.english: We have thus explained the motive expressed in the words the method of attaining all felicities, on the supposition that the compound term is a Tatpuruṣa genitively constructed.

units.sanskrit: बहुव्रीहिपक्षे तूपपादयामः।
units.english: Let it be taken as a Bahuvrīhi or relative compound.

units.sanskrit: समस्तस्य बाह्याभ्यन्तरस्य नित्यसुखादेर्या संपत्सिद्धिः तथात्वप्रकाशः, तस्याः सम्यगवाप्तिर्यस्याः प्रत्यभिज्ञायाः हेतुः सा तथोक्ता। तस्य महेश्वरस्य प्रत्यभिज्ञा, प्रति आभिमुख्येन, ज्ञानम्।
units.english: Then the recognition of Maheśvara, the knowing him through vicarious idols, has for its motive the full attainment, the manifestation, of all felicities, of every external and internal permanent happiness in their proper nature.

units.sanskrit: लोके हि स एवायं चैत्र इति प्रतिसंधानेनाभिमुखीभूते वस्तुनि ज्ञानं प्रत्यभिज्ञेति व्यवह्रियते।
units.english: In the language of everyday life, recognition is a cognition relative to an object represented in memory: for example, This (perceived) is the same (as the remembered) Caitra.

units.sanskrit: इहापि प्रसिद्धपुराणसिद्धागमानुमानादिज्ञातपरिपूर्णशक्तिके परमेश्वरे सति स्वात्मनि अभिमुखीभूते तच्छक्तिप्रतिसंधानेन ज्ञानमुदेति नूनं स एवेश्वरोऽहमिति।
units.english: In the recognition propounded in this system,—there being a God whose omnipotence is learnt from the accredited legendaries, from accepted revelation, and from argumentation,—there arises in relation to my presented personal self the cognition that I am that very God,—in virtue of my recollection of the powers of that God.

units.sanskrit: तामेतां प्रत्यभिज्ञानुपपादयामि।
units.english: This same recognition I set forth.

units.sanskrit: उपपत्तिः संभवः।
units.english: To set forth is to enforce.

units.sanskrit: संभवतीति सत्समर्थाचारणेन प्रयोजकव्यापारेण संपादयामीत्यर्थः।
units.english: I establish this recognition by a stringent process which renders it convincing. [Such is the articulate development of the first aphorism of the Recognitive Institutes.]

units.sanskrit: यदीश्वरस्वभाव एवात्मा प्रकाशते, तर्हि किमनेन प्रत्यभिज्ञाप्रदर्शनप्रयासेनेति चेत्तत्रायं समाधिः। स्वप्रकाशतया सततमवभासमानेऽप्यात्मनि मायावशाद् भागेन प्रकाशमाने पूर्णतावभाससिद्धये दृक्क्रियात्मकशक्त्याविष्करणेन प्रत्यभिज्ञा प्रदर्श्यते।
units.english: Here it may be asked: If soul is manifested only as consubstantial with God, why this laboured effort to exhibit the recognition? The answer is this:—The recognition is thus exhibited, because though the soul is, as you contend, continually manifested as self-luminous (and therefore identical with God), it is nevertheless under the influence of the cosmothetic illusion manifested as partial, and therefore the recognition must be exhibited by an expansion of the cognitive and active powers in order to achieve the manifestation of the soul as total (the self being to the natural man a part, to the man of insight the whole, of the divine pleroma).

units.sanskrit: तथा च प्रयोगः ऽअयमात्मा परमेश्वरो भवितुमर्हति। ज्ञानक्रियाशक्तिमत्त्वात्। यो यावति ज्ञाता कर्ता च स तावतीश्वरः प्रसिद्धेश्वरवद्राजवद्वा। आत्मा च विश्वज्ञाता कर्ता च। तस्मादीश्वरोऽयम्ऽ इति।
units.english: Thus, then, the syllogism: This self must be God, because it possesses cognitive and active powers; for so far forth as any one is cognitive and active, to that extent he is a lord, like a lord in the world of everyday life, or like a king, therefore the soul is God.

units.sanskrit: अवयवपञ्चकस्याश्रयणं मायावदेव नैयायिकमतस्य कक्षीकारात्।
units.english: The five-membered syllogism is here employed, because so long as we deal with the illusory order of things, the teaching of the Naiyāyikas may be accepted.

units.sanskrit: तदक्तमुदुयाकरसूनुना - कर्तरि ज्ञातरि स्वात्मन्यादिसिद्धे महेश्वरे। अजडात्मा निषेधं वा सिद्धिं वा विदधीत कः॥
units.english: It has thus been said by the son of Udayākara— "What self-luminous self can affirm or deny that self-active and cognitive is Maheśvara the primal being?

units.sanskrit: शक्त्याविष्करणेनेयं प्रत्यभिज्ञोपदर्श्यते॥
units.english: "Such recognition must be effected by an expansion of the powers, the self being cognised under illusion, and imperfectly discerned."

units.sanskrit: तथा हिसर्वेषामिह भूतानां प्रतिष्ठा जीवदाश्रया। ज्ञानं क्रिया च भूतानां जीवतां जीवनं मतम्॥
units.english: "The continuance of all living creatures in this transmigratory world lasts as long as their respiratory involucrum; knowledge and action are accounted the life of living creatures.

units.sanskrit: तत्र ज्ञानं स्वतःसिद्धं क्रिया कार्याश्रिता सती।
units.english: "Of these, knowledge is spontaneously developed, and action (or ritual), which is best at Kāśi,

units.sanskrit: परैरप्युपलक्ष्येत तथान्यज्ञानमुच्यते॥
units.english: "Is indicated by others also: different from these is real knowledge."

units.sanskrit: या चैषां प्रतिभा तत्तत्पदार्थक्रमरूपिता।
units.english: "The knowledge of these things follows the sequence of those things:

units.sanskrit: अक्रमानन्दूचिद्रपः प्रमाता स महेश्वरः॥
units.english: "The knower, whose essence is beatitude and knowledge without succession, is Maheśvara."

units.sanskrit: इति च॥ सोमानन्दनाथपादैरपि - सदा शिवात्मना वेत्ति सदा वेत्ति मदात्मना। इत्यादि।
units.english: Somānandanātha also says— "He always knows by identity with Śiva: he always knows by identity with the real."

units.sanskrit: ज्ञानाधिकारपरिसमाप्तावपि - तदैक्येन विना नास्ति संविदां लोकपद्धतिः।
units.english: Again at the end of the section on knowledge— "Unless there were this unity with Śiva, cognitions could not exist as facts of daily life:

units.sanskrit: प्रकाशैक्यात्तदेकत्वं मातैकः स इति स्थितिः॥
units.english: "Unity with God is proved by the unity of light.

units.sanskrit: स एव विमृशत्वेन नियतेन महेश्वरः।
units.english: "He is Maheśvara, the great Lord, by reason of the unbroken continuity of objects:

units.sanskrit: विमर्श एव देवस्य शुद्धे ज्ञानक्रिये यतः॥
units.english: "Pure knowledge and action are the playful activity of the deity."

units.sanskrit: ऽतमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं, तस्य भासा सर्वभिदं विभातिऽ (काठक०२/२) इति श्रुत्या प्रकाशचिद्रूपमहिम्ना सर्वस्य भावजातस्य भासकत्वमभ्युपेयते। ततश्च विषयप्रकाशस्य नीलप्रकाशः पीतप्रकाश इति विषयोपरागभेदाद्भेदः।
units.english: The following is an explanation of Abhinava-gupta:—The text, "After that as it shines shines the all of things, by the light of that shines diversely this All," teaches that God illumines the whole round of things by the glory of His luminous intelligence, and that the diversity or plurality of the object world, whereby the light which irradiates objects is a blue, a yellow light, and the like, arises from diversity of tint cast upon the light by the object.

units.sanskrit: वस्तुतस्तु देशकालाकारसंकोचवैकल्यादभेद एव।
units.english: In reality, God is without plurality or difference, as transcending all limitations of space, time, and figure.

units.sanskrit: स एव चैतन्यरूपः प्रकाशः प्रमातेत्युच्यते। तथा च पठितं शिवसूत्रेषु- ऽचैतन्यमात्मा' (१/१) इति। तस्य चिद्रूपत्वमनवच्छिन्नविमर्शत्वमनन्योन्मुखत्व - मानन्दैकघनत्वं माहेश्वर्यमिति पर्यायः।
units.english: He is pure intelligence, self-luminousness, the manifester; and thus we may read in the Śaiva aphorisms, "Self is intelligence." His synonymous titles are Intelligential Essence, Unintermitted Cognition, Irrespective Intuition, Existence as a mass of Beatitude, Supreme Domination.

units.sanskrit: स एव ह्ययं भावात्मा विमर्शः शुद्धे पारमार्थिक्यौ ज्ञानक्रिये। तत्र प्रकाशरूपता ज्ञानम्। स्वतो जगन्निर्मातृत्वं क्रिया।
units.english: This self-same existing self is knowledge. By pure knowledge and action (in the passage of Somānandanātha cited above) are meant real or transcendent cognition and activity.

units.sanskrit: तच्च निरुपितं क्रियाधिकारेएष चानन्तशक्तित्वादेवमाभासयत्यमून्। भावानिच्छावशादेषां क्रिया निर्मातृतास्य सा॥
units.english: This is described in the section on activity— "He by his power of bliss gives light unto these objects, through the efficacy of his will: this activity is creativeness."

units.sanskrit: उपसंहारेऽपि - इत्थं तथा घटपटाद्याकारजगदात्मना।
units.english: And at the close of the same section—

units.sanskrit: तिष्ठासोरेवामिच्छैव हेतुकर्तृकृता क्रिया॥ तस्मिन्सतीदमस्तीति कार्यकारणता'पि या।
units.english: "The mere will of God, when he wills to become the world under its forms of jar, of cloth, and other objects, is his activity worked out by motive and agent.

units.sanskrit: साप्यपेक्षाविहीनानां जडानां नोपपद्यते॥
units.english: "This process of essence into emanation, whereby if this be that comes to be, cannot be attributed to motiveless, insentient things."

units.sanskrit: इति न्यायेन यतो जडस्य न कारणता न वा'नीश्वरस्य चेतनस्यापि, तस्मात्तेन तेन जगद्गतजन्मस्थित्यादिभावविकारतत्तद्भेदक्रियासहस्ररूपेण स्थातुमिच्छोः स्वतन्त्रस्य भगवतो महेश्वरस्येच्छै व उत्तरोत्तरमुच्छू नस्वभावा क्रिया विश्वकर्तृत्वं वोच्यत इति।
units.english: According to these principles, causality not pertaining either to the insentient or to the non-divine intelligence, the mere will of Maheśvara, the absolute Lord, when he wills to emanate into thousands of forms, as this or that difference, this or that action, this or that modification of entity, of birth, continuance, and the like, in the series of transmigratory environments,—his mere will is his progressively higher and higher activity, that is to say, his universal creativeness.

units.sanskrit: इच्छामात्रेण जगन्निर्माणमित्यत्र दृष्टान्तोऽपि स्पष्टं निर्दिष्टः - योगिनामपि मृद्बीजे विनैवेच्छावशेन यत्।
units.english: How he creates the world by his will alone is clearly exhibited in the following illustration— "The tree or jar produced by the mere will of thaumaturgists, without clay, without seed, continues to serve its proper purpose as tree or jar."

units.sanskrit: घटादि जायते तत्तत्स्थिरभावक्रियाकरम्॥ यदि घटादिकं प्रति मृदाद्येव परमार्थतः कारणं स्यात्तर्हि कथं योगीच्छामात्रेण घटादिजन्म स्यात्? अथोच्येतअन्य एव मृद्बीजादिजन्या घटाङ्कु रादयो, योगीच्छाजन्यास्त्वन्य एवेति। तत्रापि बोध्यसेसामग्रीभेदात्तावत्कार्यभेद इति सर्वजनप्रसिद्धम्।
units.english: If clay and similar materials were really the substantial cause of the jar and the rest, how could they be produced by the mere volition of the thaumaturgist? If you say: Some jars and some plants are made of clay, and spring from seeds, while others arise from the bare volition of the thaumaturgist; then we should inform you that it is a fact notorious to all the world that different things must emanate from different materials.

units.sanskrit: ये तु वर्णयन्ति नोपादानं विना घटाद्युत्पत्तिरिति, योगी त्विच्छया परमाणून्व्यापारयन् संघटयतीति तेऽपि बोधनीयाः। यदि परिदृष्टकार्यकारणभावविपर्ययो न लभ्येत तर्हि घटे मृद्दण्डचक्रादि देहे स्त्रीपुरुषसंयोगादि सर्वमपेक्ष्येत।
units.english: As for those who say that a jar or the like cannot be made without materials to make it of, and that when a thaumaturgist makes one he does so by putting atoms in motion by his will, and so composing it: they may be informed that unless there is to be a palpable violation of the causal relation, all the co-efficients, without exception, must be desiderated; to make the jar there must be the clay, the potter's staff, the potter's wheel, and all the rest of it; to make a body there must be the congress of the male and female, and the successive results of that congress.

units.sanskrit: तथा च योगीच्छासमनन्तरसंजातघटदेहादिसंभवो दुःसमर्थ एव स्यात्।
units.english: Now, if that be the case, the genesis of a jar, a body, or the like, upon the mere volition of the thaumaturgist, would be hardly possible.

units.sanskrit: चेतन एव तु तथा भाति, भगवान् भूरिभगो महादेवोनियत्यनुवर्तनोल्लङ्घनघनतरस्वातन्त्र्य इति पक्षे न काचिदनुपपत्तिः। अत एवोक्तं वसुगुप्ताचार्यैः - निरुपादानसंभारमभित्तावेव तन्वते। जगच्चित्रं नमस्तस्मै कलानाथाय शूलिने॥
units.english: On the other hand, there is no difficulty in supposing that Mahādeva, amply free to remain within or to over-step any limit whatever, the Lord, manifold in his operancy, the intelligent principle, thus operates. Thus it is that Vasuguptācārya says— "To him that painted this world-picture without materials, without appliances, without a wall to paint it on,—to him be glory, to him resplendent with the lunar digit, to him that bears the trident."

units.sanskrit: ननु प्रत्यगात्मनः परमेश्वराभिन्नत्वे संसारसंबन्धः कथं भवेदिति चेत् - तत्रोक्तमागमाधिकारे - एष प्रमाता मायान्धः संसारी कर्मबन्धनः।
units.english: It may be asked: If the supersensible self be no other than God, how comes this implication in successive transmigratory conditions? The answer is given in the section treating of accredited institution— "This agent of cognition, blinded by illusion, transmigrates through the fatality of works:

units.sanskrit: विद्यादिज्ञापितैश्वर्यश्चिद्धनो मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.english: "Taught his divine nature by science, as pure intelligence, he is enfranchised."

units.sanskrit: ननु प्रमेयस्य प्रमात्रभिन्नत्वे बद्धमुक्तयोः प्रमेयं प्रति को विशेषः ? अत्राप्युत्तरमुक्तं तत्त्वार्थसंग्रहाधिकारे - मेयं साधारणं मुक्तः स्वात्माभेदेन मन्यते।
units.english: It may be asked: If the subject and the object are identical, what difference can there be between the self bound and the self liberated in regard to the objects cognisable by each? The answer to this question is given in a section of the Tattvārtha-Saṅgraha—

units.sanskrit: महेश्वरो यथा बद्धः पुनरत्यन्तभेदवत्॥ नन्वात्मनः परमेश्वरत्वं स्वाभाविकं चेन्नार्थः प्रत्यभिज्ञाप्रार्थनया।
units.english: "Self liberated cognises all that is cognisable as identical with itself, like Maheśvara free from bondage: the other (or unliberated) self has in it infinite plurality."

units.sanskrit: न हि बीजमप्रतिज्ञातं सति सहकारिसाकल्येऽङ्कुरं नोत्पादयति।
units.english: An objection may be raised: If the divine nature is essential to the soul, there can be no occasion to seek for this recognition; for if all requisites be supplied, the seed does not fail to germinate because it is unrecognised.

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्कस्माद्वात्मप्रत्यभिज्ञाने निर्बन्ध इति चेत् - उच्यते। श्रृणु तावदिदं रहस्यम्।
units.english: Why, then, this toilsome effort for the recognition of the soul? To such an objection we reply: Only listen to the secret we shall tell you.

units.sanskrit: द्विविधा ह्यार्थक्रियाबाह्याङ्कु रादिका, प्रमातृविश्रान्तिचमत्कारसारा प्रीत्यादिरूपा च।
units.english: All activity about objects is of two degrees, being either external, as the activity of the seed in developing the plant, or internal, as the activity which determines felicity, which consists in an intuition which terminates in the conscious self.

units.sanskrit: तत्राद्या प्रत्यभिज्ञानं नापेक्षते। द्वितीया तु तदपेक्षत एव।
units.english: The first degree of activity presupposes no such recognition as the system proposes, the second does presuppose it.

units.sanskrit: इहाप्यहमीश्वर इत्येवंभूतचमत्कारसारा परापरसिद्धिलक्षणजीवात्मैकत्वशक्तिविभूतिरूपार्थक्रियेति स्वरूपप्रत्यभिज्ञानमपेक्षणीयम्।
units.english: In the Recognitive System the peculiar activity is the exertion of the power of unifying personal and impersonal spirit, a power which is the attainment of the highest and of mediate ends, the activity consisting in the intuition I am God.

units.sanskrit: ननु प्रमातृविश्रान्तिसारार्थक्रिया प्रत्यभिज्ञानेन विना अदृष्टा सती तस्मिन्दृष्टेति क्व दृष्टम् ? अत्रोच्यतेनायकगुणगणसंश्रवणप्रवृद्धानुरागा काचन कामिनी मदनविह्वला विरहक्लेशमसहमाना मदनलेखावलम्बनेन स्वावस्थानिवेदनानि विधत्ते।
units.english: It may be urged that peculiar activity terminating in the conscious self is observed independent of recognition. To this it is replied: A certain damsel, hearing of the many good qualities of a particular gallant, fell in love with him before she had seen him, and agitated by her passion and unable to suffer the pain of not seeing him, wrote to him a love-letter descriptive of her condition.

units.sanskrit: तथा वेगात्तन्निकटमटन्त्यपि तस्मिन्नवलोकितेऽपि तदवलोकनं तदीयगुणपरामर्शाभावे जनसाधारणत्वं प्राप्ते हृदयङ्गमभावं न लभते।
units.english: He at once came to her, but when she saw him she did not recognise in him the qualities she had heard about; he appeared much the same as any other man, and she found no gratification in his society.

units.sanskrit: यदा तु दूतीवचनात् तदीयगुणपरामर्शं करोति तदा तत्क्षणमेव पूर्णभावमभ्येति।
units.english: So soon, however, as she recognised those qualities in him as her companions now pointed them out, she was fully gratified.

units.sanskrit: एवं स्वात्मनि विश्वेश्वरात्मना भासमानेऽपि तन्निर्भासनं तदीयगुणपरामर्श विरहसमये पूर्णभावं न संपादयति। यदा तु गुरुवचनादिना सर्वज्ञत्वसर्वकर्तृत्वादिलक्षणपरमेश्वरोत्कर्षपरामर्शों जायते तदा तत्क्षणमेव पूर्णात्मतालाभः।
units.english: In like manner, though the personal self be manifested as identical with the universal soul, its manifestation effects no complete satisfaction so long as there is no recognition of those attributes; but as soon as it is taught by a spiritual director to recognise in itself the perfections of Maheśvara, his omniscience, omnipotence, and other attributes, it attains the whole pleroma of being.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं चतुर्थे विमर्शे - तैस्तैरप्युपयाचितैरुपनतस्तस्याः स्थितोऽप्यन्तिके कान्तो लोकसमान एवमपरिज्ञातो न रन्तुं यथा। लोकस्यैष तथानवेक्षितगुणः स्वात्मापि विश्वेश्वरो नैवायं निजवैभवाय तदियं तत्प्रत्यभिज्ञोदिता॥
units.english: It is therefore said in the fourth section— "As the gallant standing before the damsel is disdained as like all other men, so long as he is unrecognised, though he humble himself before her with all manner of importunities: In like manner the personal self of mankind, though it be the universal soul, in which there is no perfection unrealised, attains not its own glorious nature; and therefore this recognition thereof must come into play."

units.sanskrit: (ई.प्र.४/२/२) अभिनवगुप्तादिभिराचार्यैर्विहितप्रतानोऽप्ययमर्थः संग्रहमुपक्रममाणैरस्माभिर्विस्तरभिया न प्रतानित इति सर्वं शिवम्॥
units.english: This system has been treated in detail by Abhinava-gupta and other teachers, but as we have in hand a summary exposition of systems, we cannot extend the discussion of it any further lest our work become too prolix.

units.sanskrit: अथ रसेश्वरदर्शनम् ॥९॥
units.english: This then may suffice.[3]

units.sanskrit: अपरे माहेश्वराः परमेश्वरतादात्म्यवादिनोऽपि, पिण्डस्थैर्ये सर्वाभिमता जीवन्मुक्तिः सेत्स्यतीत्यास्थाय, पिण्डस्थैर्योंपायं पारदादिपदवेदनीयं रसमेव संगिरन्ते।
units.english: Other Māheśvaras there are who, while they hold the identity of self with God, insist upon the tenet that the liberation in this life taught in all the systems depends upon the stability of the bodily frame, and therefore celebrate the virtues of mercury or quicksilver as a means of strengthening the system.

units.sanskrit: रसस्य पारदत्वं संसारपरप्रापणहेतुत्वेन।
units.english: Mercury is called pārada, because it is a means of conveyance beyond the series of transmigratory states.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तम् - संसारस्य परं पारं दत्तेऽसौ पारदः स्मृतः।
units.english: Thus it has been said— "It gives the farther shore of metempsychosis: it is called pārada."

units.sanskrit: रसर्णवेऽपि - पारदो गदितो यस्मात्परार्थं साधकोत्तमैः।
units.english: "It is styled pārada because it is employed for the highest end by the best votaries.

units.sanskrit: सुप्तोऽयं मत्समो देवि ! मम प्रत्यङ्गसम्भवः। मम देहरसो यस्माद्रसस्तेनायमुच्यते॥
units.english: "Since this in sleep identical with me, goddess, arises from my members, and is the exudation of my body, it is called rasa."

units.sanskrit: ननु प्रकारान्तरेणापि जीवन्मुक्तियुक्तौ नेयं वाचोयुक्तिर्युक्तिमतीति चेन्न, षट्स्वपि दर्शनेषु देहपातानन्तरं मुक्ते रुक्ततया तत्र विश्वासानुपपत्त्या निर्विचिकित्सप्रवृत्तेरनुपपत्तेः।
units.english: It may be urged that the literal interpretation of these words is incorrect, the liberation in this life being explicable in another manner. This objection is not allowable, liberation being set out in the six systems as subsequent to the death of the body, and upon this there can be no reliance, and consequently no activity to attain to it free from misgivings.

units.sanskrit: तदप्युक्तं तत्रैवषड्दर्शनेऽपि मुक्तिस्तु दर्शिता पिण्डपातने।
units.english: This is also laid down in the same treatise— "Liberation is declared in the six systems to follow the death of the body.

units.sanskrit: करामलकवत्सापि प्रत्यक्षा नोपलभ्यते।
units.english: "Such liberation is not cognised in perception like an emblic myrobalan fruit in the hand.

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्तं रक्षयेत्पिण्डं रसैश्चैव रसायनैः॥
units.english: "Therefore a man should preserve that body by means of mercury and of medicaments."

units.sanskrit: गोविन्दभगवत्पादाचार्यैरपि - इति धनशरीरभोगान्मत्वानित्यान्सदैव यतनीयम्।
units.english: Govinda-bhagavat also says— "Holding that the enjoyments of wealth and of the body are not permanent, one should strive

units.sanskrit: मुक्तौ सा च ज्ञानात्तच्चाभ्यासात्स च स्थिरे देहे॥
units.english: "After emancipation; but emancipation results from knowledge, knowledge from study, and study is only possible in a healthy body."

units.sanskrit: ननु विनश्वरतया दृश्यमानस्य देहस्य कथं नित्यत्वमवसीयत इति चेत्मैवं मंस्थाः। षाट्कौशिकस्य शरीरस्यानित्यत्वेऽपि रसाभ्रकपदाभिलप्यहरगौरीसृष्टिजातस्य नित्यत्वोपपत्तेः - तथा च रसहृदये - ये चात्यक्तशरीरा हरगौरीसृष्टिजां तनुं प्राप्ताः।
units.english: The body, some one may say, is seen to be perishable, how can its permanency be effected? Think not so, it is replied, for though the body, as a complexus of six sheaths or wrappers of the soul, is dissoluble, yet the body, as created by Hara and Gaurī under the names of mercury and mica, may be perdurable. Thus it is said in the Rasahṛdaya— "They who, without quitting the body, have attained to a new body, the creation of Hara and Gaurī,

units.sanskrit: मुक्तास्ते रससिद्धा मन्त्रगणः किं करो येषाम्॥ (१/७) इति॥
units.english: "They are to be lauded, perfected by mercury, at whose service is the aggregate of magic texts."

units.sanskrit: तस्माज्जीवन्मुक्तिं समीहमानेन योगिना प्रथमं दिव्यतनुर्विधेया।
units.english: The ascetic, therefore, who aspires to liberation in this life should first make to himself a glorified body.

units.sanskrit: हरगौरीसृष्टिसंयोगजनितत्वं च रसस्य हरजत्वेनाभ्रकस्य गौरीसंभवत्वेन तत्तदात्मकत्वमुक्तम् - अभ्रकस्तव बीजं तु मम बीजं तु पारदः।
units.english: And inasmuch as mercury is produced by the creative conjunction of Hara and Gaurī, and mica is produced from Gaurī, mercury and mica are severally identified with Hara and Gaurī in the verse— "Mica is thy seed, and mercury is my seed;

units.sanskrit: अनयोर्मेलनं देवि मृत्युदारिद्रयनाशनम्॥
units.english: "The combination of the two, O goddess, is destructive of death and poverty."

units.sanskrit: अत्यल्पमिदमुच्यते।
units.english: This is very little to say about the matter.

units.sanskrit: देवदैत्यमुनिमानवादिषु बहवो रससामर्थ्याद्दिव्यं देहमाश्रित्य जीवन्मुक्तिमाश्रिताः श्रूयन्ते रमेश्वरसिद्धान्ते - देवाः के चिन्महेशाद्या दैत्याः काव्यपुरस्सराः।
units.english: In the Raseśvara-siddhānta many among the gods, the Daityas, the Munis, and mankind, are declared to have attained to liberation in this life by acquiring a divine body through the efficacy of quicksilver. "Certain of the gods, Maheśa and others; certain Daityas, Śukra and others;

units.sanskrit: मुनयो बालखिल्याद्या नृपाः सोमेश्वरादयः॥
units.english: "Certain Munis, the Bālakhilyas and others; certain kings, Someśvara and others;

units.sanskrit: गोविन्दभगवत्पादाचार्यों गोविन्दनायकः।
units.english: "Govinda-bhagavat, Govinda-nāyaka,

units.sanskrit: चर्वटिः कपिलो व्यालिः कापालिः कन्दलायनः॥
units.english: "Charvaṭi, Kapila, Vyāli, Kāpāli, Kandalāyana,

units.sanskrit: एतेऽन्ये बहवः सिद्धा जीवन्मुक्ताश्चरन्ति हि।
units.english: "These and many others proceed perfected, liberated while alive,

units.sanskrit: तनुं रसमयीं प्राप्य तदात्मककथाचणाः॥
units.english: "Having attained to a mercurial body, and therewith identified."

units.sanskrit: अयमेवार्थः परमेश्वरेण परमेश्वरीं प्रति प्रपञ्चितः - कर्मयोगेण देवेशि प्राप्यते पिण्डधारणम्।
units.english: The meaning of this, as explicated by Parameśvara to Parameśvarī, is as follows:— "By the method of works is attained, O supreme of goddesses, the preservation of the body;

units.sanskrit: रसश्च पवनश्चेति कर्मयोगो द्विधा स्मृतः॥
units.english: "And the method of works is said to be twofold, mercury and air,

units.sanskrit: मूर्च्छितो हरति व्याधीन्मृतो जीवयति स्वयम्। बद्धः खेचरतां कु र्याद्रसो वायुश्च भैरवि॥
units.english: "Mercury and air swooning carry off diseases, dead they restore to life, "Bound they give the power of flying about."

units.sanskrit: मूर्च्छितस्वरूपमुक्तम् - नानावर्णों भवेत्सूतो विहाय घनचापलम्। लक्षणं दृश्यते यस्य मूर्च्छितं तं वदन्ति हि॥
units.english: "They say quicksilver to be swooning when it is perceived, as characterised thus— "Of various colours, and free from excessive volatility. "A man should regard that quicksilver as dead, in which the following marks are seen—

units.sanskrit: आर्द्रत्वं च घनत्वं च तेजो गौरवचापलम्।
units.english: "Wetness, thickness, brightness, heaviness, mobility."

units.sanskrit: अन्यत्र बद्धस्वरूपमप्यभ्यधायि - अक्षतश्च लघुद्रावी तेजस्वी निर्मलो गुरुः। स्फोटनं पुनरावृत्तौ बद्धसूतस्य लक्षणम॥इति।
units.english: The bound condition is described in another place as follows:— "The character of bound quicksilver is that it is— "Continuous, fluent, luminous, pure, heavy, and that it parts asunder under friction."

units.sanskrit: ननु हरगौरीसृष्टिसिद्धौ पिण्डस्थैर्यमास्थातुं पार्यते, तत्सिद्धिरेव कथमिति चेत्न। अष्टादशसंस्कारवशात्तदुपपत्तेः। तदुक्तमाचार्यैः - तस्य प्रसाधनविधौ सुधिया प्रतिकर्मनिर्मला प्रथमम्।
units.english: Some one may urge: If the creation of mercury by Hara and Gaurī were proved, it might be allowed that the body could be made permanent; but how can that be proved? The objection is not allowable, inasmuch as that can be proved by the eighteen modes of elaboration. Thus it is stated by the authorities—

units.sanskrit: अष्टादश संस्कारा विज्ञातव्याः प्रयत्नेन॥
units.english: "Eighteen modes of elaboration are to be carefully discriminated,

units.sanskrit: ते च संस्कारा निरुपिताः - स्वेदनमर्दनमूर्च्छनस्थापनपातननिरोधनियमाश्च।
units.english: And these modes of elaboration are enumerated thus— "Sweating, rubbing, swooning, fixing, dropping, coercion, restraining,

units.sanskrit: दीपनगमनग्रासप्रमाणमथ जारणपिधानम्। गर्भद्रुतिवाह्यद्रुतिक्षारणसंरागसारणश्चैव।
units.english: "Kindling, going, falling into globules, pulverising, covering, "Internal flux, external flux, burning, colouring, and pouring,

units.sanskrit: क्रामणवेधौ भक्षणमष्टादशधेति रसकर्म॥
units.english: "And eating it by parting and piercing it,—are the eighteen modes of treating quicksilver."

units.sanskrit: तत्प्रपञ्चस्तु गोविन्दभगवत्पादाचार्यसर्वज्ञरामेश्वरभट्टारकप्रभृतिभिः प्राचीनैराचार्यैर्निरुपित इति ग्रन्थभूयस्त्वभयादुदास्यते।
units.english: These treatments have been described at length by Govinda-bhagavat, Sarvajña-rāmeśvara and the other ancient authorities, and are here omitted to avoid prolixity.

units.sanskrit: न च रसशास्त्रं धातुवादार्थमेवेति मन्तव्यम्। देहवेधद्वारा मुक्ते रेव परमप्रयोजनत्वात्।
units.english: The mercurial system is not to be looked upon as merely eulogistic of the metal, it being immediately, through the conservation of the body, a means to the highest end, liberation.
Thus it is said in the Rasārṇava—

units.sanskrit: यज्जरया जर्जरितं कासश्वासादिदुःखविशदं च। योग्यं यन्न समाधौ प्रतिहतबुद्धीन्द्रियप्रसरम्॥ (र०हृ०१/२९) इति॥
units.english: "Declare to me, O god, that supremely efficacious destruction of the blood, that destruction of the body, imparted by thee, whereby it attained the power of flying about in the sky.

units.sanskrit: मुक्तिस्तावत्सर्वतीर्थकरसंमता।
units.english: Goddess (he replied), quicksilver is to be applied both to the blood and to the body.

units.sanskrit: चरमे शशविषाणकल्पा स्यात्।
units.english: This makes the appearance of body and blood alike.

units.sanskrit: नाजीवञ्ज्ञास्यति ज्ञेयं यदतोऽस्त्येव जीवनम्॥
units.english: A man should first try it upon the blood, and then apply it to the body."

units.sanskrit: तस्मादस्मदिष्टदेहनित्यत्वमत्यन्तादृष्टं न भवतीति पुरुषार्थकामुकैः पुरुषैरेष्टव्यम्। अत एवोक्तम् - आयतनं विद्यानां मूलं धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम्। श्रेयः परं किमन्यच्छरीरमजरामरं विहायैकम्॥
units.english: It will be asked: Why should we make this effort to acquire a celestial body, seeing that liberation is effected by the self-manifestation of the supreme principle, existence, intelligence, and beatitude? We reply: This is no objection, such liberation being inaccessible unless we acquire a healthy body.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं रसार्णवे - दर्शनात्स्पर्शनात्तस्य भक्षणात्स्मरणादपि।
units.english: Thus it is said in the Rasahṛdaya— In another place we read—

units.sanskrit: पूजनाद्रसदानाच्च दृश्यते षड्विधं फलम्॥ के दारादीनि लिङ्गानि पृथिव्यां यानि कानिचित्।
units.english: "The adoration of the sacred quicksilver is more beatific than the worship of all the phallic emblems at Kāśi and elsewhere,

units.sanskrit: तानि दृष्ट्वा तु यत्पुण्यं तत्पुण्यं रसदर्शनात॥इत्यादिना।
units.english: "Inasmuch as there is attained thereby enjoyment, health, exemption from decay, and immortality."

units.sanskrit: रसनिन्दायाः प्रत्यवायोऽपि दर्शितः - प्रमादाद्रसनिन्दायाः श्रुतावेनं स्मरेत्सुधीः।
units.english: The sin of disparaging mercury is also set out— "The adept on hearing quicksilver heedlessly disparaged should recall quicksilver to mind.

units.sanskrit: द्राक्त्यजेन्निन्दकं नित्यं निन्दया पूरिताशुभम्॥
units.english: "He should at once shun the blasphemer, who is by his blasphemy for ever filled with sin."

units.sanskrit: तस्मादस्मदुक्तया रीत्या दिव्यं देहं संपाद्य योगाभ्यासवशात्परतत्त्वे दृष्टे पुरुषार्थप्राप्तिर्भवति।
units.english: The attainment, then, of the highest end of the personal soul takes place by an intuition of the highest principle by means of the practice of union (ἕνωσις after the acquisition of a divine body in the manner we have described.

units.sanskrit: तदाभ्रूयुगमध्यागतं यच्छिखिविद्युत्सूर्यवज्जगद्भासि। के षांचित्पुण्यदृशामुन्मीलति चिन्मयं ज्योतिः॥
units.english: "The light of pure intelligence shines forth unto certain men of holy vision, "Which, seated between the two eyebrows, illumines the universe, like fire, or lightning, or the sun:

units.sanskrit: परमानन्दैकरसं परमं ज्योतिः स्वभावमविकल्पम्।
units.english: "Perfect beatitude, unalloyed, absolute, the essence whereof is luminousness, undifferenced,

units.sanskrit: विगलितसकलक्लेशं ज्ञेयं शान्तं स्वसंवेद्यम्॥
units.english: "From which all troubles are fallen away, knowable, tranquil, self-recognised:

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्नाधाय मनः स्फु रदखिलं चिन्मयं जगत्पश्यन्।
units.english: "Fixing the internal organ upon that, seeing the whole universe manifested, made of pure intelligence,

units.sanskrit: उत्सन्नकर्मबन्धो ब्रह्मत्वमिहैव चाप्नोति॥
units.english: "The aspirant even in this life attains to the absolute, his bondage to works annulled."

units.sanskrit: (र०हृ०१/२१-२३) श्रुतिश्च- ऽरसो वै सः। रसं ह्येवायं लब्ध्वानन्दी भवतिऽ (तै० २/७/१) इति।
units.english: A Vedic text also declares: That is Rasa (mercury), having obtained this he becomes beatitude.

units.sanskrit: तदित्थं भवदैन्यदुःखभरतरणोपायो रस एवेति सिद्धम्।
units.english: Thus, then, it has been shown that mercury alone is the means of passing beyond the burden of transmigratory pains.

units.sanskrit: तथा च रसस्य पर ब्रह्मणा साम्यमिति प्रतिपादकः श्लोकः - यः स्यात्प्रावरणाविमोचनधियां साध्यः प्रकृत्या पुनः संपन्नः सह तेन दीव्यति परं वैश्वानरे जाग्रति॥
units.english: And conformably we have a verse which sets forth the identity between mercury and the supreme self— "May that mercury, which is the very self, preserve us from dejection and from the terrors of metempsychosis, "Which is naturally to be applied again and again by those that aspire to liberation from the enveloping illusion,

units.sanskrit: ज्ञातो यद्यपरं न वेदयति च स्वस्मात्स्वयं द्योतते।
units.english: "Which, when it arises, pains no other soul, which shines forth by itself from itself."

units.sanskrit: इह खलु निखिलप्रेक्षावान् निसर्गप्रतिकू लवेदनीयतया निखिलात्मसंवेदनसिंद्धं दुःखं जिहासुस्तद्धानोपायं जिज्ञासुः परमेश्वरसाक्षात्कारमुपायमाकलयति।
units.english: Whoso wishes to escape the reality of pain, which is established by the consciousness of every soul through its being felt to be essentially contrary to every rational being, and wishes therefore to know the means of such escape,—learns that the knowledge of the Supreme Being is the true means thereof, from the authority of such passages as these (Śvetāśvatara Upan.

units.sanskrit: यदा चर्मवदाकाशं वेष्टयिष्यन्ति मानवाः।
units.english: vi. "When men shall roll up the sky as a piece of leather,

units.sanskrit: तदा शिवमविज्ञाय दुःखस्यान्तो भविष्यति॥
units.english: "Then shall there be an end of pain without the knowledge of Śiva."

units.sanskrit: इत्यादिवचननिचयप्रामाण्यात्। परमेश्वरसाक्षात्कारश्च श्रवणमननभावनाभिर्भावनीयः।
units.english: Now the knowledge of the Supreme is to be gained by hearing (śravaṇa), thought (manana), and reflection (bhāvanā), as it has been said—

units.sanskrit: यदाहआगमेनानुमानेन ध्यानाभ्यासबलेन च।
units.english: "By scripture, by inference, and by the force of repeated meditation,—

units.sanskrit: त्रिधा प्रकल्पयन्प्रज्ञां लभते योगमुत्तमम्॥
units.english: "By these three methods producing knowledge, he gains the highest union (yoga)."

units.sanskrit: तत्र मननमनुमानाधीनम्। अनुमानं च व्याप्तिज्ञानाधीनम्। व्याप्तिज्ञानं च पदार्थविवेकसापेक्षम्। अतः पदार्थषट्कम् ऽअथातो धर्म व्याख्यास्यामः' (क०सू०१/१/१) इत्यादिकायां दशलक्षण्यां कणभक्षेण भगवता व्यवस्थापितम्।
units.english: Here thought depends on inference, and inference depends on the knowledge of the vyāpti (or universal proposition), and the knowledge of the vyāpti follows the right understanding of the categories,—hence the saint Kaṇāda[2] establishes the six categories in his tenfold treatise, commencing with the words, "Now, therefore, we shall explain duty."

units.sanskrit: तत्राह्निकद्वयात्मके प्रथमेऽध्याये समवेताशेषपदार्थकथनमकारि।
units.english: In the first book, consisting of two daily lessons, he describes all the categories which are capable of intimate relation.

units.sanskrit: द्वितीयाह्निके जातिविशेषयोर्निरूपणम्। आह्निकद्वययुक्ते द्वितीयेऽध्याये द्रव्यनिरुपणम्। तत्रापि प्रपमाह्निक भूतविशेषलक्षणम्।
units.english: In the first āhnika he defines those which possess "genus" (jāti), in the second "genus" (or "generality") itself and "particularity." In the similarly divided second book he discusses "substance," giving in the first āhnika the characteristics of the five elements, and in the second he establishes the existence of space and time.

units.sanskrit: आह्निकद्वययुक्ते तृतीये आत्मान्तःकरणलक्षणम्। तत्राप्यात्मलक्षणं प्रथमे।
units.english: In the third book he defines the soul and the internal sense, the former in the first āhnika, the latter in the second.

units.sanskrit: द्वितीयेऽन्तःकरणलक्षणम्। आह्निकद्वययुक्ते चतुर्थे शरीरतदुपयोगिविवेचनम्।
units.english: In the fourth book he discusses the body and its adjuncts, the latter in the first āhnika, and the former in the second.

units.sanskrit: द्वितीये शरीरविवेचनम।आह्निकद्वयवति पञ्चमे कर्मप्रतिपादनम्। तत्रापि प्रथमे शरीरसंबन्धिकर्मचिन्तनम्। द्वितीये मानसकर्मचिन्तनम्।
units.english: In the fifth book he investigates action; in the first āhnika he considers action as connected with the body, in the second as belonging to the mind.

units.sanskrit: आह्निकद्वयशालिनि षष्ठे श्रौतधर्मनिरूपणम्। तत्रापि प्रथमे दानप्रतिग्रहधर्मविवेकः। द्वितीये चातुराश्रम्योचितधर्मनिरूपणम्।
units.english: In the sixth book he examines merit and demerit as revealed in Śruti; in the first āhnika he discusses the merit of giving, receiving gifts, &c., in the second the duties of the four periods of religious life.

units.sanskrit: तथाविधे सप्तमे गुणसमवायप्रतिपादनम्। तत्रापि प्रथमे बुद्धिनिरपेक्षगुणप्रतिपादनम्। द्वितीये तत्सापेक्षगुणप्रतिपादनं समवायप्रतिपादनं च।
units.english: In the seventh book he discusses quality and intimate relation; in the first āhnika he considers the qualities independent of thought, in the second those qualities which are related to it, and also intimate relation.

units.sanskrit: अष्टमे निर्विकल्पकसविकल्पकप्रत्यक्षप्रमाणचिन्तनम्।
units.english: In the eighth book he examines "indeterminate" and "determinate" perception, and means of proof.

units.sanskrit: नवमे बुद्धिविशषप्रतिपादनम्।
units.english: In the ninth book he discusses the characteristics of intellect.

units.sanskrit: दशमेऽनुमानभेदप्रतिपादनम्।
units.english: In the tenth book he establishes the different kinds of inference.[3]

units.sanskrit: तत्रोद्देशो लक्षणं परीक्षा चेति त्रिविधास्य शास्त्रस्य प्रवृत्तिः (वात्स्यायन० १/१/१)। ननु विभागापेक्षया चातुर्विध्ये वक्तव्ये कथं त्रैविध्यमुक्तमिति चेत्।
units.english: The method of this system is said to be threefold, "enunciation," "definition," and "investigation."[4] "But," it may be objected, "ought we not to include 'division,' and so make the method fourfold, not threefold?" We demur to this, because "division" is really included in a particular kind of enunciation.

units.sanskrit: तत्र द्रव्यगुणाकर्मसामान्यविशेषसमवाया इति षडेव ते पदार्था इत्युद्देशः।
units.english: Thus when we declare that substance, quality, action, generality, particularity, and intimate relation are the only six positive categories,—this is an example of enunciation.

units.sanskrit: किमत्र क्रमनियमे कारणम् ? उच्यते समस्तपदार्थायतनत्वेन प्रधानस्य द्रव्यस्य प्रथममुद्देशः। अनन्तरं गुणात्वोपाधिना सकलद्रव्यवृत्तेर्गुणस्य। तदनु सामान्यवत्त्वसाम्यात्कर्मणः। पश्चात्तात्त्रितयाश्रितस्य सामान्यस्य। तदनन्तरं समवायाधिकरणस्य विशेषस्य।
units.english: If you ask "What is the reason for this definite order of the categories?" we answer as follows:—Since "substance" is the chief, as being the substratum of all the categories, we enounce this first; next "quality," since it resides in its generic character in all substances [though different substances have different qualities]; then "action," as it agrees with "substance" and "quality" in possessing "generality;"[5] then "generality," as residing in these three; then "particularity," inasmuch as it possesses "intimate relation;"[6] lastly, "intimate relation" itself; such is the principle of arrangement.

units.sanskrit: ननु षडेव पदार्था इति कथं कथ्यते अभावस्यापि सद्भावात् इति चेत्मैवं वोचः। नञर्थानुल्लिखितधीविषयतया भावरूपतया षडेवेति विवक्षितत्वात्।
units.english: If you ask, "Why do you say that there are only six categories since 'non-existence' is also one?" we answer: Because we wish to speak of the six as positive categories, i.e., as being the objects of conceptions which do not involve a negative idea.

units.sanskrit: तथापि कथं षडेवेति नियम उपपद्यते ? विकल्पानुपपत्तेः।
units.english: "Still," the objector may retort, "how do you establish this definite number 'only six'? for either horn of the alternative fails.

units.sanskrit: नियमव्यवच्छे द्यं प्रमितं न वा। प्रमितत्वे कथं निषेधः अप्रमितत्वे कथंतराम् न हि कश्चित्प्रेक्षावान्मूषिकविषाणं प्रतिषेद्धंउ यतते। ततश्चानुपपत्तेर्न नियम इति चेत्मैवं भाषिष्ठाः। सप्तमतया प्रमितेऽन्धकारादौ भावत्वस्य भावतया प्रमिते शक्तिसादृश्यादौ सप्तमत्वस्य च निषेधादिति कृतं विस्तरेण।
units.english: For, we ask, is the thing to be thus excluded already thoroughly ascertained or not? If it is thoroughly ascertained, why do you exclude it? and still more so, if it is not thoroughly ascertained? What sensible man, pray, spends his strength in denying that a mouse has horns? Thus your definite number 'only six' fails as being inapplicable." This, however, we cannot admit; if darkness, &c., are allowed to form certainly a seventh category (as "non-existence"), we thus (by our definite number) deny it to be one of the six positive categories,—and if others attempt to include "capacity," "number," &c., which we allow to be certainly positive existences, we thus deny that they make a seventh category.

units.sanskrit: तत्र द्रव्यादित्रितयस्य द्रव्यत्वादिजातिर्लक्षणम्।
units.english: Substantiality, &c. (dravyatvādi), i.e., the genera of substance, quality, and action, are the definition of the triad substance, quality, and action respectively.

units.sanskrit: द्रव्यत्वं नाम गगनारविन्दसमवेतत्वे सति नित्यत्वे सति गन्धासमवेतत्वम्।
units.english: The genus of substance (dravyatva) is that which, while it alike exists with intimate relation in the (eternal) sky and the (transitory) lotus, is itself eternal,[7] and does not exist with intimate relation in smell.[8]

units.sanskrit: गुणत्वं नाम समवायिकारणासमवेतासमवायिकारणभिन्नसमवेतसत्तासाक्षाद्व्याप्यजातिः। कर्मत्वं नाम नित्यासमवेतत्वसहितसत्तासाक्षाद्व्याप्यजातिः। सामान्यं तु प्रध्वंसप्रतियोगित्वरहितमनेकसमवेतम्। विशेषो नामान्योन्याभावविरोधिसामान्यरहितः समवेतः। समावायस्तु समवायरहितः संबन्धः इति षष्णां लक्षणानि व्यवस्थितानि।
units.english: The genus of quality (guṇatva) is that which is immediately subordinate to the genus existence, and exists with intimate relation in whatever is not an intimate or mediate cause.[9] The genus of action (karmatva) is that which is immediately subordinate to the genus existence, and is not found with intimate relation in anything eternal.[10] Generality (or genus, sāmānya) is that which is found in many things with intimate relation, and can never be the counter-entity to emergent non-existence.[11] Particularity[12] (viśeṣa) exists with intimate relation, but it is destitute of generality, which stops mutual non-existence.[13] Intimate relation (samavāya) is that connection which itself has not intimate relation.[14] Such are the definitions of the six categories.

units.sanskrit: द्रव्यं नवविधं पृथिव्यप्तेजोवाय्वाकाशकालदिगात्ममनांसि इति।
units.english: Substance is ninefold,—earth, water, fire, air, ether, time, space, soul, and mind.

units.sanskrit: तत्र पृथिव्यादिचतुष्टयस्य पृथिवीत्वादिजातिर्लक्षणम्।
units.english: The genera of earth, &c. (pṛthivītva), are the definitions of the first four.

units.sanskrit: अप्त्वं नाम सरित्सागरसमवेतत्वे सति ज्वलनासमवेतं सामान्यम्। तेजस्त्वं नाम चन्द्रचामीकरसमवेतत्वे सति सलिलासमवेतं सामान्यम्। वायुत्वं नाम त्वगिन्द्रियसमवेतद्रव्यत्वसाक्षाद्व्याप्यजातिः।
units.english: The genus of water is that generality which is found with intimate relation in water, being also found in intimate relation in river and sea. The genus of fire is that generality which is found with intimate relation in fire, being also found with intimate relation in the moon and gold.

units.sanskrit: आकाशकालदिशामेकै कत्वादपरजात्यभावे परिभाषिक्यस्तित्रः संज्ञा भवन्ति आकाशं कालो दिगिति।
units.english: As ether, space, and time, from their being single, cannot be subordinate genera, their several names stand respectively for their technical appellations.

units.sanskrit: संयोगाजन्यजन्यविशेषगुणसमानाधिकरणविशेषाधिकरणमाकाशम्। विभुत्वे सति दिगसमवेतपरत्वासमवायिकारणाधिकरणः कालः। अकालत्वे सत्यविशेषगुणा महती दिक्। आत्ममनसोरात्मत्वमनस्त्वे।
units.english: Ether is the abode of particularity, and is found in the same subject with the non-eternal (janya) special quality which is not produced by contact.[17] Time is that which, being a pervading substance, is the abode of the mediate cause[18] of that idea of remoteness (paratva) which is not found with intimate relation in space;[19] while space is that pervading substance which possesses no special qualities and yet is not time.[20] The general terms ātmatva and manastva are the respective definitions of soul (ātman) and mind (manas).

units.sanskrit: आत्मत्वं नामामूर्तसमवेतद्रव्यत्वापरजातिः।
units.english: The general idea of soul is that which is subordinate to substance, being also found with intimate relation in that which is without form[21] (amūrtta).

units.sanskrit: मनस्त्वं नाम द्रव्यसमवायिकारण◌आत्वरहिताणुसमवेतद्रव्यत्वापरजातिः।
units.english: The general idea of mind is that which is subordinate to substance, being also found existing with intimate relation in an atom, but [unlike other atoms] not the intimate cause of any substance.

units.sanskrit: रूपरसगनस्पर्शसंख्यापरिमाणपृथकत्वसंयोगविभागपरत्वपरत्वबुद्धिसुखदुःखेच्छाद्वेषप्रयत्नाश्च कण्ठोक्ताः सप्तदशचशब्दसमुच्चिता गुरुत्वद्रवत्वस्नेहसंस्कारादृष्टशब्दाः सप्तैवेत्येवं चतुर्विंशतिर्गुणाः।
units.english: There are twenty-four qualities; seventeen are mentioned directly in Kaṇāda's Sūtras (i. 1, 6), "colour, taste, smell, touch, number, quantity, severalty, conjunction, disjunction, remoteness, proximity, intelligence, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, and effort;" and, besides these, seven others are understood in the word "and," viz., gravity, fluidity, viscidity, faculty, merit, demerit, and sound.

units.sanskrit: तत्र रूपादिशब्दान्तानां रूपत्वादिजातिर्लक्षणम्।
units.english: Their respective genera (rūpatva, &c.) are their several definitions.

units.sanskrit: रूपत्वं नाम नीलसमवेतगुणत्वापरजातिः।
units.english: The class or genus of "colour" is that which is subordinate to quality and exists with intimate relation in blue.

units.sanskrit: अनया दिशा शिष्टानां लक्षणानि द्रष्टव्यानि।
units.english: In the same way may be formed the definitions of the rest.

units.sanskrit: कर्म पञ्चविधम्। उत्क्षेपणापक्षेपणाकु ञ्चनप्रसारणगमनभेदात्। भ्रमणरेचनादीनां गमने एवान्तर्भावः। उत्क्षेपणादीनामुत्क्षेपणत्वादिजातिर्लक्षणम्।
units.english: "Action" is fivefold, according to the distinction of throwing upwards, throwing downwards, contracting, expanding, and going: revolution, evacuating, &c., being included under "going." The genus of throwing upwards, &c., will be their respective definitions.

units.sanskrit: तत्रोत्क्षेपणत्वं नामोर्ध्वदेशसंयोगासमवायिकारणसमवेतकर्मत्वापरजातिः।
units.english: The genus of throwing upwards is a subordinate genus to action; it exists with intimate relation, and is to be known as the mediate cause of conjunction with a higher place.

units.sanskrit: एवमपक्षेपणत्वादीनां लक्षणं कर्तव्यम्।
units.english: In the same manner are to be made the definitions of throwing downwards, &c.

units.sanskrit: सामान्यं द्विविधं परमपरं च। परं सत्ता द्रव्यगुणसमवेता। अपरं द्रव्यत्वादि।
units.english: Generality (or genus) is twofold, extensive and non-extensive; existence is extensive as found with intimate connection in substance and quality, or in quality and action; substance, &c., are non-extensive.

units.sanskrit: तल्लक्षणं प्रागेवोक्तम्।
units.english: The definition of generality has been given before.

units.sanskrit: विशेषाणामनन्तत्वात् समवायस्य चैकत्वाद् विभागो न संभवति।
units.english: Particularity and intimate relation cannot be divided,—in the former case in consequence of the infinite number of separate particularities, in the latter from intimate relation being but one; their definitions have been given before.

units.sanskrit: तल्लक्षणं च प्रागेवावादि।
units.english: There is a popular proverb—

units.sanskrit: द्वित्वे च पाकजोत्पत्तौ विभागे च विभागजे। यस्य न स्खलिता बुद्धिस्तं वै वैशेषिकं विदुः ॥
units.english: "Duality, change produced by baking, and disjunction produced by disjunction,—he whose mind vacillates not in these three is the true Vaiśeṣika;" and therefore we will now show the manner of the production of duality, &c.

units.sanskrit: इत्याभाणकस्य सद्भावाद्द्वित्वाद्युत्पत्तिप्रकारः प्रदर्श्यते। तत्र प्रथममिन्द्रियार्थसंनिकर्षः (१)। तस्मादेकत्वसामान्यज्ञानम् ( २)। ततोऽपेक्षाबुद्धिः (३)। ततो द्वित्वोत्पत्तिः (४)।
