units.sanskrit: स च श्वासप्रश्वासयोर्गतिविच्छेदस्वरूपः। तत्र श्वासो नाम बाह्यस्य वायोरन्तरानयनम्। प्रश्वासः पुनः कोष्ठयस्य बहिर्निःसारणम्।
units.english: Inspiration is the drawing in of the external air; expiration is the expelling of the air within the body; and "regulation of the breath" is the cessation of activity in both movements.

units.sanskrit: तयोरुभयोरपि संचरणाभावः प्राणायामः। ननु नेदं प्राणायामसामान्यलक्षणम्। तद्विशेषेषु रेचकपूरककुम्भकप्रकारेषु तदनुगतेरयोगादिति चेत्नैष दोषः, सर्वत्रापि श्वासप्रश्वासगतिविच्छेदसंभवात्।
units.english: "But [it may be objected] this cannot be accepted as a general definition of 'regulation of breath,' since it fails to apply to the special kinds, as rechaka, pūraka, and kumbhaka." We reply that there is here no fault in the definition, since the "cutting short of the motion of inspiration and expiration" is found in all these special kinds.

units.sanskrit: तथा हिकोष्ठ्यस्य वायोर्बहिर्निःसरणं रेचकः प्राणायामो यः प्रश्वासत्वेन प्रागुक्तः। बाह्यस्य वायोरन्तर्धारणं पूरको यः श्वासरूपः। अन्तःस्तम्भवृत्तिः कुम्भको यस्मिञ्जलमिव कुम्भे निश्चलतया प्राणाख्यो वायुरवस्थाप्यते।
units.english: Thus rechaka, which is the expulsion of the air within the body, is only that regulation of the breath, which has been mentioned before as "expiration;" and pūraka, which is the [regulated] retention of the external air within the body, is the "inspiration;" and kumbhaka is the internal suspension of breathing, when the vital air, called prāṇa, remains motionless like water in a jar (kumbha).

units.sanskrit: तत्र सर्वत्र श्वासप्रश्वासद्वयगतिविच्छेदोऽस्त्येवेति नास्ति शङ्कावकाशः।
units.english: Thus the "cutting short of the motion of inspiration and expiration" applies to all, and consequently the objector's doubt is needless.

units.sanskrit: स च वायुः सूर्योदयमारभ्य सार्धघटिकाद्वयं घटीयन्त्रस्थितघटभ्रमणन्यायेनैकैकस्यां नाडयां भवति। एवं सत्यहर्निशं श्वासप्रश्वासयोः षट्शताधिकैकविंशतिसहस्राणि जायन्ते।
units.english: Now this air, beginning from sunrise, remains two ghaṭikās and a half[78] in each artery[79] (nāḍi), like the revolving buckets on a waterwheel.[80] Thus in the course of a day and night there are produced 21,600 inspirations and expirations.

units.sanskrit: अत एवोक्तं मन्त्रसमर्पणरहस्यवेदिभिरजपामन्त्रसमर्पणे - षट्शतानि गणेशाय षट्सहस्रं स्वयंभुवे।
units.english: Hence it has been said by those who know the secret of transmitting the mantras, concerning the transmission of the ajapāmantra[81]— "Six hundred to Gaṇeśa, six thousand to the self-existent Brahman,

units.sanskrit: विष्णवे षट्सहस्रं च षट्सहस्रं पिनाकिने॥
units.english: "Six thousand to Viṣṇu, six thousand to Śiva,

units.sanskrit: सहस्रमेकं गुरवे सहस्रं परमात्मने।
units.english: "One thousand to the Guru (Bṛhaspati), one thousand to the Supreme Soul,

units.sanskrit: सहस्रमात्मने चैवमर्पयामि कृतं जपम्॥
units.english: "And one thousand to the soul: thus I make over the performed muttering."

units.sanskrit: तथा नाडीसंचारणदशायां वायोः संचरणे पृथिव्यादीनि तत्त्वानि वर्णविशेषवशात्पुरुषार्थाभिलाषुकैः पुरुषैरवगन्तव्यानि।
units.english: So at the time of the passing of the air through the arteries, the elements, earth, &c., must be understood, according to their different colours, by those who wish to obtain the highest good.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तमभियुक्तैः - सार्धं घटीद्वयं नाड्योरेकैकार्कोदयाद्वहेत्। अरघट्टघटीभ्रान्तिन्यायो नाड्योः पुनः पुनः॥
units.english: This has been thus explained by the wise— "Let each artery convey the air two ghaṭīs and a half from sunrise. "There is a continual resemblance of the two arteries[82] to the buckets on a revolving waterwheel.

units.sanskrit: शतानि तत्र जायन्ते निश्वासोच्छ्वासयोर्नव। खखषट्कद्विकैः संख्याहोरात्रे सकले पुनः॥
units.english: "Nine hundred inspirations and expirations of the air take place [in the hour], "And all combined produce the total of twenty-one thousand six hundred in a day and night.

units.sanskrit: षट्त्रिंशद्गुरुवर्णानां या वेला भणने भवेत्।
units.english: "The time that is spent in uttering thirty-six guṇa letters,[83]

units.sanskrit: सा वेला मरुतो नाड्यन्तरे संचरतो भवेत्॥
units.english: "That time elapses while the air passes along in the interval between two arteries.

units.sanskrit: प्रत्येकं पञ्च तत्त्वानि नाड्योश्च वहमानयोः।
units.english: "There are five elements in each of the two conducting arteries,—

units.sanskrit: वहन्त्यहर्निशं तानि ज्ञातव्यानि यतात्मभिः॥
units.english: "They bear it along day and night; these are to be known by the self-restrained.

units.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं वह्निरधस्तोयं तिरश्चीनः समीरणः।
units.english: "Fire bears above, water below; air moves across;

units.sanskrit: भूमिरर्धपुटे व्योम सर्वगं प्रवहेत्पुनः॥
units.english: "Earth in the half-hollow; ether moves everywhere.

units.sanskrit: वायोर्वह्नेरपां पृथ्व्या व्योम्नस्तत्त्वं वहेत्क्रमात्।
units.english: "They bear along in order,—air, fire, water, earth, ether;

units.sanskrit: वहन्त्योरुभयोर्नाड्योर्ज्ञातव्योऽयं क्रमः सदा॥
units.english: "This is to be known in its due order in the two conducting arteries.

units.sanskrit: पृथ्व्याः पलानि पञ्चाशच्चत्वारिंशत्ताथाम्भसः।
units.english: "The palas[84] of earth are fifty, of water forty,

units.sanskrit: अग्नेस्त्रिंशत्पुनर्वायोर्विंशतिर्नभसो दश॥
units.english: "Of fire thirty, of air twenty, of ether ten.

units.sanskrit: प्रवाहकालसंख्येयं हेतुस्तत्र प्रदर्श्यते।
units.english: "This is the amount of time taken for the bearing; but the reason that the two arteries are so disturbed

units.sanskrit: पृथ्वी पञ्चगुणा तोयं चतुर्गुणमथानलः॥
units.english: "Is that earth has five properties,[85] water four,

units.sanskrit: त्रिगुणो द्विगुणो र्वायुर्वियदेकगुणं भवेत्।
units.english: "Fire has three, air two, and ether one.

units.sanskrit: गुणं प्रति दश पलान्युर्व्यां पञ्चाशदित्यतः॥
units.english: "There are ten palas for each property; hence earth has fifty palas,

units.sanskrit: एकैकहानिस्तोयादेस्तथा पञ्च गुणाः क्षितेः।
units.english: "And each, from water downwards, loses successively. Now the five properties of earth

units.sanskrit: गन्धो रसश्च रूपं च स्पर्शः शब्दः क्रमादमी॥
units.english: "Are odour, savour, colour, tangibility, and audibleness; and these decrease one by one.

units.sanskrit: तत्त्वाभ्यां भूजलाभ्यां स्याच्छान्तिः कार्ये फलोन्नतिः।
units.english: "The two elements, earth and water, produce their fruit by the influence of 'quiet,'

units.sanskrit: दीप्तास्थिराव्यूहवृत्तिस्तेजोवाद्यम्बरेषु च॥ पृथ्व्यप्तेजोमरुद्व्योमतत्त्वानां चिह्नमुच्यते।
units.english: "But fire, air, and ether by the influence of 'brightness,' 'restlessness,' and 'immensity.'[86] "The characteristic signs of earth, water, fire, air, and ether are now declared;—

units.sanskrit: आद्ये स्थैर्यं स्वचित्तस्य शैत्ये कामोद्भवो भवेत्॥
units.english: "Of the first steadfastness of mind; through the coldness of the second arises desire;

units.sanskrit: तृतीये कोपसंतापौ चतुर्थे चञ्चलात्मता।
units.english: "From the third anger and grief; from the fourth fickleness of mind;

units.sanskrit: पञ्चमे शून्यतैव स्यादथवाधर्मवासना॥
units.english: "From the fifth the absence of any object, or mental impressions of latent merit.

units.sanskrit: श्रुत्योरङ्गुष्ठकौ मध्याङ्गुल्यौ नासापुटद्वये। सृक्किण्योः प्रान्त्यकोपान्त्याङ्गुली शेषे दृगन्तयोः॥
units.english: "Let the devotee place his thumbs in his ears, and a middle finger in each nostril, "And the little finger and the one next to it in the corners of his mouth, and the two remaining fingers in the corners of his eyes,

units.sanskrit: न्यस्यान्तःस्थपृथिव्यादितत्त्वज्ञानं भवेत्क्रमात्।
units.english: "Then there will arise in due order the knowledge of the earth and the other elements within him,

units.sanskrit: पीतश्वेतारुणश्यामैर्बिन्दुर्भिर्निरुपाधि खम्॥ इत्यादिना।
units.english: "The first four by yellow, white, dark red, and dark blue spots,[87]—the ether has no symbol."

units.sanskrit: यथावद्वायुतत्त्वमवगम्य तन्नियमने विधीयमाने विवेकज्ञानावरणकर्मक्षयो भवति।
units.english: When the element air is thus comprehended and its restraint is accomplished, the evil influence of works which concealed discriminating knowledge is destroyed [ii.

units.sanskrit: ऽतपो न परं प्राणायामाद्ऽ इति।
units.english: "There is no austerity superior to regulation of the breath."[88] And again—

units.sanskrit: ऽदह्यन्ते ध्मायमानानां धातूनां हि यथा मलाः। प्राणायामैस्तु दह्यन्ते तद्वदिन्द्रियजा मलाः॥ऽ इति च।
units.english: "As the dross of metals, when they are melted, is consumed, "So the serpents of the senses are consumed by regulation of the breath."[89]

units.sanskrit: तदेवं यमादिभिः संस्कृतमनस्कस्य योगिनः संयमाय प्रत्याहारः कर्तव्यः।
units.english: Now in this way, having his mind purified by the "forbearances" and the other things subservient to concentration, the devotee is to attain "self-mastery" (saṃyama)[90] and "restraint" (pratyāhāra).

units.sanskrit: चक्षुरादीनामिन्द्रियाणां प्रतिनियतरञ्जनीयकोपनीयमोहनीयप्रवणत्वप्रहाणेनाविकृतस्वरूपप्रवणचित्तानुकारः प्रत्याहारः।
units.english: "Restraint" is the accommodation of the senses, as the eye, &c., to the nature of the mind,[91] which is intent on the soul's unaltered nature, while they abandon all concernment with their own several objects, which might excite desire or anger or stupid indifference.

units.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि विषयेभ्यः प्रतीपमाह्रियन्तेऽस्मिन्निति व्युत्पत्तेः।
units.english: This is expressed by the etymology of the word; the senses are drawn to it (ā + hṛ), away from them (pratīpa).

units.sanskrit: ननु तदा चित्तमभिनिविशते नेन्द्रियाणिह तेषां बाह्यविषयत्वेन तत्र सामर्थ्याभावात्। अतः कथं चित्तानुकारः? अद्धा। अत एव वस्तुतस्तस्यासंभवमाभिसंधाय सादृश्यार्थमिवशब्दं चकार सूत्रकारः- ऽस्वविषयासंप्रयोगे चित्तस्वरूपानुकार इवेन्द्रियाणां प्रत्याहारः (पा. यो. सू. २/५४) इति।
units.english: "But is it not the mind which is then intent upon the soul and not the senses, since these are only adapted for external objects, and therefore have no power for this supposed action? How, therefore, could they be accommodated to the nature of the mind?" What you say is quite true; and therefore the author of the aphorisms, having an eye to their want of power for this, introduced the words "as it were," to express "resemblance." "Restraint is, as it were, the accommodation of the senses to the nature of the mind in the absence of concernment with each one's own object" [ii.

units.sanskrit: सादृश्यं च चित्तानुकारनिमित्तं विषयासंप्रयोगः।
units.english: Their absence of concernment with their several objects for the sake of being accommodated to the nature of the mind is this "resemblance" which we mean.

units.sanskrit: यदा चित्तं निरुध्यते तदा चक्षुरादीनां निरोधे प्रयत्नान्तरं नापेक्षणीयम्। यथा मधुकरराजं मधुमक्षिका अनुवर्तन्ते तथेन्द्रियाणि चित्तमिति।
units.english: Since, when the mind is restrained, the eye, &c., are restrained, no fresh effort is to be expected from them, and they follow the mind as bees follow their king.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं विष्णुपुराणे - शब्दादिष्वनुरक्तानि निगृह्याक्षाणि योगवित्।
units.english: This has been declared in the Viṣṇu-purāṇa [vi. "Let the devotee, restraining his organs of sense, which ever tend to pursue external objects,

units.sanskrit: कुर्याच्चित्तानुकारीणि प्रत्याहारपरायणः॥
units.english: "Himself intent on restraint, make them conformable to the mind;

units.sanskrit: वश्यता परमा तेन जायतेऽतिचलात्मनाम्। इन्द्रियाणामवश्यैस्तैर्न योगी योगसाधकः॥ (वि.पु.६/७/४३,४४) इति।
units.english: "By this is effected the entire subjugation of the unsteady senses; "If they are not controlled, the yogin will not accomplish his yoga."[92]

units.sanskrit: नाभिचक्रहृदयपुण्डरीकनासाग्रादावाध्यात्मिके हिरण्यगर्भवासवप्रजापतिप्रभृतिके बाह्ये वा देशे चित्तस्य विषयान्तरपरिहारेण स्थिरीकरणं धरणा।
units.english: "Attention" (dhāraṇā) is the fixing the mind, by withdrawing it from all other objects, on some place, whether connected with the internal self, as the circle of the navel, the lotus of the heart, the top of the sushumṇā artery, &c., or something external, as Prajāpati, Vāsava, Hiraṇyagarbha, &c.

units.sanskrit: तदाह-'देशबन्धश्चित्तस्य धारणा' (पात.यो.सू.३/१।) इति पौराणिकाश्च - प्राणायामेन पवनं प्रत्याहारेण चेन्द्रियम्।
units.english: This is declared by the aphorism, "'Attention' is the fixing the mind on a place" [iii. 1]; and so, too, say the followers of the Purāṇas—

units.sanskrit: वशीकृत्य ततः कु र्याच्चित्तस्थानं शुभाश्रये॥
units.english: "Let him next make the perfect asylum the dwelling-place of his mind."[93]

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्देशे ध्येयावलम्बनस्य प्रत्ययस्य विसदृशप्रत्ययप्रहाणेन प्रवाहो ध्यानम्। तदुक्तं - ऽतत्र प्रत्ययैकतानता ध्यानम्ऽ (पात. यो. सू. ३/२) इति।
units.english: The continual flow of thought in this place, resting on the object to be contemplated, and avoiding all incongruous thoughts, is "contemplation" (dhyāna); thus it is said, "A course of uniform thought there, is 'contemplation'" [iii.

units.sanskrit: अन्यैरप्युक्तम् - तद्रूपप्रत्ययैकाग्रया संततिश्चान्यनिःस्पृहा।
units.english: Others also have said— "A continued succession of thoughts, intent on objects of that kind and desiring no other,

units.sanskrit: तद्धयानं प्रथमैरङ्गैः षङ्भिर्निष्पाद्यते नृप॥
units.english: "This is 'contemplation,'—it is thus effected by the first six of the ancillary things."

units.sanskrit: प्रसङ्गाच्चरममङ्गं प्रागेव (द.१५. पं. १४७) प्रत्यपीपदाम। तदनेन योगाङ्गानुष्ठानेनादरनैरन्तर्यदीर्घकालसेवितेन समाधिप्रतिपक्षक्लेशप्रक्षयेऽभ्यासवैराग्यवशान्मधुमत्यादिसिद्धिलाभो भवति।
units.english: By this practice of the ancillary means of yoga, pursued for a long time with uninterrupted earnestness, the "afflictions" which hinder meditation are abolished, and through "exercise" and "dispassion" the devotee attains to the perfections designated by the names Madhumatī and the rest.

units.sanskrit: अथ किमेवमकस्मादस्मानतिविकटाभिरत्यन्ताप्रसिद्धाभिः कर्णाटगौडलाटभाषाभिर्भीषयते भवान्। न हि वयं भवन्तं भीषयामहे। किं तु मधुमत्यादिपदार्थव्युत्पादनेन तोषयामः। ततश्चाकुतोभयेन भवता श्रूयतामवधानेन।
units.english: "But why do you needlessly frighten us with unknown and monstrous words from the dialects of Karṇāṭa, Gauḍa,[94] and Lāṭa?"[95] We do not want to frighten you, but rather to gratify you by explaining the meaning of these strange words; therefore let the reader who is so needlessly alarmed listen to us with attention.

units.sanskrit: तत्र मधुमती नामाभ्यासवैराग्यादिवशादपास्तरजस्तमालशसुखप्रकाशमयसत्त्वभावनयानवद्यवैशारद्यविद्योतनरूपऋतंभरप्रज्ञाख्या समाधिसिद्धिः।
units.english: i. The Madhumatī perfection,—this is the perfection of meditation, called "the knowledge which holds to the truth," consisting in the illumination of unsullied purity by means of the contemplation of "goodness," composed of the manifestation of joy, with every trace of "passion" or "darkness" abolished by "exercise," "dispassion," &c.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तम् - ऽऋतंभरा तत्र प्रज्ञा' (पात. यो. सू. १/४८) इति।
units.english: Thus it is said in the aphorisms, "In that case there is the knowledge which holds to the truth" [i.

units.sanskrit: ऋतं सत्यं बिभर्ति कदाचिदपि न विपर्ययेणाच्छाद्यते।
units.english: It holds "to the truth," i.e., to the real; it is never overshadowed by error.

units.sanskrit: तत्र स्थितौ दार्ढ्ये सति द्वितीयस्य योगिनः सा प्रज्ञा भवतीत्यर्थः।
units.english: "In that case," i.e., when firmly established, there arises this knowledge to the second yogin.

units.sanskrit: चत्वारः खलु योगिनः प्रसिद्धाः प्राथमकल्पिको मधुभूमिकः प्रज्ञाज्योतिरतिक्रान्तभावनीयश्चेति।
units.english: For the yogins or devotees to the practice of yoga are well known to be of four kinds, viz.,— i.

units.sanskrit: तत्राभ्यासी प्रवृत्तमात्रज्योतिः प्रथमः। न त्वनेन परचित्तादिगोचरज्ञानरूपं ज्योतिर्वशीकृतमित्युक्तं भवति।
units.english: The prāthamakalpika, in whom the light has just entered,[96] but, as it has been said, "he has not won the light which consists in the power of knowing another's thoughts, &c.;" 2.

units.sanskrit: ऋतंभरप्रज्ञो द्वितीयः। भूतेन्द्रियजयी तृतीयः।
units.english: The madhubhūmika, who possesses the knowledge which holds to the truth; 3. The prajñājyotis, who has subdued the elements and the senses; 4.

units.sanskrit: परवैराग्यसंपन्नश्चतुर्थः।
units.english: The atikrānta-bhāvanīya, who has attained the highest dispassion. ii.

units.sanskrit: मनोजवित्वादयो मधुप्रतीकसिद्धयः।
units.english: The Madhupratīkā perfections are swiftness like thought, &c.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं -'मनोजवित्वं विकरणभावः प्रधानजयश्च (पात.यो.सू.३/४८) इति।
units.english: These are declared to be "swiftness like thought, the being without organs, and the conquest of nature" [iii.

units.sanskrit: मनोजवित्वं नाम कायस्य मनोवदनुत्तमो गतिलाभः। विकरणभावः कायनिरपेक्षाणामिन्द्रियाणामभिमतदेशकालविषयापेक्षवृत्तिलाभः। प्रधानजयः प्रकृतिविकारेषु सर्वेषु वशित्वम्।
units.english: "Swiftness like thought" is the attainment by the body of exceeding swiftness of motion, like thought; "the being without bodily organs"[97] is the attainment by the senses, irrespective of the body, of powers directed to objects in any desired place or time; "the conquest of nature" is the power of controlling all the manifestations of nature.

units.sanskrit: एताश्च सिद्धयः करणपञ्चकरूपजयात्तृतीयस्य योगिनः प्रादुर्भवन्ति। यथा मधुन एकदेशोऽपि स्वदते तथा प्रत्येकमेव ताः सिद्धयः स्वदन्त इति मधुप्रतीकाः। सर्वभावाधिष्ठातृत्वादिरूपा विशोका सिद्धिः।
units.english: These perfections appear to the full in the third kind of yogin, from the subjugation by him of the five senses and their essential conditions.[98] These perfections are severally sweet, each one by itself, as even a particle of honey is sweet, and therefore the second state is called Madhupratīkā [i.e., that whose parts are sweet].

units.sanskrit: इति च।
units.english: iii.

units.sanskrit: न च परिशेषावधारणानुपपत्तिः।
units.english: The Viśokā perfection consists in the supremacy over all existences, &c.

units.sanskrit: श्रुतमतवेदान्तद्रजन्याद्वितीयात्मविज्ञानाभ्यासेन विद्योदये संसारनिदानाविद्यानिवृत्त्युपलक्षितब्रह्मात्मतालक्षणपरमपुरुषार्थसिद्धेः।
units.english: This is said in the aphorisms, "To him who possesses, to the exclusion of all other ideas, the discriminative knowledge of the quality of goodness and the soul, arises omniscience and the supremacy over all existences" [iii.

units.sanskrit: तथा हिइदं रजतमिति प्रतीतौ शुक्ते रालम्बनत्वं पुरोदेशसत्तामात्रेणावलम्ब्यते कारणत्वेन भासमानत्वेन वा। नाद्यः। पुरोवर्तिनां लोष्टादीनामप्यालम्बनत्वप्रसङ्गात्। अथ कलधौतबोधकरणसंस्कारोद्बोधकारणत्वेन तद्द्वारा रजतज्ञानकारणत्वादालम्बनत्वं मन्यसे।
units.english: The "supremacy over all existences" is the overcoming like a master all entities, as these are but the developments of the quality of "goodness" in the mind [the other qualities of "passion" and "darkness" being already abolished], and exist only in the form of energy and the objects to be energised upon.[99] The discriminative knowledge of them, as existing in the modes "subsided," "emerged," or "not to be named,"[100] is "omniscience." This is said in the aphorisms [i.

units.sanskrit: अन्यथा समीचीनं रजतज्ञानं कदाचिददयमासादुयेत् । तन्न।
units.english: 36], "Or a luminous immediate cognition, free from sorrow[101] [may produce steadiness of mind]." iv.

units.sanskrit: अविनश्यतोः सहावस्थाननिषेधेपि विनश्यदविनश्यतोः सहावस्थानस्यानिषिद्धत्वेन निरन्तरोत्पन्नयोस्तदुपपत्तेः। ननु रजतज्ञानाद्रजतार्थी रजते प्रवर्ततां नाम। पौरस्त्ये वस्तुनि कथं प्रवृत्तिः स्यादिति चेन्न। स्वरूपतो विषयतश्चागृहीतभेदयोर्ग्रहणस्मरणयोः संनिहितरजतगोचरज्ञानसारूप्येण वस्तुतः परस्परं विभिन्नयोरप्यभेदोचितसामानाधिकरण्यव्यपदेशहेतुत्वोपपत्तेः। ग्रहणस्मरणयोः संनिहितरजतज्ञानसारूप्यं कथम्।
units.english: The Saṃskāraśeṣatā state is also called asaṃprajñāta, i.e., "that meditation in which distinct recognition of an object is lost;" it is that meditation "without a seed" [i.e., without any object] which is able to stop the "afflictions" that produce fruits to be afterwards experienced in the shape of rank, length of life, and enjoyment; and this meditation belongs to him who, in the cessation of all modifications of the internal organ, has reached the highest "dispassion." "The other kind of meditation [i.e., that in which distinct recognition of an object is lost] is preceded by that exercise of thought which produces the entire cessation of modifications; it has nothing left but the latent impressions" [of thought after the departure of all objects] [i.e., saṃskāraśeṣa, i.

units.sanskrit: एवं ग्रहणस्मरणे अपि दोषवशाद्विद्यमानमपीदमंशरजतांशयोरसंसर्ग भेदं नावगाहत इति।
units.english: Thus this foremost of men, being utterly passionless towards everything, finds that the seeds of the "afflictions," like burned rice-grains, are bereft of the power to germinate, and they are abolished together with the internal organ.

units.sanskrit: अपरोक्षावभासेन समानार्थग्रहेण च। अवैलक्षण्यसांवीत्तिरिति तावत्समर्थिता॥ व्यवहारोपि तत्तुल्यस्तत एव प्रवर्तते। (प्रक.प.४/३३/३७) एवमगृहीतविवेकमापन्नसंनिहितरूप्यज्ञानसारूप्यं ग्रहणस्मरणद्वयमयथाव्यवहारहेतुरिति सिद्धम्।
units.english: When these are destroyed, there ensues, through the full maturity of his unclouded "discriminative knowledge," an absorption of all causes and effects into the primal prakṛti; and the soul, which is the power of pure intelligence, abiding in its own real nature, and escaped from all connection with the phenomenal understanding (buddhi), or with existence, reaches "absolute isolation" (kaivalya).

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तममृतकलायाम् - अत्रोच्यते द्वयी संविद्वस्तुनो भूतलादिनः। एका संसृष्टविषया तन्मात्रविषया परा। तन्मात्रविषया वापि द्वयी साथ निगद्यते।
units.english: Final liberation is described by Patañjali as two perfections: "Absolute isolation is the repressive absorption[102] of the 'qualities' which have consummated the ends of the soul, i.e., enjoyment and liberation, or the abiding of the power of intelligence in its own nature" [iv.

units.sanskrit: नैकः पर्यनुयोक्तव्यस्तादृगर्थविचारणे॥ तथापि मामकस्यानुमानस्य किं दूषणं दत्तमासीत्। यद्यनुमानदूषणं विना न परितुष्यति हन्त कालात्ययापदिष्ठता। कृष्णवर्त्मानुष्णात्वानुमानवत्। एतावन्तं कालं यदिदं रजतमित्यभादसौ शुक्तिरिति प्रत्यक्षेण प्राचीनप्रत्ययस्यायथार्थत्वं प्रवेदयता यथार्थत्वानुमानस्यापहृतविषयत्वाद्वाध्यत्वसंभवात्।
units.english: Nor should any one object, "Why, however, should not the individual be born again even though this should have been attained?" for that is settled by the well-known principle that "with the cessation of the cause the effect ceases," and therefore this objection is utterly irrelevant, as admitting neither inquiry nor decision; for otherwise, if the effect could arise even in the absence of the cause, we should have blind men finding jewels, and such like absurdities; and the popular proverb for the impossible would become a possibility.

units.sanskrit: तथा हि। शुक्तीदमंशेन्द्रियसंप्रयोगादिदमाकारान्तःपरिणामरूपमेकं ज्ञानं जायते।
units.english: And so, too, says the Śruti, "A blind man found a jewel; one without fingers seized it; one without a neck put it on; and a dumb man praised it."[103]

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्विषयावच्छिन्नफलस्याप्येकत्वाज्ज्ञानैक्यमुपचर्यते। तदुक्तम्। शुक्तीदमंशचैतन्यस्थिताविद्या विजृम्भते। रागादिदोषसंस्कारसचिवा रजतात्मना॥ इदमाकारवृत्त्यक्तचैतन्यस्था तथाविधा।
units.english: Thus we see that, like the authoritative treatises on medicine, the Yoga-śāstra consists of four divisions; as those on medicine treat of disease, its cause, health, and medicine, so the Yoga-śāstra also treats of phenomenal existence, its cause, liberation, and its cause.

units.sanskrit: बाधाभावात्पदार्थानां सत्त्वत्रैविध्यमिष्यते॥ तात्त्विं ब्रह्मणः सत्त्वं व्योमादेर्व्यावहारिकम्। रूप्यादेरर्थजातस्य प्रातिभासिकमिष्यते॥ लौकिके न प्रमाणेन यद्वाध्यं लौकिके वधौ। तत्प्रातिभासिकं सत्त्वं बाध्यं सत्येव मातरि॥
units.english: This existence of ours, full of pain, is what is to be escaped from; the connection of nature and the soul is the cause of our having to experience this existence; the absolute abolition of this connection is the escape; and right insight is the cause thereof.[104] The same fourfold division is to be similarly traced as the case may be in other Śāstras also.
Thus all has been made clear.

units.sanskrit: नरेन्द्रगिरिश्रीचरणौस्त्वित्थमुक्तमअप्रकाशितप्रकाशव्यवहारहेतुत्वं हेत्वर्थः। तस्य चोभयत्रानुगतत्वान्नासिद्धयादिरिति।
units.english: The system of Śaṅkara, which comes next in succession, and which is the crest-gem of all systems, has been explained by us elsewhere; it is therefore left untouched here.[1]
